stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why Morning Routines Matter（为什么晨间习惯很重要）
body:
How you spend the first hour after waking up often shapes the rest of your day. Many people reach for their phones right away, check messages in bed, and rush out the door without eating breakfast. As a result, they already feel tired and behind schedule before nine o'clock.

In fact, a good morning routine does not have to be complicated or strict. You do not need to wake up at five in the morning or exercise for an hour. Even twenty quiet minutes can make a clear difference. For example, waking up fifteen minutes earlier gives you enough time to open the window, stretch your body, and enjoy a simple meal.

When you follow a few small steps in the same order every morning, your brain learns what comes next. This saves energy because you do not have to make too many tiny decisions right after waking up. Over time, these calm habits help lower morning stress and improve your mood.

Try starting with just two easy habits tomorrow, such as making your bed and drinking a glass of warm water. A steady start will help you feel more ready for whatever the day brings.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: How you spend the first hour after waking up often shapes the rest of your day.
sentences.main_clause: 主语从句 How you spend the first hour after waking up + 谓语 shapes + 宾语 the rest of your day。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：句首由 How 引导一个名词性从句作主语（“你如何度过醒来后的第一小时”），整句话把这整件事视为单数概念，因此谓语动词 shapes 用第三人称单数形式。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: This saves energy because you do not have to make too many tiny decisions right after waking up.
sentences.main_clause: 主句 This saves energy + 原因状语从句 because you do not have to make too many tiny decisions...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：because 引导原因状语从句，说明前面“节省精力”的原因；have to 表示“不得不”，其否定形式 do not have to 意为“不必”，而不是“禁止”。

translation:
你如何度过醒来后的第一个小时，往往决定了你这一天剩下的时间。许多人一睁眼就伸手拿手机，躺在床上刷消息，然后没吃早饭就匆匆出门。结果，不到九点，他们就已经感到疲惫，而且觉得时间不够用了。

其实，好的晨间习惯并不需要复杂或严苛。你没必要早上五点就起床，也不必锻炼整整一个小时。哪怕只是安静的二十分钟，也能带来明显的改变。比如，早起十五分钟，就能让你有足够的时间开窗通风、伸展身体，再吃一顿简单的早餐。

当你每天早上按相同的顺序完成几个小步骤时，你的大脑就会记住接下来要做什么。这能帮你节省精力，因为你不用在刚醒来时做太多琐碎的决定。久而久之，这些平和的习惯有助于减轻早上的压力，改善你的心情。

不妨明天就从两个简单的小习惯开始，比如整理床铺和喝一杯温水。一个平稳的开端，会让你更有准备去迎接这一天的各种事情。

quizzes.question: What does the writer think of a good morning routine?

options.text: It must start at five o'clock.
It needs at least one hour of exercise.
It can be simple and take just a short time.
It works only if you check messages first.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段明确提到“a good morning routine does not have to be complicated or strict... Even twenty quiet minutes can make a clear difference”，说明晨间习惯可以很简单、只需很短时间。

quizzes.question: Why does following the same morning steps save energy?

options.text: You can skip breakfast every day.
You avoid making too many small choices early.
You will sleep longer at night.
You do not need to open the window.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段指出“This saves energy because you do not have to make too many tiny decisions right after waking up”，即避免了刚醒来时做太多小决定。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: The Habit of Drinking Water（喝水与健康）
body:
Most of us know that water is important for our bodies, yet it is surprisingly easy to forget to drink enough of it. During a busy school day or workday, people often reach for coffee, milk tea, or sweet juice instead. While these drinks taste nice, they cannot truly replace plain water.

Our bodies lose water all the time through breathing, sweating, and normal daily movement. When we do not drink enough, even mild dryness can cause a headache, make us feel sleepy, or weaken our focus. Sometimes, when you feel hungry in the afternoon, your body is actually asking for water rather than food.

You do not need to force yourself to finish a huge bottle all at once. A better way is to take small sips throughout the day. Keep a reusable water bottle on your desk where you can easily see it. You can also connect drinking water to daily moments, such as having one glass before each meal or right after you return from class.

If plain water feels boring to you, try adding a slice of lemon or a few mint leaves for a fresh taste. Building this simple habit costs almost nothing, yet it quietly supports your energy and health every single day.

vocabulary.meaning: 令人惊讶地；出人意料地

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: While these drinks taste nice, they cannot truly replace plain water.
sentences.main_clause: 让步状语从句 While these drinks taste nice + 主句 they cannot truly replace plain water。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：While 放在句首时常表示“虽然、尽管”（相当于 Although），用于引出让步关系；taste 是系动词，后面直接接形容词 nice 作表语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Keep a reusable water bottle on your desk where you can easily see it.
sentences.main_clause: 祈使句 Keep a reusable water bottle on your desk + 定语从句 where you can easily see it。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：动词原形 Keep 开头构成祈使句，表示建议；关系副词 where 引导定语从句修饰先行词 your desk，说明“在你能轻松看到它的桌面上”。

translation:
我们大多数人都知道水对身体很重要，但令人惊讶的是，人很容易忘记喝足够的水。在忙碌的上学或工作日里，人们常常顺手去拿咖啡、奶茶或甜果汁。虽然这些饮品味道不错，但它们并不能真正替代白开水。

我们的身体时刻都在通过呼吸、出汗和日常活动流失水分。当饮水不足时，哪怕只是轻微缺水，也可能引起头痛、让人犯困，或削弱专注力。有时候，你在下午觉得饿了，其实你的身体真正需要的是水，而不是食物。

你不需要强迫自己一次灌完一大瓶水。更好的做法是在一天中分次小口喝水。在书桌上放一个可重复使用的水杯，让它处于你一眼就能看到的位置。你也可以把喝水和日常节点联系起来，比如每顿饭前喝一杯，或刚下课回来时喝一杯。

如果你觉得白开水太寡淡，可以试着加一片柠檬或几片薄荷叶来提味。养成这个简单的小习惯几乎不花什么成本，却能每天默默为你的精力和健康提供支持。

quizzes.question: What may happen when your body does not get enough water?

options.text: You may feel sleepy or have a headache.
You will always feel very cold.
You will enjoy plain water more.
You will need much less sleep.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出，即使轻微缺水也“can cause a headache, make us feel sleepy, or weaken our focus”，与 A 项完全对应。

quizzes.question: Which tip does the writer suggest for drinking more water?

options.text: Drink a whole large bottle at one time.
Replace water with sweet juice at lunch.
Put a bottle in plain sight on your desk.
Only drink water before going to bed.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段建议“Keep a reusable water bottle on your desk where you can easily see it”，即把水杯放在书桌上显眼的地方。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Screens and Your Sleep（手机使用与睡眠）
body:
Before turning off the lights at night, many of us tell ourselves, "Just five more minutes on my phone." Yet one short video easily leads to another, and soon an hour has passed. Checking screens late at night has become one of the biggest reasons why young people struggle to fall asleep.

There are two main problems with using a phone in bed. First, the bright light from the screen sends a wrong signal to your brain. It makes your brain think that it is still daytime, so your body slows down the production of sleep hormones. Second, exciting news, funny clips, or endless messages keep your mind active when it should be resting.

Breaking this late-night habit does not mean giving up your phone completely. A practical step is to create a "screen-free" rule for the last thirty minutes before bedtime. Place your charger across the room instead of next to your pillow. That way, you cannot reach for your phone without getting up.

During that half hour, try reading a light book, listening to soft music, or simply stretching gently. When you give your eyes and mind a real break from screens, falling asleep becomes much easier—and you wake up feeling far more refreshed.

vocabulary.meaning: 挣扎着做某事；很难做到
神清气爽的；精力恢复的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Checking screens late at night has become one of the biggest reasons why young people struggle to fall asleep.
sentences.main_clause: 动名词短语作主语 Checking screens late at night + 系动词 has become + 表语 one of the biggest reasons...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：Checking screens late at night 是动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数 has become；why young people struggle to fall asleep 是 why 引导的定语从句，修饰前面的 reasons。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: It makes your brain think that it is still daytime, so your body slows down the production of sleep hormones.
sentences.main_clause: 前半句 It makes your brain think that... + 结果连词 so + 后半句 your body slows down...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：make sb. do sth. 表示“使某人做某事”，注意 think 用省略 to 的不定式；that it is still daytime 是 think 的宾语从句；so 连接并列分句，表示结果。

translation:
晚上关灯之前，我们很多人都会对自己说：“再刷五分钟手机就睡。”然而一条短视频很容易接着下一条，很快一个小时就过去了。深夜看屏幕，已经成为年轻人难以入睡的最大原因之一。

在床上看手机主要有两个问题。首先，屏幕发出的亮光会向大脑传递错误的信号。它会让大脑以为现在还是白天，于是身体就会减缓睡眠激素的分泌。其次，令人兴奋的新闻、搞笑视频或没完没了的消息，会让本该休息的大脑一直处于活跃状态。

改掉这个熬夜习惯，并不意味着要彻底放弃手机。一个切实可行的办法，是在睡前最后三十分钟定下“不碰屏幕”的规矩。把充电器放到房间另一头，而不是枕头边。这样一来，如果不下床，你就够不到手机。

在那半小时里，可以试着看几页轻松的书、听听轻音乐，或者简单舒展一下身体。当你让眼睛和大脑真正从屏幕中歇一口气时，入睡就会轻松得多，第二天醒来也会神清气爽。

quizzes.question: How does bright screen light affect your sleep?

options.text: It makes your brain think it is still daytime.
It helps your eyes relax faster.
It causes your room to feel colder.
It increases sleep hormones immediately.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段说明“It makes your brain think that it is still daytime, so your body slows down the production of sleep hormones”，因此选 A。

quizzes.question: Why does the writer advise putting the charger across the room?

options.text: To protect your phone battery.
To stop you from reaching your phone in bed.
To keep the bedroom light bright.
To remind you to wake up early.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段提到“That way, you cannot reach for your phone without getting up”，目的是防止躺在床上顺手拿手机。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: The Joy of Cooking at Home（在家做饭的乐趣）
body:
Ordering food online is fast and convenient, especially when you come home tired from work or study. With just a few taps on a screen, a hot meal arrives at your door. Yet after weeks of takeout, many people start to miss the warm smell of a home-cooked dinner.

Cooking at home does not mean preparing complex restaurant dishes. A bowl of tomato and egg noodles, or some fried rice with fresh vegetables, takes less than twenty minutes to make. Even beginners can follow short video recipes step by step. Best of all, when you cook for yourself, you know exactly what goes into your food—less oil, less salt, and fresher ingredients.

There is also something deeply calming about working in the kitchen. Washing vegetables, listening to the sound of a pan heating up, and smelling garlic in warm oil can help you slow down after a busy day. Your hands stay busy while your mind gets a welcome rest from screens and textbooks.

Besides saving money, homemade food brings a quiet sense of pride. Sharing a simple dish you cooked yourself with family or friends turns an ordinary evening into a warm memory.

vocabulary.meaning: 一步一步地；循序渐进地

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Best of all, when you cook for yourself, you know exactly what goes into your food.
sentences.main_clause: 时间状语从句 when you cook for yourself + 主句 you know exactly what goes into your food。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：主句谓语 know 后面接了一个由 what 引导的宾语从句 what goes into your food（“你的食物里放了些什么”），what 在从句中兼作主语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Sharing a simple dish you cooked yourself with family or friends turns an ordinary evening into a warm memory.
sentences.main_clause: 动名词短语主语 Sharing a simple dish... + 谓语 turns + 宾语 an ordinary evening + 介词短语 into a warm memory。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：you cooked yourself 是省略了关系代词 that/which 的定语从句，修饰 a simple dish；turn A into B 意为“把 A 变成 B”。

translation:
点外卖既快捷又方便，尤其是当你下班或放学累得回家时。只需在屏幕上点几下，一份热腾腾的饭菜就会送到门口。不过，连吃几周外卖后，很多人还是会怀念家里做饭的温暖香气。

在家做饭并不意味着要准备像餐厅那样复杂的菜肴。一碗西红柿鸡蛋面，或者一盘加了新鲜蔬菜的蛋炒饭，不到二十分钟就能做好。即使是新手，也可以跟着短视频食谱一步一步学。最棒的是，自己做饭时，你能清楚地知道食材里放了什么——更少的油、更少的盐，还有更鲜嫩的原料。

在厨房忙碌本身也有一种让人平静下来的魔力。洗菜、听着平底锅慢慢升温的声音、闻着热油里蒜蓉的香味，都能帮你在忙碌一天后放慢节奏。双手忙起来的同时，大脑也刚好从手机屏幕和课本中得到片刻休息。

除了省钱之外，家常菜还会带来一份踏实的成就感。把自己亲手做的简单菜肴分享给家人或朋友，就能把一个普通的夜晚变成一段温暖的记忆。

quizzes.question: According to paragraph 2, what is a key benefit of cooking for yourself?

options.text: You can learn to run a restaurant.
You have full control over what goes into your meal.
You never need to wash dishes afterward.
You can finish every dish in two minutes.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出“you know exactly what goes into your food—less oil, less salt, and fresher ingredients”，说明自己做饭能掌控食材和油盐用量。

quizzes.question: How can working in the kitchen help your mind?

options.text: It helps you slow down and take a break from screens.
It teaches you how to order food faster.
It forces you to memorize long textbooks.
It makes you feel busier and more stressed.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段提到“can help you slow down after a busy day. Your hands stay busy while your mind gets a welcome rest from screens and textbooks”，故选 A。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Walking 30 Minutes a Day（每天散步 30 分钟）
body:
When people decide to get healthier, they often think of buying a gym membership or running five kilometers right away. Sadly, hard plans are easy to quit after just one or two weeks. Sometimes, the most effective exercise is also the simplest one: walking for thirty minutes a day.

Walking requires no special skills or expensive gear—just a comfortable pair of shoes. Unlike heavy workouts, it puts very little pressure on your knees and joints, so people of almost any age can enjoy it safely. Even better, you do not have to walk all thirty minutes in one go. Two fifteen-minute walks, or even three ten-minute walks after meals, bring real benefits.

A daily walk does wonders for both your body and your mind. Moving at a steady pace improves blood flow, helps digestion, and keeps your energy up. At the same time, stepping outside into fresh air gives your brain space to clear away worries. Many writers and students notice that good ideas often appear while they are walking outdoors.

Next time you feel stuck at your desk, put on your shoes and go around the block. Thirty minutes of walking may seem small, but over a year it adds up to a healthier, happier you.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Unlike heavy workouts, it puts very little pressure on your knees and joints, so people of almost any age can enjoy it safely.
sentences.main_clause: 介词短语 Unlike heavy workouts + 主句 it puts very little pressure... + 并列分句 so people... can enjoy it safely。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：Unlike 是介词，意为“与……不同”；little 修饰不可数名词 pressure，表示“几乎没有”，带有否定意味；so 引出结果。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Many writers and students notice that good ideas often appear while they are walking outdoors.
sentences.main_clause: 主句 Many writers and students notice + 宾语从句 that good ideas often appear...（含时间状语从句 while...）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：that 引导宾语从句，作 notice 的宾语；在该宾语从句内部，又嵌套了 while 引导的时间状语从句，表示“在户外散步期间”。

translation:
当人们决定让自己更健康时，常常立刻想到去办张健身卡，或者马上跑五公里。遗憾的是，过于艰难的计划往往坚持一两周就容易放弃。有时候，最有效的运动恰恰也是最简单的：每天散步三十分钟。

散步不需要特殊技巧，也不用买昂贵的装备——一双舒适的鞋子就够了。和高强度训练不同，它对膝盖和关节的压力很小，所以几乎任何年龄段的人都能安全地享受这项运动。更好的是，你不必一次性走完三十分钟。分两次每次走十五分钟，甚至三顿饭后各走十分钟，都能带来实实在在的好处。

每天散步对身心都大有裨益。保持稳定的步速行走能促进血液循环、帮助消化，并让你维持充沛精力。同时，走出门呼吸新鲜空气，还能给大脑留出空间，把烦恼清一清。许多作家和学生都发现，好点子常常是在户外散步时冒出来的。

下次如果你在书桌前觉得思路卡住了，就穿上鞋去街区转一圈吧。三十分钟的散步看似不起眼，但日积月累一整年，就会让你变得更健康、更快乐。

quizzes.question: Why do hard fitness plans often fail quickly?

options.text: Gym memberships are always sold out.
People find them too difficult to keep up.
Doctors tell people not to run.
Walking takes too much special gear.

quizzes.explanation: 第一段提到“hard plans are easy to quit after just one or two weeks”，说明太难的计划让人难以坚持。

quizzes.question: What does the writer say about the 30 minutes of walking?

options.text: It must be finished before breakfast.
It can be broken into shorter walks during the day.
It only works if you walk very fast.
It is mainly useful for professional writers.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出“you do not have to walk all thirty minutes in one go. Two fifteen-minute walks, or even three ten-minute walks after meals, bring real benefits”，故选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: How to Take Good Class Notes（如何记好课堂笔记）
body:
In class, some students try to write down every single word the teacher says. By the end of the lesson, their hands hurt, yet they barely remember what the main point was. Good note-taking is not about copying like a machine; it is about listening actively and recording key ideas.

First, write in short phrases instead of full sentences. Use symbols and arrows to show how ideas connect. For instance, an arrow can show cause and effect, while a star can mark something your teacher repeats twice. Leaving a bit of blank space on each page is also helpful, because you can add missing details later.

Second, pay close attention to clues during the talk. Teachers often slow down, raise their voice, or say phrases like "the most important reason" before sharing key facts. Those moments tell you what belongs in your notebook.

Finally, the secret to great notes happens after class, not during it. Spend just five minutes that evening reviewing what you wrote. Fix messy words, underline the main topic, and write one brief summary sentence at the bottom. When exam week arrives, those clear, organized notes will feel like gold.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: By the end of the lesson, their hands hurt, yet they barely remember what the main point was.
sentences.main_clause: 时间状语 By the end of the lesson + 分句 1 their hands hurt + 转折连词 yet + 分句 2 they barely remember what...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：yet 在这里作并列连词，表示转折（“然而”）；what the main point was 是 remember 的宾语从句，注意宾语从句要用陈述语序（what + 主语 + 谓语）。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Leaving a bit of blank space on each page is also helpful, because you can add missing details later.
sentences.main_clause: 动名词短语主语 Leaving a bit of blank space on each page + 系表结构 is also helpful + 原因状语从句 because...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：Leaving... 动名词短语作主语，因此系动词用单数 is；missing 是现在分词作定语，意为“遗漏的、缺失的”。

translation:
在课堂上，有些同学总是试图把老师说的每一个字都记下来。一节课结束时，手写酸了，可他们几乎不记得重点到底是什么。记好笔记不是像机器一样照抄，而是主动倾听并记录核心观点。

首先，用简短的词组代替完整的长句子。善用符号和箭头来展示观点之间的联系。比如，用箭头表示因果关系，用星号标出老师重复强调两遍的内容。每页笔记留出一点空白也很实用，因为课后你还可以把遗漏的细节补上去。

其次，听课时要留意老师给出的提示信号。老师在讲关键知识点前，往往会放慢语速、提高音量，或者说出“最重要的原因”这类提示语。这些时刻就是在告诉你，哪些内容应该记进笔记本里。

最后，好笔记的秘诀其实发生在下课之后，而不是课上。当天晚上花短短五分钟回顾一下写下的内容：整理潦草的字迹、给主题画线，并在页尾写上一句简短的小结。到了考试周，这些清晰又有条理的笔记就会像金子一样宝贵。

quizzes.question: Why should you leave blank space on your note pages?

options.text: To draw pictures when you feel bored.
To add missing details after class.
To make your notebook look thicker.
To avoid using symbols or arrows.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段明确说明“Leaving a bit of blank space on each page is also helpful, because you can add missing details later”，故选 B。

quizzes.question: What does the writer suggest doing on the same evening after class?

options.text: Copying all the notes onto a new page.
Reviewing the notes for five minutes and adding a summary.
Memorizing every word the teacher said.
Sharing your notebook with everyone in class.

quizzes.explanation: 最后一段建议当天晚上花五分钟复习笔记、整理词句并在页底写一句简短总结（one brief summary sentence），与 B 项一致。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Focus Better with the Pomodoro Technique（番茄工作法提高专注力）
body:
Have you ever sat down to study for two hours, only to spend half that time checking your phone or staring at the wall? When a task feels huge, our brains naturally look for ways to escape. One simple method called the Pomodoro Technique can help you stay focused without burning out.

The idea comes from an Italian student who used a tomato-shaped kitchen timer in the 1980s. The rules are very easy to follow. First, pick just one task to work on. Next, set a timer for twenty-five minutes and work without stopping until the bell rings. When time is up, take a five-minute break to stretch, get water, or look out the window. After four rounds like this, take a longer rest of fifteen to thirty minutes.

Why does this short cycle work so well? Twenty-five minutes feels safe and manageable. Instead of worrying about finishing a whole textbook, you only need to focus until the next break. And because you know a short rest is coming soon, it is much easier to ignore small distractions along the way.

If you have trouble getting started today, set a timer for just one twenty-five-minute round. Often, starting is the hardest part—and once you begin, momentum carries you forward.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Have you ever sat down to study for two hours, only to spend half that time checking your phone or staring at the wall?
sentences.main_clause: 现在完成时一般疑问句 Have you ever sat down to study... + 结果状语 only to spend...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：only to do sth. 放在句尾常表示“结果却……”，带有出乎意料或略感无奈的意味；spend time (in) doing sth. 表示“花时间做某事”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: And because you know a short rest is coming soon, it is much easier to ignore small distractions along the way.
sentences.main_clause: 原因状语从句 because you know... + 形式主语结构 it is much easier to ignore small distractions...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：主句采用 It is + adj. + to do sth. 句型，it 为形式主语，真正主语是后面的不定式短语 to ignore small distractions；much 用于修饰比较级 easier，加强程度。

translation:
你是否也曾坐下来打算学习两小时，结果却花了一半时间刷手机或对着墙壁发呆？当一项任务让人觉得庞大无比时，大脑本能地就会想逃避。一种叫“番茄工作法”的简单技巧，能帮你保持专注又不会把自己累垮。

这个点子源自二十世纪八十年代一位意大利学生，他当时用了厨房里一个番茄形状的计时器。规则非常简单：首先，只选定一件事来做；接着，把计时器设为二十五分钟，在铃声响起前专心工作、不中断；时间一到，就休息五分钟，伸伸懒腰、倒杯水或望望窗外；这样完成四轮后，再休息十五到三十分钟。

为什么这么短的循环却这么管用？因为二十五分钟让人觉得轻松、可控。你不必焦虑怎么啃完一整本教材，只需要专注到下一次休息就行。而且你知道很快就能休息一会儿，途中就更容易忽略那些让人分心的小事。

如果你今天觉得迟迟开不了头，不妨先定一个二十五分钟的计时器。很多时候，万事开头难——只要你开始行动，势头自然会推着你继续往前。

quizzes.question: After finishing four 25-minute rounds, what should you do?

options.text: Start a completely new timer immediately.
Take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.
Work for another two hours without resting.
Buy a new kitchen timer.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段明确写道“After four rounds like this, take a longer rest of fifteen to thirty minutes”，故选 B。

quizzes.question: Why is a 25-minute block easy to stick to?

options.text: It feels manageable and a break is always nearby.
It lets you check your phone every five minutes.
It finishes a whole textbook in one round.
It requires no timer at all.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段解释“Twenty-five minutes feels safe and manageable... because you know a short rest is coming soon, it is much easier to ignore small distractions”，因此选 A。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: The Warm Company of a Pet（养宠物带来的陪伴）
body:
Coming home to an empty apartment after a long day can feel quiet in a lonely way. For millions of people, however, opening the front door brings an excited bark at their feet or a soft cat rubbing gently against their legs. That small greeting alone can turn a heavy mood into a smile.

Living with a pet offers a special kind of comfort. Animals do not judge your mistakes, ask about your grades, or worry about your job. They simply sit beside you when you feel down and celebrate when you walk through the door. Studies have shown that petting a dog or listening to a cat purr can slow down your heartbeat and reduce daily stress.

Pets also bring healthy structure to their owners' lives. Dog owners, for instance, step outside every morning and evening for walks, which means more fresh air and friendly chats with neighbors. Feeding a pet on time teaches patience and responsibility, especially for students living away from home for the first time.

Of course, caring for an animal takes time, money, and real effort. Still, for those who are ready, the quiet loyalty and warmth of a pet become one of life's sweetest gifts.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Studies have shown that petting a dog or listening to a cat purr can slow down your heartbeat and reduce daily stress.
sentences.main_clause: 主句 Studies have shown + 宾语从句 that petting a dog or listening to a cat purr can slow down... and reduce...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：宾语从句的主语是由 or 连接的两个动名词短语 petting a dog 和 listening to a cat purr，表示“抚摸狗狗或听猫咪打呼噜”；slow down 和 reduce 由 and 连接作并列谓语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Dog owners, for instance, step outside every morning and evening for walks, which means more fresh air and friendly chats with neighbors.
sentences.main_clause: 主句 Dog owners... step outside... for walks + 非限制性定语从句 which means...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：which 引导非限制性定语从句，前面有逗号隔开，用来指代前面整个主句所描述的“早晚出门遛狗”这件事，谓语动词 means 因此用单数。

translation:
忙碌一整天后回到空荡荡的公寓，那种安静有时会让人感到孤单。然而，对成百上千万人来说，一打开家门，脚边就会响起兴奋的狗叫声，或者有只软绵绵的小猫轻轻蹭过来。光是这声小小的问候，就能把沉重的心情变成微笑。

和宠物生活在一起，能带来一种特别的慰藉。动物不会对你的失误指手画脚，不会追问你的成绩，也不在乎你的工作顺不顺利。它们只是在你低落时静静陪在身边，在你推门回家时欢欣雀跃。研究表明，抚摸狗狗或听猫咪发出呼噜声，能减缓心跳、缓解日常压力。

宠物还会给主人的生活带来健康的规律。比如养狗的人每天早晚都要出门遛弯，这意味着能呼吸更多新鲜空气，也更容易和邻居友好地聊上几句。按时喂养宠物能培养耐心与责任感，对第一次离家独自生活学习的学生来说尤其如此。

当然，照顾一只动物需要投入时间、金钱和实打实的精力。但对做好准备的人而言，宠物那份安静的忠诚与温暖，会成为生命中最甜蜜的礼物之一。

quizzes.question: According to the passage, why do pets bring special comfort?

options.text: They never judge you and stay beside you calmly.
They can help you finish your homework.
They cost almost no time or effort to keep.
They always make your apartment completely silent.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段提到“Animals do not judge your mistakes... They simply sit beside you when you feel down”，因此选 A。

quizzes.question: How do dogs add healthy structure to their owners' lives?

options.text: Owners eat more fast food together.
Owners go outside regularly for daily walks.
Owners stay indoors all weekend.
Owners sleep later every morning.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段指出养狗的人“step outside every morning and evening for walks”，从而接触新鲜空气并与邻居交流，故选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Tidy Room, Clear Mind（整理房间与心情）
body:
Look around your room for a moment. Is there a pile of clothes on the chair, or old papers covering your desk? Many of us tell ourselves we are "too busy" to clean up, yet living in a messy space quietly drains our energy without our noticing.

When your desk is full of random objects, your eyes see unfinished tasks everywhere. Even when you sit down to read or study, part of your mind stays distracted by the clutter around you. On the other hand, walking into a neat room sends a calm message to your brain: things are under control.

You do not need a whole weekend to turn your room around. Try the "ten-minute reset" rule every evening before bed. Put dirty clothes into the basket, throw away useless trash, and return books and pens to their proper spots. Small, regular actions prevent mess from turning into a mountain.

Tidying up is not just about making a space look nice for visitors. It is a simple way to care for yourself. When you clear the table where you study and create order in your room, you often notice your thoughts becoming clearer too.

vocabulary.meaning: 处于掌控之中；井然有序

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Many of us tell ourselves we are "too busy" to clean up, yet living in a messy space quietly drains our energy without our noticing.
sentences.main_clause: 主句 Many of us tell ourselves... + 转折分句 yet living in a messy space quietly drains our energy...。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：too + adj. + to do sth. 意为“太……而不能……”；后半句中 living in a messy space 作主语；without our noticing 中 our 是动名词 noticing 的逻辑主语，表示“在我们不知不觉中”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When you clear the table where you study and create order in your room, you often notice your thoughts becoming clearer too.
sentences.main_clause: 时间状语从句 When you clear the table... and create order... + 主句 you often notice your thoughts becoming clearer too。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：where you study 是定语从句修饰 the table；主句中 notice + 宾语 + doing 表示“注意到某物正在发生变化（变得更清晰）”。

translation:
花一秒钟环顾一下你的房间。椅子上是不是堆着衣服，或者书桌上铺满了旧纸张？我们很多人常安慰自己“太忙了”没空收拾，但生活在凌乱的空间里，其实会在不知不觉中悄悄消耗我们的精力。

当书桌上堆满各种杂物时，你的眼睛看到的到处都是“未完成的任务”。哪怕你坐下来看书或学习，大脑仍有一部分注意力会被周围的杂乱分散。相反，走进一间整洁的房间，会向大脑传递一个平和的信号：一切尽在掌控之中。

你不需要用一整个周末来彻底大扫除。可以试试每天睡前的“十分钟整理法”：把脏衣服放进洗衣篮，扔掉没用的垃圾，再把书和笔放回原本的位置。每天一点小动作，就能防止杂物越积越多、堆成小山。

整理房间不只是为了让客人看着好看，它也是照顾自己的一种简单方式。当你清理好学习的桌面、让房间恢复秩序时，往往会发现自己的思绪也跟着变得更清晰了。

quizzes.question: How can a messy desk affect you when you try to study?

options.text: It helps you finish your tasks faster.
It distracts part of your mind.
It makes the room feel warmer.
It improves your memory.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出“Even when you sit down to read or study, part of your mind stays distracted by the clutter around you”，故选 B。

quizzes.question: What is the 'ten-minute reset' rule?

options.text: Spend a whole weekend reorganizing the house.
Clean for ten minutes every night before sleeping.
Throw away all your old books and pens.
Invite friends over before cleaning up.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段解释“Try the 'ten-minute reset' rule every evening before bed”，并列举放衣服、扔垃圾、归位文具等动作，故选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why Paper Books Still Matter（为什么阅读纸质书仍有魅力）
body:
Today, we can carry thousands of e-books inside a thin phone or tablet. Digital reading is cheap, light, and great for long trips. Even so, paper books have never disappeared—and in recent years, many young readers have even fallen back in love with them.

Reading on paper feels different from scrolling on a screen. When you hold a real book, you can feel the weight of the pages and smell the ink. Your fingers turn one page after another, showing your progress naturally. Because a paper book has no pop-up messages or links to click, your attention stays inside the story instead of jumping around.

Studies also suggest that people often remember details better when they read on paper. Without realizing it, your mind remembers where a certain idea appeared—perhaps near the top of a left-hand page, or right beside a folded corner. Writing short notes in the margin with a pencil also creates a personal connection with the text.

Screens are wonderful tools for quick news and search, yet paper books offer something rarer: quiet focus. Turning off your phone for an evening and opening a real book still feels like stepping into another world.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Because a paper book has no pop-up messages or links to click, your attention stays inside the story instead of jumping around.
sentences.main_clause: 原因状语从句 Because a paper book has no... + 主句 your attention stays inside the story instead of jumping around。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：to click 是动词不定式作后置定语修饰 links（“可点击的链接”）；instead of 后接动名词 jumping around，表示“而不是跳来跳去”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Turning off your phone for an evening and opening a real book still feels like stepping into another world.
sentences.main_clause: 并列动名词短语主语 Turning off your phone... and opening a real book + 系动词 feels like + 宾语 stepping into another world。
sentences.grammar: 语法点拨：Turning off... and opening... 表达的是“关掉手机并翻开实体书”这一整体动作，因此谓语 feels 用单数；feel like doing sth. 在此意为“感觉像是在做某事”。

translation:
如今，我们可以在一部轻薄的手机或平板电脑里装进上千本电子书。数字阅读既便宜又轻便，特别适合长途旅行。即便如此，纸质书从未消失——而且近年来，许多年轻读者甚至重新爱上了纸质阅读。

纸上阅读的体验和滑动屏幕很不一样。当你捧起一本真正的书时，你能感受到书页的厚度，闻到油墨的清香。手指一页一页地翻动，能很自然地让你看到阅读进度。因为纸质书里没有弹窗消息，也没有链接可点，你的注意力会留在故事本身，而不是四处跳跃。

还有研究表明，人们在读纸质书时往往能更牢地记住细节。在不知不觉中，大脑会记下某个观点出现在哪里——也许是在左手边那一页的上方，或者就在一个折起的页角旁。用铅笔在页边空白处写几句简短批注，也会让你与文字建立起一种私人的连接。

屏幕非常适合用来快速获取新闻和查资料，但纸质书能提供一种更难得的东西：安静的专注。找一个晚上关掉手机，翻开一本实体书，那种感觉依然像是步入了另一个世界。

quizzes.question: Why is it easier to stay focused on a paper book?

options.text: Paper books are always much shorter.
Paper books have no pop-up messages or links.
Paper books can store thousands of stories.
Paper books read aloud to you automatically.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段提到“Because a paper book has no pop-up messages or links to click, your attention stays inside the story instead of jumping around”，故选 B。

quizzes.question: How does reading on paper help memory according to paragraph 3?

options.text: Your mind remembers where information appeared on the page.
You can search any word in one second.
Ink smells always make people stay awake.
Pencils automatically highlight important sentences.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段说明“your mind remembers where a certain idea appeared—perhaps near the top of a left-hand page, or right beside a folded corner”，故选 A。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: A Visit to a Public Library（公共图书馆的价值）
body:
On Saturday mornings, my local public library is already lively before nine o'clock. Elderly readers pick up the morning newspapers near the window, while college students carry their laptops to the quiet tables upstairs. In a small corner with colorful cushions, parents read picture books aloud to their young children.

Many people think libraries are only for borrowing paper books, yet a modern library offers much more than shelves of stories. First, it is one of the few indoor places in a city where anyone can stay for hours without buying a cup of coffee or paying an entrance fee. For someone preparing for an important exam or looking for a job, a warm desk and free internet access can make a real difference.

Libraries also bring neighbors together in simple ways. Last month, my community library held a weekend repair workshop, where volunteers taught residents how to fix broken lamps and torn clothes. Another room hosted a free English speaking club for beginners.

Even though smartphones allow us to read almost anything online, a screen cannot replace a calm public space shared by people of all ages. Walking out of the library with two books under my arm always makes me feel that a city cares about learning.

vocabulary.meaning: 使用权，接触的机会（internet access 网络接入）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: First, it is one of the few indoor places in a city where anyone can stay for hours without buying a cup of coffee or paying an entrance fee.
sentences.main_clause: it is one of the few indoor places（主系表结构，it 指代前文的 a modern library）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：where anyone can stay... 是关系副词 where 引导的定语从句，修饰前面的名词 places，表示“在那里任何人都可以待上好几个小时”；without buying... or paying... 是介词短语作伴随状语，表示“无需买咖啡或付门票”，介词 without 后接动名词形式。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Walking out of the library with two books under my arm always makes me feel that a city cares about learning.
sentences.main_clause: Walking out of the library ... makes me feel that ...（动名词短语作主语 + 谓语 + 宾语 + 宾补）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Walking out of the library... 是动名词短语作主语，谓语动词 makes 用第三人称单数形式；with two books under my arm 是“with + 宾语 + 介词短语”结构作伴随状语；that a city cares about learning 是 that 引导的宾语从句，说明 feel 的具体内容。

translation:
周六早上九点不到，我家附近的公共图书馆就已经很热闹了。老年读者在窗边拿起早报，大学生则带着笔记本电脑走上楼去安静的桌旁学习。在摆着彩色软垫的小角落里，家长们正大声给年幼的孩子读绘本。

很多人以为图书馆只能用来借阅纸质书，但现代图书馆能提供的远不止一排排的故事书。首先，它是城市里为数不多的室内场所之一，任何人不需要买一杯咖啡或付入场费就能在里面待上好几个小时。对于正在备战重要考试或找工作的人来说，一张温暖的书桌和免费网络往往能起到很大的帮助。

图书馆还以简单的方式把邻里联系在一起。上个月，我的社区图书馆举办了一场周末维修工作坊，志愿者教居民如何修理坏掉的台灯和破损的衣服。另一个房间还为初学者开设了免费的英语口语角。

尽管智能手机让我们几乎可以在网上读到任何内容，但屏幕无法取代一个让各年龄段的人共同享有的安静公共空间。每次腋下夹着两本书走出图书馆，我总会觉得这座城市是在乎学习的。

quizzes.question: What does the writer mainly tell us about a modern public library in Paragraph 2?

options.text: It sells cheap coffee to students.
It only lends paper books to local residents.
It provides a free and helpful space for everyone.
It is mainly built for elderly newspaper readers.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出图书馆不需要买咖啡或交入场费就能待好几个小时，还能为备考或求职者提供温暖的书桌和免费网络，因此是一个免费且有益的公共空间，选 C。

quizzes.question: Why did the community library hold a repair workshop last month?

options.text: To raise money for new computers.
To teach residents how to fix broken items.
To help children practice reading aloud.
To encourage people to buy new lamps.

quizzes.explanation: 根据第三段第二句“where volunteers taught residents how to fix broken lamps and torn clothes”，可知维修工作坊是为了教居民修理坏掉的物品，选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Cycling to Work or School（骑自行车通勤的好处）
body:
Every weekday at half past seven, traffic on the main road slows to a crawl. Buses wait behind long lines of cars, and drivers check their watches with worried faces. Meanwhile, people on bicycles move steadily along the bike lane, enjoying the cool morning air.

Choosing a bicycle for a short trip to work or school brings several practical benefits. To begin with, cycling saves both time and money during rush hour. A three-kilometer ride usually takes about fifteen minutes, and you never have to worry about bus delays or parking spaces. Over a whole year, the money saved on fuel or tickets can easily pay for a nice holiday.

Riding a bike is also an easy way to stay active. Many office workers and students spend most of the day sitting at a desk. When they cycle for thirty minutes a day, their legs grow stronger, and their minds feel clearer before the first class or meeting begins.

Of course, safety always comes first on busy streets. Wearing a helmet, using front and rear lights in the evening, and following traffic signals are basic habits every rider should keep. When the weather is dry and the distance is right, cycling turns a boring daily trip into the best part of the morning.

vocabulary.meaning: 慢得像爬一样，行驶极其缓慢

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Meanwhile, people on bicycles move steadily along the bike lane, enjoying the cool morning air.
sentences.main_clause: people ... move steadily along the bike lane（主语 + 谓语 + 状语）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：on bicycles 是介词短语作后置定语，修饰 people；逗号后的 enjoying the cool morning air 是现在分词短语作伴随状语，说明骑车人在骑行过程中的状态。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Wearing a helmet, using front and rear lights in the evening, and following traffic signals are basic habits every rider should keep.
sentences.main_clause: Wearing..., using..., and following... are basic habits（三个并列动名词短语作主语 + 系动词 + 表语）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：因为主语是由 and 连接的三个并列动名词短语，所以系动词用复数 are；句尾 every rider should keep 是一个省略了关系代词 that/which 的定语从句，修饰 habits。

translation:
每个工作日的七点半，主干道上的车流就会慢得像爬一样。公交车排在长长的汽车队伍后面，司机们一脸焦急地看着手表。与此同时，骑自行车的人沿着自行车道平稳前行，享受着清晨凉爽的空气。

选择骑自行车去上班或上学等短途出行能带来不少实际好处。首先，在早晚高峰期骑车既省时又省钱。三公里的路程通常只需要大约十五分钟，你完全不用担心公交延误或找停车位的问题。一整年下来，省下的油钱或车票钱足以让你轻松来一次不错的度假。

骑自行车也是保持身体活力的简单方式。许多上班族和学生一天中大部分时间都坐在书桌前。如果他们每天骑车三十分钟，腿部会更有力量，在第一节课或早会开始前头脑也会更清醒。

当然，在繁忙的街道上安全永远是第一位的。戴好头盔、晚上打开前后车灯以及遵守交通信号，是每位骑行者都应该保持的基本习惯。当天气干燥、路程合适时，骑车能把枯燥的日常通勤变成早晨最惬意的一段时光。

quizzes.question: Why is cycling helpful during rush hour according to Paragraph 2?

options.text: Riders can carry more luggage than bus passengers.
It avoids traffic jams and saves money on travel.
Bike lanes are wider than car roads in every city.
Companies usually pay workers to ride to the office.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段提到三公里骑行只需约15分钟，不用担心公交延误或停车，还能省下油钱或车票钱，即既避开拥堵又省钱，选 B。

quizzes.question: Which safety habit is mentioned in the last paragraph?

options.text: Riding slowly on sidewalks.
Checking the weather map every hour.
Using lights on the bike at night.
Avoiding main roads on weekends.

quizzes.explanation: 最后一段明确提到了三项安全习惯：戴头盔、晚上使用前后车灯（using front and rear lights in the evening）以及遵守交通信号，选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Patience in Learning a New Skill（学习一门新技能的耐心）
body:
When Emma bought her first guitar last spring, she imagined herself playing favorite songs within two weeks. Instead, her fingertips hurt after ten minutes of practice, and the chords sounded messy and flat. By the end of the first month, she almost put the guitar in the back of her closet.

Many learners hit this same wall when they start something new, whether it is cooking, swimming, or speaking a foreign language. At the beginning, our minds understand what a skill should look like, yet our hands, ears, or muscles have not caught up yet. That gap between expectation and real ability often feels discouraging.

The secret to crossing that gap is patience combined with small daily steps. Rather than practicing for three hours once a week, practicing for twenty minutes every evening helps the brain build steady memory. Slowly, the movements that once felt awkward become natural and automatic.

Emma did not give up. She decided to practice just two simple chords each night before dinner. Three months later, she played a whole song for her family without stopping. Real progress rarely arrives overnight; it grows quietly through patient, everyday effort.

vocabulary.meaning: 令人气馁的，使人沮丧的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: At the beginning, our minds understand what a skill should look like, yet our hands, ears, or muscles have not caught up yet.
sentences.main_clause: our minds understand ..., yet our hands, ears, or muscles have not caught up yet（由并列连词 yet 连接的转折并列句）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：what a skill should look like 是 what 引导的宾语从句，作 understand 的宾语；yet 在此处作连词，表示转折关系，相当于 but，语气更强调前后的反差。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Slowly, the movements that once felt awkward become natural and automatic.
sentences.main_clause: the movements ... become natural and automatic（主系表结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：that once felt awkward 是关系代词 that 引导的定语从句，修饰主语 the movements，其中 felt 作系动词，后接形容词 awkward；主句谓语 become 同样为系动词，用复数形式与 movements 保持一致。

translation:
去年春天艾玛买下第一把吉他时，她原以为两周内就能弹奏自己喜欢的歌。然而事实却是，练了十分钟她的指尖就生疼，弹出的和弦也杂乱又走音。到了第一个月底，她差点把吉他塞到衣柜最里面。

许多学习者在开始接触新事物时都会遇到同样的瓶颈，无论是做饭、游泳还是学一门外语。一开始，我们的大脑明白这项技能应该是什么样子，但手、耳朵或肌肉还没有跟上节奏。期待与真实水平之间的这种落差常常让人感到灰心。

跨越这道鸿沟的秘诀是耐心加上每天的小步积累。比起一周一次练三个小时，每晚练习二十分钟更有助于大脑建立稳定的记忆。慢慢地，曾经觉得别扭的动作会变得自然而顺畅。

艾玛没有放弃。她决定每天晚饭前只练习两个简单的和弦。三个月后，她不停顿地为家人完整弹奏了一首歌。真正的进步很少一夜之间到来，它是在日复一日的耐心努力中悄悄生长的。

quizzes.question: Why did Emma nearly stop playing the guitar after the first month?

options.text: Her guitar was broken and hard to repair.
Her fingers hurt and the music did not sound good.
Her family complained about the noise every night.
She decided to learn swimming instead.

quizzes.explanation: 第一段说明她练了十分钟指尖就疼，而且和弦听起来杂乱走音，因此第一月底差点放弃，选 B。

quizzes.question: What helped Emma finally play a whole song?

options.text: Practicing two simple chords each night.
Taking a three-hour lesson every weekend.
Watching videos without touching the guitar.
Buying an expensive new guitar.

quizzes.explanation: 第四段提到艾玛决定每晚晚饭前只练两个简单的和弦，三个月后就能完整弹奏一首歌，选 A。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Smart Spending in Daily Life（节俭与理性消费）
body:
Online sales often look too good to miss. A bright red banner promises fifty percent off, and a small clock counts down the final hours. Before you know it, a pair of shoes or a new jacket sits in your shopping cart, even though your closet is already full.

Being careful with money does not mean living a dull life or refusing every small pleasure. Smart spending simply means thinking twice before you pay and choosing things you truly value. One useful habit is the "twenty-four-hour rule." Whenever you see something non-essential online, wait one full day before buying it. In many cases, the sudden excitement fades by the next morning, and you realize you do not actually need it.

Another helpful step is tracking small daily costs. A fancy drink every afternoon or a few takeout meals a week may look cheap on their own, yet together they can eat up a large part of a student's monthly budget. Cooking simple meals at home or carrying a reusable water bottle saves money without lowering your quality of life.

When you spend thoughtfully on what really matters, you feel less stress about bills and have more freedom for meaningful goals, such as taking a course or traveling with friends.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Before you know it, a pair of shoes or a new jacket sits in your shopping cart, even though your closet is already full.
sentences.main_clause: a pair of shoes or a new jacket sits in your shopping cart（主语 + 谓语 + 地点状语）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：句首 Before you know it 是固定习语，意为“不知不觉中”；句尾 even though your closet is already full 是 even though 引导的让步状语从句，表示“尽管你的衣柜已经满了”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When you spend thoughtfully on what really matters, you feel less stress about bills and have more freedom for meaningful goals, such as taking a course or traveling with friends.
sentences.main_clause: you feel less stress ... and have more freedom ...（主语 + 并列谓语 feel 和 have）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：When you spend... 是时间状语从句，其中 what really matters 是 what 引导的宾语从句，作介词 on 的宾语，意为“真正重要的东西”；such as taking... or traveling... 举例说明 meaningful goals。

translation:
网上促销常常让人觉得不买就亏了。鲜红的横幅写着半价优惠，旁边的小时钟还在倒数最后几个小时。不知不觉间，一双鞋或一件新外套就躺进了你的购物车，尽管你的衣柜早就塞满了。

花钱谨慎并不意味着过枯燥的生活，或者拒绝每一个小乐趣。理性消费只是指在付款前多想一步，选择自己真正看重的东西。一个很有用的习惯是“二十四小时法则”：每当在网上看到非必需品时，先等满一天再买。很多时候，到了第二天早上，最初的兴奋感就会消退，你会意识到自己其实并不需要它。

另一个有用的做法是记录每天的小额开销。每天下午买一杯精致饮品，或每周点几次外卖，单看似乎很便宜，但加在一起却可能花掉学生每月预算的很大一部分。在家做简单的饭菜或随身带一个可重复使用的水杯，既能省钱又不会降低生活质量。

当你把钱深思熟虑地花在真正重要的事情上时，账单带来的压力会减少，你也会拥有更多自由去实现有意义的目标，比如报一门课程或和朋友一起旅行。

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the "twenty-four-hour rule"?

options.text: To wait for stores to offer higher discounts.
To avoid buying things out of sudden excitement.
To compare prices across twenty-four websites.
To return unwanted clothes within one day.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出，等待一天后“the sudden excitement fades by the next morning, and you realize you do not actually need it”，可见其目的是避免冲动消费，选 B。

quizzes.question: What does the writer say about small daily costs like afternoon drinks?

options.text: They are always worth buying for students.
They can quietly take up a big share of a budget.
They are much healthier than home-cooked meals.
They have nothing to do with financial stress.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段提到这些日常小额开销“单看便宜，合起来却能消耗掉学生月度预算的很大一部分（eat up a large part of a student's monthly budget）”，选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: How Weather Affects Our Mood（天气如何影响人的情绪）
body:
Have you ever noticed how a bright blue sky makes it easier to get out of bed, while a dark, rainy morning makes you want to pull the blanket back over your head? Weather does more than decide what jacket we wear; it also shapes our energy and feelings.

Sunlight plays a major role in this process. When natural light enters our eyes, it sends signals to the brain to produce chemicals that keep us awake and cheerful. During long winter weeks with gray skies, some people feel unusually tired or quiet because they receive less daylight.

Rain and wind affect people in different ways, too. On a cool, stormy afternoon, heavy clouds can make a room feel dim, and indoor plans often replace outdoor exercise. Less movement and fresh air may leave us feeling sleepy or slightly impatient. On the other hand, some people actually love rainy days because the soft sound of raindrops helps them focus on reading or resting.

Although we cannot control the forecast, we can respond to it wisely. Opening curtains wide in the morning, taking a short walk at noon, or turning on warm indoor lamps on gloomy days can lift our spirits no matter what the sky looks like outside.

vocabulary.meaning: 振奋精神，使人心情变好

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: When natural light enters our eyes, it sends signals to the brain to produce chemicals that keep us awake and cheerful.
sentences.main_clause: it sends signals to the brain（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语 + 状语）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：When natural light enters our eyes 为时间状语从句；to produce chemicals 为不定式短语作目的状语；句末 that keep us awake and cheerful 是定语从句，修饰 chemicals，其中 keep + 宾语 + 形容词 表示“使……保持某种状态”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: On the other hand, some people actually love rainy days because the soft sound of raindrops helps them focus on reading or resting.
sentences.main_clause: some people actually love rainy days（主谓宾结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：On the other hand 作过渡插入语，引出对比观点；because... 引导原因状语从句，其中 help sb. (to) do sth. 省略了不定式符号 to，focus on 后接动名词 reading or resting 作并列宾语。

translation:
你有没有注意到，晴朗的蓝天会让人更容易起床，而阴暗的下雨天却让人想把被子重新拉过头顶？天气决定的不只是我们穿哪件外套，它也在悄悄影响着我们的精力和情绪。

阳光在这个过程中起着重要作用。当自然光进入眼睛时，它会向大脑发出信号，促使大脑分泌让我们保持清醒和愉快的化学物质。在漫长而阴沉的冬季，由于接受的日光较少，有些人会觉得格外疲倦或沉默寡言。

风雨也会以不同的方式影响人们。在凉爽的暴风雨午后，厚厚的云层会让房间显得昏暗，室内安排往往会取代户外锻炼。运动和新鲜空气减少后，我们可能会感到犯困或有些急躁。不过另一方面，有些人其实很喜欢雨天，因为轻柔的雨声能帮助他们专心阅读或好好休息。

虽然我们无法控制天气预报，但我们可以聪明地应对天气变化。早上把窗帘大大拉开、中午出去短走一会儿，或者在阴沉的日子里打开温暖的室内灯，无论窗外天空如何，都能让我们的心情明朗起来。

quizzes.question: Why do some people feel tired during long, gray winter weeks?

options.text: They spend too much time exercising outdoors.
They receive less natural sunlight.
They drink less water in cold weather.
They wake up too early every morning.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段明确指出，阴天的冬天让人感到疲倦或安静，是因为“they receive less daylight”（接收到的日光较少），选 B。

quizzes.question: Why do some people enjoy rainy days according to Paragraph 3?

options.text: Rain cleans the air for outdoor running.
The sound of rain helps them concentrate or relax.
Stores usually offer discounts when it rains.
They like wearing warm jackets and boots.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段最后一句说明有些人喜欢雨天，是因为轻柔的雨声帮助他们专注于阅读或休息（focus on reading or resting），选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Volunteering in the Community（社区志愿者经历）
body:
Last autumn, I signed up for a weekend volunteer program at a neighborhood center near my apartment. At first, I felt nervous because I did not know anyone there and worried that I might not be helpful enough. Still, I showed up at nine o'clock on Sunday with a bottle of water and a notebook.

My main job was helping older residents use their smartphones. Some wanted to learn how to send voice messages to their grandchildren, while others needed help booking doctor appointments online. None of these tasks seemed hard to me, yet each small success brought huge smiles to their faces. One grandfather, Mr. Chen, wrote down every step carefully in large letters so he could practice at home.

Over the next two months, I noticed changes in myself as well. Explaining things clearly taught me to slow down and listen carefully. I also met students, nurses, and retired teachers who worked side by side every weekend. Our neighborhood stopped feeling like a row of closed doors and started to feel like a real community.

You do not need special skills or lots of money to volunteer. Giving just two hours of your time can brighten someone else's week and teach you something valuable in return.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: At first, I felt nervous because I did not know anyone there and worried that I might not be helpful enough.
sentences.main_clause: I felt nervous（主系表结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：because... 引导原因状语从句，说明紧张的原因；在原因从句中，动词 did not know 和 worried 由 and 连接并列，而 that I might not be helpful enough 是 worried 后面的宾语从句。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: One grandfather, Mr. Chen, wrote down every step carefully in large letters so he could practice at home.
sentences.main_clause: One grandfather wrote down every step（主谓宾结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Mr. Chen 作 One grandfather 的同位语，补充说明具体是谁；so he could practice at home 是 so（相当于 so that）引导的目的状语从句，表示“以便他回家后能练习”。

translation:
去年秋天，我报名参加了公寓附近一家社区中心的周末志愿服务项目。起初我很紧张，因为我在那里谁都不认识，还担心自己帮不上什么忙。尽管如此，周日上午九点我还是带着一瓶水和一本笔记本准时到了那里。

我的主要任务是教社区里的老人使用智能手机。有的人想学怎么给孙辈发语音消息，有的人则需要帮忙在网上预约挂号。这些事对我来说都不难，但每一次小小的成功都让他们脸上绽放出灿烂的笑容。有位陈爷爷用大字仔细记下每一步操作，好回家自己练习。

在接下来的两个月里，我也注意到了自己的变化。把事情讲清楚的过程教会了我放慢语速、认真倾听。我还认识了每个周末并肩服务的学生、护士和退休教师。我们的社区不再像一排紧闭的门，而开始有了真正大家庭的感觉。

做志愿服务并不需要特别的技能或很多钱。哪怕只付出两个小时的时间，也能点亮别人的一周，而你自己也会收获宝贵的成长。

quizzes.question: What did the writer help older residents do at the neighborhood center?

options.text: Clean their apartments on weekends.
Learn how to use smartphones.
Cook healthy meals together.
Write letters to their grandchildren.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段第一句明确说明“My main job was helping older residents use their smartphones”，选 B。

quizzes.question: How did volunteering change the writer?

options.text: It helped the writer learn to be patient and listen well.
It inspired the writer to become a hospital nurse.
It made the writer realize smartphones are hard to use.
It gave the writer a chance to earn extra money.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段指出志愿服务教会了作者放慢脚步并认真倾听（taught me to slow down and listen carefully），选 A。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Tea and Coffee Cultures（茶与咖啡的文化差异）
body:
In nearly every country, people start their day or welcome guests with a warm drink. Around the world, tea and coffee are the two most popular choices, yet each drink carries its own rhythm and social habits.

Tea has a long history in Asia and parts of Europe. In China and Japan, preparing tea is often seen as a moment to slow down. Hosts heat water carefully, pour leaves into a pot, and invite guests to sit and talk without rushing. In Britain, afternoon tea became a friendly tradition where friends share cups of black tea with milk alongside small cakes. Tea usually invites calm conversation and quiet focus.

Coffee, on the other hand, is closely linked to busy modern life. In cities from Rome to New York, small cafés open early for workers who need a quick boost before catching a train. Many people order a cup to go, while others sit in a lively café with laptops open. At the same time, in countries like Ethiopia and Turkey, coffee is still enjoyed slowly as an important symbol of hospitality.

Whether you prefer green tea or dark coffee, both drinks do more than wake up the body—they create moments for people to pause and connect.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: In Britain, afternoon tea became a friendly tradition where friends share cups of black tea with milk alongside small cakes.
sentences.main_clause: afternoon tea became a friendly tradition（主系表结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：where friends share... 是关系副词 where 引导的定语从句，修饰抽象名词 tradition（表示“在这个传统中”）；black tea with milk 是“加奶红茶”，alongside small cakes 表示“搭配小蛋糕”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: In cities from Rome to New York, small cafés open early for workers who need a quick boost before catching a train.
sentences.main_clause: small cafés open early for workers（主语 + 谓语 + 状语）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：who need a quick boost... 是关系代词 who 引导的定语从句，修饰 workers；before catching a train 中介词 before 后接动名词短语作时间状语。

translation:
几乎在每个国家，人们都会用一杯热饮开启新的一天或款待客人。放眼世界，茶和咖啡是最受欢迎的两种选择，但每一种饮品都承载着独特的节奏与社交习惯。

茶在亚洲和欧洲部分地区有着悠久的历史。在中国和日本，泡茶常常被视为放慢脚步的时刻。主人会仔细烧水，把茶叶放进茶壶，邀请客人不慌不忙地坐下来聊天。在英国，下午茶成了一种温馨的传统，朋友们会一边喝着加奶红茶，一边分享小蛋糕。茶通常带来平和的交谈与安静的专注。

相比之下，咖啡与忙碌的现代生活联系得更为紧密。从罗马到纽约的各大城市里，小咖啡馆一大早就开门，迎接那些赶火车前需要快速提神的上班族。许多人会点一杯打包带走，也有人坐在热闹的咖啡馆里打开电脑工作。与此同时，在埃塞俄比亚和土耳其等国家，咖啡至今依然被人们慢慢品尝，作为热情好客的重要象征。

无论你偏爱绿茶还是黑咖啡，这两种饮品的作用都不只是唤醒身体——它们更为人们创造了停下来彼此交流的时刻。

quizzes.question: What kind of atmosphere does tea usually bring according to Paragraph 2?

options.text: Fast and noisy work meetings.
Calm talks and a slower pace.
Quick breakfasts before catching a train.
Strict rules that guests must memorize.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段描述泡茶是放慢脚步的时刻，人们不慌不忙地聊天，最后总结道“Tea usually invites calm conversation and quiet focus”，选 B。

quizzes.question: What do Ethiopia and Turkey show about coffee in Paragraph 3?

options.text: Coffee is only drunk with milk in those countries.
People there never drink coffee in the morning.
Coffee can also be a slow tradition of welcoming guests.
Cafés there are mostly built for laptop workers.

quizzes.explanation: 第三段最后一句指出，在埃塞俄比亚和土耳其，咖啡依然被人们慢慢享用，是热情好客的重要象征（enjoyed slowly as an important symbol of hospitality），选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: The Benefits of Keeping a Diary（写日记的好处）
body:
Before going to sleep, many people spend their last twenty minutes scrolling through messages and short videos on their phones. When they finally turn off the light, their heads still feel crowded with random thoughts. Writing a few lines in a paper diary is a simple way to calm the mind.

You do not need to write long, beautiful paragraphs to keep a diary. Even five minutes of honest writing each evening helps you sort out your feelings. When a problem stays inside your head, it often feels huge and confusing. Once you put it down on paper, it becomes clearer and easier to handle.

A diary also protects everyday memories that we easily forget. Months later, you might smile when you read about a funny mistake in class, a warm meal with a friend, or the nervous night before a big exam. Looking back at old pages shows how much you have grown over time.

If you want to start this habit, keep a notebook and a pen next to your bed. Write down three things that happened today and one thing you learned. Over weeks and months, those quiet pages will become a trusted friend.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Once you put it down on paper, it becomes clearer and easier to handle.
sentences.main_clause: it becomes clearer and easier to handle（主系表结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Once 在此处引导时间/条件状语从句，意为“一旦”；表语是并列的形容词比较级 clearer and easier，其后接不定式 to handle 作状语（主动形式表被动含义，修饰形容词 easier）。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Looking back at old pages shows how much you have grown over time.
sentences.main_clause: Looking back at old pages shows ...（动名词短语作主语 + 谓语 + 宾语从句）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Looking back at old pages 是动名词短语作主语，因此谓语 shows 用第三人称单数；how much you have grown over time 是 how much 引导的宾语从句，使用现在完成时 have grown 强调从过去到现在的成长变化。

translation:
在睡觉前，很多人会花最后二十分钟刷手机上的消息和短视频。当他们终于关灯时，脑子里依然挤满了杂乱的念头。在纸质日记本上写几行字，是让头脑平静下来的简单方法。

写日记不需要写出又长又华丽的段落。哪怕每天晚上花五分钟坦诚地写一写，也能帮你理清思绪。当一个烦恼只留在脑海里时，它往往显得又大又令人困惑；一旦把它写到纸上，事情就会变得更清晰、更容易处理。

日记还能留住那些我们很容易遗忘的日常回忆。几个月后，当你读到课上闹过的一个有趣小错误、和朋友吃的一顿热乎饭，或者大考前那个紧张的夜晚时，你可能会会心一笑。翻看旧日记会让你看到自己在时间里的成长。

如果你想养成这个习惯，就在床边放一个笔记本和一支笔。每天记下发生的三件事和学到的一点心得。几周、几个月过去，这些安静的书页会成为你值得信赖的朋友。

quizzes.question: How does writing about a problem in a diary help according to Paragraph 2?

options.text: It lets other people solve the problem for you.
It makes the problem clearer and easier to deal with.
It improves your handwriting in five minutes.
It helps you forget everything that happened today.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段最后一句指出“Once you put it down on paper, it becomes clearer and easier to handle”，选 B。

quizzes.question: What advice does the writer give for starting a diary habit?

options.text: Write at least two full pages every morning.
Share your diary online with close friends.
Put a notebook by your bed and note three events and one lesson.
Read old diaries before checking your phone.

quizzes.explanation: 最后一段建议在床边放笔记本和笔，每天写下三件发生的事和一点学到的东西，选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why City Parks Matter（城市公园的重要性）
body:
Tall office buildings, wide roads, and shopping malls can make a modern city look impressive, yet living surrounded only by stone and glass quickly feels tiring. That is why green parks are often called the lungs and heart of a city.

On a practical level, trees and grass improve the local environment. In summer, leafy trees shade sidewalks and keep nearby streets noticeably cooler. When heavy rain falls, park soil absorbs water instead of letting it flood busy roads. Birds and small insects also rely on these green spaces as safe homes in the middle of crowded neighborhoods.

Just as importantly, city parks support our mental and physical health. Early in the morning, people jog along tree-lined paths or practice tai chi on open lawns. After lunch, office workers sit on benches for ten minutes to rest their eyes from bright computer screens. On weekends, families spread picnic blankets while children run freely on the grass.

Unlike cafes or gyms, parks welcome everyone equally without asking for money. Even a small neighborhood park reminds busy city residents to breathe deeply and enjoy a bit of nature every day.

vocabulary.meaning: 令人印象深刻的，气派的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: When heavy rain falls, park soil absorbs water instead of letting it flood busy roads.
sentences.main_clause: park soil absorbs water（主谓宾结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：When heavy rain falls 为时间状语从句；instead of letting it flood busy roads 是介词短语作状语，表示“而不是让雨水淹没繁忙道路”，其中 let + 宾语 + 动词原形 表示“让……做某事”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Even a small neighborhood park reminds busy city residents to breathe deeply and enjoy a bit of nature every day.
sentences.main_clause: a small neighborhood park reminds busy city residents to breathe ... and enjoy ...（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语 + 宾补）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：动词固定搭配 remind sb. to do sth.（提醒某人做某事）；不定式符号 to 后连接两个并列的动词原形 breathe 和 enjoy，第二个 to 省略。

translation:
高耸的写字楼、宽阔的马路和购物中心能让一座现代城市显得气派十足，但如果生活四周全是石头和玻璃，很快就会让人感到疲惫。正因如此，绿色公园常被称为城市的“肺”与“心脏”。

从实际功能来说，树木和草地能改善当地环境。夏天，枝叶茂盛的大树为人行道遮荫，让附近的街道明显凉爽一些。下大雨时，公园的泥土会吸收雨水，避免积水淹没繁忙的马路。鸟类和小昆虫也依靠这些绿地，在拥挤的街区中间拥有安全的家园。

同样重要的是，城市公园有益于我们的身心健康。清晨，人们沿着林荫小道慢跑，或者在开阔的草坪上打太极。午饭后，上班族会坐在长椅上休息十分钟，让眼睛从明亮的电脑屏幕前放松一下。到了周末，一家人铺开野餐垫，孩子们则在草地上自由奔跑。

与咖啡馆或健身房不同，公园不收费，平等地欢迎每一个人。哪怕只是一个小小的社区公园，也在提醒忙碌的城市居民每天深呼吸一下，亲近片刻自然。

quizzes.question: How do parks help a city during heavy rain according to Paragraph 2?

options.text: Their trees block strong winds from buildings.
Their soil takes in water and reduces road flooding.
Workers pump rainwater into nearby gyms.
Sidewalks dry faster under tall office buildings.

quizzes.explanation: 第二段指出大雨时“park soil absorbs water instead of letting it flood busy roads”，即公园泥土能吸水并减少道路积水，选 B。

quizzes.question: What makes city parks different from cafes or gyms in the last paragraph?

options.text: Parks are only open early in the morning.
Parks offer free access to everyone.
Parks have brighter lights for reading.
Parks are usually built outside the city.

quizzes.explanation: 最后一段第一句说明“Unlike cafes or gyms, parks welcome everyone equally without asking for money”，即公园免费对所有人开放，选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Learning from Mistakes（犯错是学习的一部分）
body:
Nobody enjoys getting a test paper back covered in red marks. In many classrooms, students hide their mistakes quickly because they fear looking silly in front of classmates. As a result, they often lose the best chance to improve.

In fact, mistakes are not signs of failure; they are useful clues. When you pronounce an English word wrong or use the wrong tense in a sentence, your error points directly to something you have not mastered yet. Without that mistake, you might keep guessing without ever noticing the gap.

Think about how young children learn to walk. A toddler falls dozens of times every single day, yet nobody says the child is bad at walking. Each fall teaches the body a tiny lesson about balance. Older learners can treat study mistakes in the same calm way.

A practical habit is keeping a small mistake notebook. Instead of only copying the right answer, write one short line explaining why you missed it—for example, "forgot past tense" or "misread the question." Reviewing those notes before your next exam turns yesterday's errors into tomorrow's confidence.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: In many classrooms, students hide their mistakes quickly because they fear looking silly in front of classmates.
sentences.main_clause: students hide their mistakes（主谓宾结构）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：because... 引导原因状语从句；fear looking silly 中 fear 后接动名词短语 looking silly 作宾语，其中 look 作系动词，意为“看起来……”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Instead of only copying the right answer, write one short line explaining why you missed it—for example, "forgot past tense" or "misread the question."
sentences.main_clause: write one short line（祈使句，省略主语 you）。
sentences.grammar: 语法点：句首 Instead of only copying... 是介词短语作状语，表示“不要只是抄写正确答案”；explaining why you missed it 是现在分词短语作后置定语，修饰 line，其中 why you missed it 是宾语从句。

translation:
没有人喜欢拿到一张布满红叉的试卷。在许多教室里，学生们会很快把错题藏起来，因为他们害怕在同学面前出丑。结果，他们往往错过了提升自己最好的机会。

事实上，错误并不是失败的标志，而是有用的线索。当你读错一个英文单词或在句子中用错时态时，这个错误正好直接指出了你还没有掌握的知识点。如果没有这次犯错，你可能会一直靠猜，却始终发现不了这个漏洞。

想想小孩子是怎么学走路的。学步期的幼儿每天都要摔倒几十次，但没有人会说这个孩子不擅长走路。每一次摔倒都在教身体学会一点关于平衡的经验。大一点的学习者也可以用同样平和的心态对待学习中的错误。

一个很实用的习惯是准备一个小错题本。不要只抄下正确答案，而是写一句简短的话说明自己为什么做错——比如“忘了用过去时”或者“看错了题目”。在下次考试前复习这些笔记，就能把昨天的失误变成明天的自信。

quizzes.question: Why do many students hide their mistakes in class?

options.text: They think red marks look ugly on paper.
They do not want to seem foolish to others.
Their teachers ask them not to show scores.
They already know all the right answers.

quizzes.explanation: 第一段第二句明确指出，学生把错误藏起来是因为“they fear looking silly in front of classmates”（害怕在同学面前显得愚蠢/出丑），选 B。

quizzes.question: What does the writer advise students to write in a mistake notebook?

options.text: Every new word from the textbook.
Only the teacher's praise on the test.
Both the correct answer and the reason for the mistake.
A list of classmates' scores for comparison.

quizzes.explanation: 最后一段指出“Instead of only copying the right answer, write one short line explaining why you missed it”，即除了正确答案外还要写出错因，选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why Trees Cool Our Cities (树木如何为城市降温)
body:
In summer, big cities often feel much hotter than the countryside. Tall buildings, dark roads, and busy cars trap heat during the day. At night, the concrete walls slowly release that warmth, so the air stays hot even after the sun goes down. Fortunately, urban trees offer a simple and natural way to fight this heat.

Trees cool cities in two main ways. First, their thick leaves block sunlight before it reaches the ground. Walking under a row of trees feels much nicer than walking on an open street. A shaded sidewalk can be several degrees cooler than a sunny one, and buildings beside trees also stay cooler inside. As a result, people do not need to run their air conditioners as hard.

Second, trees work like natural coolers through their leaves. They pull water from the soil through their roots and send small drops of water into the air. When this water turns into gas, it takes heat away from the surrounding air. One large, healthy tree can have the cooling power of several small room air conditioners.

Planting more trees does more than lower temperatures. Green streets also make neighborhoods prettier, clean the air, and give birds a safe home. For crowded cities facing hotter summers, protecting old trees and planting new ones is a smart investment for everyone.

vocabulary.meaning: 遮荫；阴凉处（shaded 为形容词“有树荫的”）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: At night, the concrete walls slowly release that warmth, so the air stays hot even after the sun goes down.
sentences.main_clause: the concrete walls release that warmth（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语），so the air stays hot（主语 + 系动词 + 表语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：本句是由连词 so 连接的并列句，表示因果关系；句首 At night 为时间状语；句末 even after the sun goes down 是由 after 引导的时间状语从句，说明空气持续炎热的时间。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When this water turns into gas, it takes heat away from the surrounding air.
sentences.main_clause: it takes heat away（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语 + 副词）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：When this water turns into gas 是由 when 引导的时间状语从句，turn into 意为“变成”；主句中的 take ... away from ... 意为“从……带走……”。

translation:
夏天，大城市往往比农村感觉热得多。高大的建筑、深色的路面和川流不息的汽车在白天会锁住热量。到了夜晚，混凝土墙体缓慢释放这些热量，因此即使太阳落山后，空气依然闷热。幸运的是，城市里的树木为对抗这种炎热提供了一种简单而自然的方法。

树木主要通过两种方式为城市降温。首先，茂密的树叶能在阳光照到地面之前将其挡住。在树荫下行走比在空旷的街道上走舒服得多。有树荫的人行道比阳光直射的路面低好几度，树木旁边的建筑物室内也会更凉爽。因此，人们就不需要把空调开得那么足。

其次，树木还能通过树叶发挥“天然空调”的作用。它们通过根部从土壤中吸收水分，再把微小的水滴散发到空气中。当这些水分蒸发成气体时，就会带走周围空气的热量。一棵高大健康的树，其降温能力相当于好几台小型室内空调。

多种树的好处不只是降低气温。绿意盎然的街道还能美化社区、净化空气，并为鸟类提供安全的栖息地。对于面临更炎热夏季的拥挤城市来说，保护老树和种植新树对每个人而言都是一项明智的投资。

quizzes.question: Why does the air in big cities stay hot at night?

options.text: Cars produce more heat after sunset.
Concrete walls slowly let out the daytime heat.
Air conditioners send warm air into the streets.
Urban trees block cool wind from entering the city.

quizzes.explanation: 由第一段第三句“At night, the concrete walls slowly release that warmth, so the air stays hot even after the sun goes down.”可知，混凝土墙体在夜间缓慢释放白天的热量，对应选项 B 中的 let out（释放）。

quizzes.question: How do trees cool the air besides giving shade?

options.text: By taking heat out of the soil with their roots.
By stopping rain from reaching the ground.
By sending water into the air through their leaves.
By covering dark roads with fallen leaves.

quizzes.explanation: 由第三段第二、三句可知，树木通过树叶把水汽散发到空气中，水分蒸发时带走周围热量，因此选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Plastic in the Ocean (海洋里的塑料垃圾)
body:
Plastic is light, cheap, and strong, so people use it every day for bottles, food bags, and packaging. However, this useful material causes a serious problem when it ends up in the ocean. Every year, millions of tons of plastic waste enter the sea through rivers, beaches, and ships.

Unlike paper or fruit skins, plastic does not break down quickly in nature. Instead, sunlight and ocean waves slowly break large pieces into tiny bits. These tiny pieces are called microplastics, and they float in the water for a very long time.

This pollution harms sea animals in many ways. Sea turtles often mistake floating plastic bags for jellyfish and eat them. Birds and fish also swallow small plastic pieces because they look like food. When plastic fills an animal's stomach, the animal feels full, stops eating real food, and may grow weak or die. Other sea creatures get trapped in old fishing nets and cannot swim freely.

Thankfully, everyone can help reduce ocean plastic. People can bring reusable cloth bags when shopping and carry a refillable water bottle instead of buying single-use bottles. Recycling properly and joining local beach cleanups also make a real difference. Small daily habits, when shared by millions of people, can keep our oceans cleaner and safer.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: However, this useful material causes a serious problem when it ends up in the ocean.
sentences.main_clause: this useful material causes a serious problem（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：when it ends up in the ocean 是时间/条件状语从句，说明塑料造成严重问题的情境；句首 However 表示转折，引出塑料带来的负面影响。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: People can bring reusable cloth bags when shopping and carry a refillable water bottle instead of buying single-use bottles.
sentences.main_clause: People can bring reusable cloth bags ... and carry a refillable water bottle（主语 + 情态动词 + 并列谓语动词短语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：when shopping 是 when they are shopping 的省略形式；instead of buying single-use bottles 为介词短语作状语，表示“而不是购买一次性水瓶”，instead of 后接动名词。

translation:
塑料既轻便、便宜又结实，所以人们每天都用它来做瓶子、食品袋和外包装。然而，这种有用的材料一旦进入海洋，就会引发严重的问题。每年都有数百万吨塑料垃圾通过河流、海滩和船只流入大海。

与纸张或果皮不同，塑料在自然界中不会很快分解。相反，阳光和海浪会慢慢把大块塑料碎裂成微小的颗粒。这些微小颗粒被称为微塑料，它们会在海水中漂浮很长时间。

这种污染在很多方面伤害着海洋动物。海龟常常把漂浮的塑料袋误认为是水母而吃掉。鸟类和鱼类也会吞下看起来像食物的小块塑料。当塑料填满动物的胃时，动物会觉得饱了，不再吃真正的食物，进而变得虚弱甚至死亡。还有些海洋生物会被废旧渔网缠住，无法自由游动。

值得庆幸的是，每个人都能帮忙减少海洋塑料。人们购物时可以自带可重复使用的布袋，随身带一个可反复灌装的水壶，而不是买一次性瓶装水。正确进行垃圾回收和参加当地海滩清理活动也能带来实实在在的改变。小小的日常习惯，只要有千百万人一起坚持，就能让我们的海洋更洁净、更安全。

quizzes.question: What happens to plastic in the ocean over time?

options.text: It turns into safe food for fish.
It breaks down completely within a few days.
Sunlight and waves break it into tiny pieces.
It sinks immediately and disappears in the sand.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第二句“Instead, sunlight and ocean waves slowly break large pieces into tiny bits.”可知，阳光和海浪会把塑料分解成微小碎片，故选 C。

quizzes.question: Why is eating plastic dangerous for sea animals?

options.text: Plastic makes them swim too fast.
Plastic fills their stomachs and stops them from eating real food.
Plastic changes the color of their skin.
Plastic forces them to leave the ocean.

quizzes.explanation: 由第三段第四句“When plastic fills an animal's stomach, the animal feels full, stops eating real food, and may grow weak or die.”可知，塑料填满胃部会让动物不再吃真食物，故选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why Bees Matter (蜜蜂对农业的重要性)
body:
When people hear the word "bee," they often think of sweet honey or a painful sting. Yet bees do something far more important than making honey. They help plants grow food for us.

Most flowering plants need pollen to move from one flower to another before they can produce seeds or fruit. When a bee lands on a flower to drink sweet nectar, yellow pollen sticks to its furry body. Then, when the bee flies to the next flower, some of that pollen falls off. Scientists call this process pollination. Without bees, many crops would not grow well.

In fact, bees help produce about one-third of the food we eat every day. Apples, strawberries, almonds, tomatoes, and coffee all depend heavily on bees. If bees disappeared, supermarkets would have far less fresh fruit and fewer vegetables, and food prices would rise sharply. Even farm animals would suffer, because many plants used for animal feed also need bees.

Sadly, bee numbers have dropped in many parts of the world due to habitat loss, farm chemicals, and changing weather. Luckily, ordinary people can help protect bees. Planting native flowers in gardens or on balconies gives bees safe food, and avoiding harmful garden sprays keeps them healthy.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: When a bee lands on a flower to drink sweet nectar, yellow pollen sticks to its furry body.
sentences.main_clause: yellow pollen sticks to its furry body（主语 + 谓语 + 介词短语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：When a bee lands on a flower to drink sweet nectar 是时间状语从句，其中 to drink sweet nectar 为动词不定式作目的状语；stick to 表示“黏附在……上”。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: If bees disappeared, supermarkets would have far less fresh fruit and fewer vegetables, and food prices would rise sharply.
sentences.main_clause: supermarkets would have far less fresh fruit and fewer vegetables 与 food prices would rise sharply 构成并列主句。
sentences.grammar: 解析：本句包含由 If 引导的条件句，用一般过去时 disappeared 和 would + 动词原形 表示对现在或未来不太可能发生情况的假设（虚拟语气入门用法）；far 修饰比较级 less，表示“少得多”。

translation:
当人们听到“蜜蜂”这个词时，往往会想到甜美的蜂蜜或被蜇的疼痛。然而，蜜蜂所做的事情比酿蜜重要得多——它们帮助植物为我们生长食物。

大多数开花植物都需要花粉从一朵花传播到另一朵花，才能结出种子或果实。当蜜蜂落在花朵上吸食甜美的花蜜时，黄色的花粉就会沾在它毛茸茸的身体上。接着，当蜜蜂飞向下一朵花时，一部分花粉就会掉落下来。科学家把这个过程称为“授粉”。没有蜜蜂，许多农作物都无法长好。

事实上，我们每天吃的食物中，大约有三分之一离不开蜜蜂的帮助。苹果、草莓、杏仁、西红柿和咖啡都高度依赖蜜蜂。如果蜜蜂消失了，超市里的新鲜水果和蔬菜就会少得多，食品价格也会大幅上涨。就连农场里的牲畜也会受到影响，因为许多用作动物饲料的植物同样需要蜜蜂授粉。

令人遗憾的是，由于栖息地丧失、农业化学品和气候变化，世界上许多地区的蜜蜂数量都在下降。好在普通人也能帮忙保护蜜蜂。在花园或阳台上种植本地花卉能为蜜蜂提供安全的食物，而避免使用有害的园艺喷雾剂则能保护它们的健康。

quizzes.question: What happens when a bee visits a flower for nectar?

options.text: It eats all the seeds inside the flower.
Pollen sticks to its body and moves to the next flower.
It turns the flower petals into honey.
It protects the plant from cold weather.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第二、三句可知，蜜蜂采花蜜时花粉会沾在身上，飞到下一朵花时部分花粉掉落，从而完成授粉，故选 B。

quizzes.question: According to the passage, how can ordinary people help bees?

options.text: By buying more coffee and almonds.
By keeping bees inside their kitchens.
By planting native flowers and avoiding harmful sprays.
By moving wild bees to big supermarkets.

quizzes.explanation: 由最后一段最后一句“Planting native flowers in gardens or on balconies gives bees safe food, and avoiding harmful garden sprays keeps them healthy.”可知，选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why Many Museums Are Free (博物馆为什么免费开放)
body:
In cities such as London, Beijing, and Washington, D.C., visitors can walk into world-famous museums without buying a ticket. At first, this might seem surprising. After all, running a large museum costs a lot of money every year for electricity, security, and careful care of old objects. So why do so many public museums stay free?

The main reason is that museums belong to the public. Many of them receive support from the government or donations from generous citizens. Because taxpayers already help pay for these buildings, people believe everyone should have an equal chance to enjoy them. A student with little pocket money should be able to see great paintings or dinosaur bones just like a wealthy traveler.

Free entry also encourages people to visit more often. When a museum charges a high ticket price, families usually go once and try to see everything in a single tired afternoon. When entry is free, visitors can drop in for just one hour, look closely at a single room, and return another weekend. In this way, learning becomes a relaxed part of daily life.

Of course, free museums still need money to survive. They often raise funds through museum shops, cafés, special paid exhibitions, and visitor donation boxes. By keeping the main doors open to all, these museums share history, art, and science with the whole community.

vocabulary.meaning: 顺道拜访；顺便进去看看

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Because taxpayers already help pay for these buildings, people believe everyone should have an equal chance to enjoy them.
sentences.main_clause: people believe (that) everyone should have an equal chance（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语从句）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：Because taxpayers already help pay for these buildings 是由 Because 引导的原因状语从句；主句中 believe 后省略了引导宾语从句的 that；to enjoy them 为不定式作定语，修饰 chance。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When a museum charges a high ticket price, families usually go once and try to see everything in a single tired afternoon.
sentences.main_clause: families usually go once and try to see everything（主语 + 并列谓语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：When a museum charges a high ticket price 是时间/条件状语从句；try to do sth. 意为“尽力做某事”；in a single tired afternoon 为介词短语作时间状语。

translation:
在伦敦、北京和华盛顿特区等城市，游客不用买票就能走进世界著名的博物馆。乍一听，这似乎让人有些惊讶。毕竟，运营一座大型博物馆每年在电费、安保和文物精心养护方面都需要花费大量资金。那么，为什么这么多公共博物馆依然免费开放呢？

最主要的原因在于博物馆属于公众。其中许多博物馆都得到政府资助或热心市民的捐赠。既然纳税人已经为这些场馆出了力，人们便认为每个人都应该有平等的机会去欣赏它们。一个零花钱不多的学生，也应该像富裕的游客一样，能够看到伟大的画作或恐龙化石。

免费入场还能鼓励人们更频繁地参观。如果博物馆门票很贵，一家人往往只去一次，并且试图在一个疲惫的下午把所有展区都看完。而免费开放时，参观者可以只顺道逛上一个小时，仔细看看某一个展厅，下个周末再来看别的。这样一来，学习就成了日常生活中轻松自然的一部分。

当然，免费博物馆依然需要资金来维持运转。它们通常会通过博物馆商店、咖啡馆、收费特展以及游客捐款箱来筹集经费。通过向所有人敞开大门，这些博物馆得以与整个社会分享历史、艺术和科学。

quizzes.question: Why do many public museums offer free entry?

options.text: They do not need much money to run.
They belong to the public and are supported by taxes or donations.
Few people want to visit museums if they have to pay.
They only show paintings from local students.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第一至三句可知，博物馆属于公众，受政府拨款（纳税人出资）或市民捐助支持，因此大家都应有平等机会免费参观，故选 B。

quizzes.question: How do free museums still make money?

options.text: By charging extra money for electricity.
By selling old dinosaur bones.
Through shops, cafés, special paid shows, and donation boxes.
By asking every visitor to buy a yearly ticket.

quizzes.explanation: 由最后一段第二句“They often raise funds through museum shops, cafés, special paid exhibitions, and visitor donation boxes.”可知，选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Teamwork and Listening (团队合作与倾听他人)
body:
At school and in the workplace, many projects are too big for one person to finish alone. Working in a team allows people with different skills to share ideas and divide tasks. However, good teamwork does not happen automatically. One of the most important skills behind every strong team is active listening.

In many group discussions, people are eager to share their own opinions. While someone else is speaking, they might already be planning what to say next. As a result, they miss useful details and make their teammates feel ignored. Over time, quiet members stop speaking up, and the group loses valuable ideas.

Active listening means giving the speaker your full attention. When a teammate talks, look at them, put down your phone, and let them finish their thought without interrupting. After they speak, you can ask a short question or repeat their main point in your own words. This simple habit shows respect and helps everyone avoid misunderstandings.

Great teams are not built only by the loudest voices. When every member feels heard, trust grows quickly. People become more willing to help one another, solve problems together, and turn small ideas into strong results.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: While someone else is speaking, they might already be planning what to say next.
sentences.main_clause: they might already be planning what to say next（主语 + 情态动词 + 进行时谓语 + 宾语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：While someone else is speaking 为 while 引导的时间状语从句，表示两个动作同时发生；what to say next 是“疑问词 + 不定式”结构，作 planning 的宾语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When a teammate talks, look at them, put down your phone, and let them finish their thought without interrupting.
sentences.main_clause: look at them, put down your phone, and let them finish their thought（三个并列祈使句）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：主句用三个并列的动词原形开头构成祈使句，提出具体建议；let sb. do sth. 表示“让某人做某事”；without interrupting 是介词短语作伴随状语。

translation:
在学校和职场中，许多项目都过于庞大，一个人无法独立完成。团队合作让拥有不同技能的人能够分享想法、分工协作。然而，良好的团队合作并不会自然而然地发生。每一支优秀团队背后最重要的能力之一，就是“积极倾听”。

在许多小组讨论中，人们总是急于表达自己的观点。当别人在发言时，他们可能已经在盘算自己接下来要说什么了。结果，他们漏掉了有用的细节，也让队友觉得自己被忽视了。久而久之，性格内向的成员就不再发言，整个团队也会失去宝贵的创意。

积极倾听意味着把全部注意力放在说话人身上。当队友发言时，看着对方，放下手机，不要打断，让他们把话说完。等对方讲完后，你可以提一个简短的问题，或者用自己的话复述一遍他们的核心意思。这个简单的习惯能体现出尊重，也能帮助大家避免误解。

优秀的团队从来不是只靠嗓门最大的人建成的。当每位成员都感到自己被倾听时，信任就会迅速建立起来。大家会更愿意彼此帮助、共同解决问题，并把小小的灵感变成出色的成果。

quizzes.question: What often happens when people only focus on what they want to say next?

options.text: The meeting finishes much earlier.
Teammates feel ignored and stop sharing ideas.
Everyone agrees on the same plan.
The project becomes easier for one person.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第三、四句可知，只顾着准备自己下一句要说什么会让人漏掉细节，让队友感到被忽视，长此以往沉默的成员就不再发言，团队失去好想法，故选 B。

quizzes.question: Which of the following is a sign of active listening?

options.text: Checking messages on your phone while others talk.
Stopping a speaker to correct their grammar.
Asking a short question after your teammate finishes.
Speaking louder than everyone else in the room.

quizzes.explanation: 由第三段第三句“After they speak, you can ask a short question or repeat their main point in your own words.”可知，在队友说完后简短提问是积极倾听的表现，故选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: The Charm of Train Travel (火车旅行的魅力)
body:
