Today, airplanes can carry passengers across a country in just a few hours. Still, millions of travelers choose to take the train instead. For many people, train travel is not just a way to reach a city; it is an enjoyable part of the holiday itself.

Unlike airports, which are often far outside the city, train stations usually sit right in the center of town. Travelers do not have to arrive two hours early or pass through long security lines. They can simply step onto the platform, find their seat, and relax as the train pulls away smoothly.

Once the journey begins, a train offers a special kind of comfort. There is more room to stretch your legs, walk to the dining car, or read a book without feeling crowded. Best of all, big windows frame the changing countryside like a moving painting. You can watch green fields, quiet villages, snow-covered mountains, and rivers pass by slowly.

Train travel is also kinder to the planet. Modern electric trains produce much less carbon pollution per passenger than airplanes or private cars. Whether you take a fast high-speed train for work or a slow scenic line for fun, riding the rails gives you time to slow down and truly see the world.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Unlike airports, which are often far outside the city, train stations usually sit right in the center of town.
sentences.main_clause: train stations usually sit right in the center of town（主语 + 谓语 + 地点状语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：Unlike airports 是介词短语作对比状语；which are often far outside the city 是由 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，用来补充说明 airports 的位置特点。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Whether you take a fast high-speed train for work or a slow scenic line for fun, riding the rails gives you time to slow down and truly see the world.
sentences.main_clause: riding the rails gives you time to slow down and truly see the world（动名词短语作主语 + 谓语 + 间接宾语 + 直接宾语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：Whether ... or ... 引导让步状语从句，意为“无论……还是……”；主句中动名词短语 riding the rails 作主语，谓语动词用单数 gives。

translation:
如今，飞机只需几个小时就能把乘客送往国家的另一端。即便如此，仍有数百万旅客选择坐火车出行。对许多人来说，火车旅行不仅仅是到达某座城市的方式，它本身就是假期中令人愉悦的一部分。

机场通常建在远离市区的地方，而火车站往往就坐落在城市中心。旅客不必提前两个小时到站，也不用排长长的安检队伍。他们只需走上站台、找到座位，在列车平稳驶离时放松下来即可。

旅程一旦开始，火车便能带来一种独特的舒适感。车厢里有更宽敞的空间，你可以伸伸腿、走到餐车去，或者毫无拥挤感地读一本书。最棒的是，宽大的车窗把沿途变换的乡村风景框成了一幅流动的画卷。你可以看着绿色的田野、安静的村庄、白雪覆盖的山峦和河流缓缓掠过。

火车旅行对地球也更加友好。按每位乘客计算，现代电力机车产生的碳污染比飞机或私家车少得多。无论你是为了出差乘坐高速列车，还是为了休闲选择慢速观光线路，乘火车旅行都能给你留出时间放慢脚步，真正去欣赏这个世界。

quizzes.question: What is one advantage of train stations compared with airports?

options.text: They always have bigger dining rooms.
They are usually located in the city center.
They require passengers to arrive two hours early.
They offer free tickets to students.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第一句“Unlike airports, which are often far outside the city, train stations usually sit right in the center of town.”可知，火车站通常位于市中心，故选 B。

quizzes.question: Why is train travel better for the environment?

options.text: Trains only run during the daytime.
Electric trains make less carbon pollution per passenger.
Trains help plant trees along the tracks.
Train tickets use no paper at all.

quizzes.explanation: 由第四段第二句“Modern electric trains produce much less carbon pollution per passenger than airplanes or private cars.”可知，现代电力火车人均碳污染更少，故选 B。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Why We Dream (为什么我们会做梦)
body:
Almost everyone dreams, even if we sometimes forget our dreams by breakfast. During a typical night of sleep, our brains go through several stages. Most vivid dreams happen during a stage called REM sleep, when our eyes move quickly behind closed eyelids and our brain becomes almost as active as it is during the day.

For centuries, people wondered why dreams happen. Today, scientists still do not have one single answer, but they have discovered several strong clues. First, dreams seem to help us organize memories. Throughout the day, we take in thousands of sights, words, and feelings. At night, the brain sorts through this information, keeps what matters, and throws away useless details.

Second, dreaming may help us deal with strong emotions. Have you ever noticed that a scary event feels slightly less painful after a good night's sleep? During dreams, the brain replays emotional moments in a safe environment, which can calm worry and reduce stress.

Finally, some researchers believe dreams act like a quiet rehearsal for real life. When we dream about taking a difficult test or missing a bus, our brain practices reacting to challenges. Whatever the exact reason, healthy sleep and dreams clearly keep our minds sharp and balanced.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: At night, the brain sorts through this information, keeps what matters, and throws away useless details.
sentences.main_clause: the brain sorts through this information, keeps what matters, and throws away useless details（主语 + 三个并列谓语动词短语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：what matters 是由 what 引导的宾语从句，作 keeps 的宾语，意为“重要的东西”；三个并列动作清晰展现了大脑整理记忆的过程。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: During dreams, the brain replays emotional moments in a safe environment, which can calm worry and reduce stress.
sentences.main_clause: the brain replays emotional moments in a safe environment（主语 + 谓语 + 宾语 + 地点状语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：, which can calm worry and reduce stress 是由 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，这里的 which 指代前面整个主句所描述的“大脑在安全环境中重演情绪时刻”这一过程。

translation:
几乎每个人都会做梦，尽管有时吃早饭时我们就把梦忘光了。在一晚正常的睡眠中，大脑会经历好几个阶段。大多数逼真的梦都发生在“快速眼动睡眠（REM）”阶段——此时，我们的眼球会在紧闭的眼皮后面快速转动，大脑的活跃程度几乎和白天一样。

几个世纪以来，人们一直好奇为什么会做梦。如今，科学家们虽然还没有找到唯一确切的答案，但已经发现了几条有力的线索。首先，梦似乎能帮助我们整理记忆。白天里，我们接收了成千上万的画面、话语和感受。到了夜晚，大脑会梳理这些信息，留下重要的内容，扔掉无用的细节。

其次，做梦或许能帮助我们处理强烈的情绪。你有没有注意过，睡一觉之后，原本让人害怕的事好像没那么痛心了？在梦中，大脑会在一个安全的环境里重放带有情绪的片段，这有助于平复焦虑、减轻压力。

最后，一些研究者认为，梦就像是对现实生活的一次安静排练。当我们梦到参加一场很难的考试或错过公交车时，大脑其实是在练习如何应对挑战。无论真正的原因是什么，健康的睡眠和梦境显然能让我们的头脑保持敏锐与平衡。

quizzes.question: When do most vivid dreams take place?

options.text: Right before we eat breakfast.
During REM sleep when the brain is very active.
Only when we take a difficult test.
During the quietest stage when the brain stops working.

quizzes.explanation: 由第一段第三句“Most vivid dreams happen during a stage called REM sleep, when our eyes move quickly behind closed eyelids and our brain becomes almost as active as it is during the day.”可知，选 B。

quizzes.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a possible purpose of dreams?

options.text: Organizing daily memories.
Reducing worry and stress.
Practicing how to face challenges.
Learning new foreign languages automatically.

quizzes.explanation: 文章第二、三、四段分别提到梦有助于整理记忆（A）、平复情绪减轻压力（B）以及模拟应对挑战（C），并未提及“自动学会外语”，因此选 D。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: How Music Helps Us Relax (音乐如何帮助放松)
body:
After a long day of studying or working, many people put on headphones and press play on their favorite songs. Within minutes, their shoulders drop and their minds feel lighter. Music is more than simple entertainment; it can have a real, physical effect on the human body.

Scientists have found that slow, gentle music helps slow down a fast heartbeat and lower blood pressure. When we listen to calm melodies—such as soft piano pieces, acoustic guitar, or quiet nature sounds—our brains release fewer stress chemicals. At the same time, music can increase brain chemicals linked to comfort and happiness. That is why hospitals sometimes play soft music in waiting rooms to help nervous patients feel at ease.

Music also works well because it gives a busy mind something pleasant to focus on. When you feel worried about tomorrow's exam or a hard task, your thoughts may run in circles. Following a familiar rhythm helps break that cycle and brings your attention back to the present moment.

Of course, everyone relaxes to different sounds. Some people prefer classical music, while others feel calmest listening to jazz or folk songs. Whenever life feels noisy and rushed, ten quiet minutes with the right playlist can be an easy way to recharge.

vocabulary.meaning: 原地打转；反复胡思乱想

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: That is why hospitals sometimes play soft music in waiting rooms to help nervous patients feel at ease.
sentences.main_clause: That is why ...（主语 + 系动词 + 表语从句）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：why hospitals sometimes play soft music ... 是由 why 引导的表语从句，意为“那就是为什么……”；to help nervous patients feel at ease 为目的状语，help sb. (to) do sth. 后接不带 to 的不定式 feel。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Some people prefer classical music, while others feel calmest listening to jazz or folk songs.
sentences.main_clause: Some people prefer classical music 与 others feel calmest 由 while 连接。
sentences.grammar: 解析：while 在此表示对比，意为“而，然而”；listening to jazz or folk songs 是现在分词短语作伴随/方式状语，说明感到最平静时的状态。

translation:
在学习或工作了漫长的一天后，许多人会戴上耳机，播放自己最喜欢的歌曲。几分钟之内，紧绷的肩膀放松下来，心情也变得轻快。音乐不只是简单的消遣，它还能对人体产生实实在在的生理影响。

科学家发现，舒缓轻柔的音乐有助于减慢过快的心跳并降低血压。当我们聆听平静的旋律时——比如柔和的钢琴曲、原声吉他或轻柔的自然声响——大脑释放的压力激素就会减少。同时，音乐还能增加与舒适和愉悦感相关的脑内化学物质。正因如此，医院有时会在候诊室播放轻音乐，帮助紧张的病人放松心情。

音乐之所以管用，还在于它能给忙碌的大脑一个愉悦的专注点。当你为明天的考试或一项艰巨的任务感到焦虑时，思绪可能会不停地原地打转。跟着熟悉的节奏走，能帮你打破这种循环，把注意力拉回到当下。

当然，每个人偏好的放松音乐各不相同。有些人喜欢古典乐，而另一些人听爵士乐或民谣时最能平静下来。每当生活显得嘈杂而匆忙时，用一份合适的歌单静静听上十分钟，就是一种简单的“充电”方式。

quizzes.question: What physical effect can slow, gentle music have on our body?

options.text: It makes the heart beat faster.
It helps lower blood pressure and calm stress.
It stops the brain from thinking during sleep.
It gives people more energy to run quickly.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第一、二句可知，舒缓的音乐能放慢心跳、降低血压并减少大脑释放压力化学物质，故选 B。

quizzes.question: Why do hospitals sometimes play soft music in waiting rooms?

options.text: To make the waiting rooms look more modern.
To remind doctors when to start working.
To help nervous patients feel more relaxed.
To cover the noise of busy streets outside.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段最后一句“That is why hospitals sometimes play soft music in waiting rooms to help nervous patients feel at ease.”可知，是为了让紧张的病人感到放松（at ease），故选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: Exploring Deep Space (太空探索的简单科普)
body:
Since ancient times, human beings have looked up at the night sky and wondered what lies beyond the stars. Over the last seventy years, space exploration has turned many of those questions into real discoveries. Rockets, satellites, and space telescopes now help us study planets and galaxies far from Earth.

Why do countries spend so much time and money exploring space? First, space science helps us understand our own planet better. Weather satellites high above Earth track storms, measure sea temperatures, and warn communities before dangerous floods or typhoons arrive. GPS satellites also guide ships, airplanes, and everyday map apps on our phones.

Second, space exploration drives new technology. Many tools invented for astronauts—such as better water filters, light materials, and scratch-resistant glasses—later become useful products in normal homes and hospitals.

Today, scientists are sending robotic rovers to Mars and looking for signs of ancient water on distant moons. Even though sending people deep into space remains difficult and expensive, human curiosity keeps pushing us forward. Exploring the universe teaches us not only about faraway worlds, but also about how precious and fragile our home planet truly is.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Weather satellites high above Earth track storms, measure sea temperatures, and warn communities before dangerous floods or typhoons arrive.
sentences.main_clause: Weather satellites track storms, measure sea temperatures, and warn communities（主语 + 三个并列谓语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：high above Earth 为后置定语修饰 satellites；before dangerous floods or typhoons arrive 是时间状语从句，说明发出预警的时机。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Even though sending people deep into space remains difficult and expensive, human curiosity keeps pushing us forward.
sentences.main_clause: human curiosity keeps pushing us forward（主语 + 谓语 + 动名词宾语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：Even though 引导让步状语从句，意为“尽管，即使”；从句中动名词短语 sending people deep into space 作主语；主句 keep doing sth. 表示“持续做某事”。

translation:
自古以来，人类就仰望夜空，好奇群星之外究竟有什么。在过去的七十年里，太空探索把许多这样的疑问变成了真实的发现。如今，火箭、人造卫星和太空望远镜帮助我们研究距离地球十分遥远的行星与星系。

各国为什么要花这么多时间和金钱去探索太空呢？首先，太空科学能帮助我们更好地了解自己的星球。地球上空的气象卫星可以追踪风暴、测量海水温度，并在危险的洪水或台风到来前向各地发出预警。全球定位（GPS）卫星还为船只、飞机以及我们手机上的日常地图软件提供导航。

其次，太空探索推动了新技术的发展。许多最初为宇航员发明的工具——比如更好的净水过滤器、轻便材料以及防刮镜片——后来都成了普通家庭和医院里的实用产品。

如今，科学家们正把自动探测车送上火星，并在遥远的卫星上寻找远古水源的痕迹。尽管把人类送往深空依然既困难又昂贵，但人类的好奇心不断推动着我们向前迈进。探索宇宙不仅让我们了解遥远的世界，也让我们明白地球家园是何等珍贵而脆弱。

quizzes.question: How do weather satellites help people on Earth?

options.text: They control the speed of ocean winds.
They track storms and give early warnings before disasters.
They carry clean water from space to dry cities.
They make GPS apps run without electricity.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第三句“Weather satellites high above Earth track storms, measure sea temperatures, and warn communities before dangerous floods or typhoons arrive.”可知，气象卫星追踪风暴并在灾害来临前发出预警，故选 B。

quizzes.question: What does the third paragraph tell us about space technology?

options.text: It is only useful for astronauts on the Moon.
It costs too much for normal hospitals to use.
Tools made for space often improve everyday life on Earth.
It has stopped developing in recent years.

quizzes.explanation: 由第三段第二句可知，为宇航员发明的许多工具后来在普通家庭和医院中也成了实用产品，说明太空技术改善了日常生活，故选 C。

stage_label: 第一阶段 · 打底适应期
title: A Letter to My Future Self (给未来自己的一封信)
body:
Dear Future Me,

I am writing this letter on a quiet Sunday evening, wondering what your life looks like three years from now. Right now, I am trying hard to build better study habits. Sometimes the road feels long, and I still make plenty of mistakes when I read English or solve difficult problems. Even so, I want you to remember how seriously I tried today.

Over the next few years, I hope you do not give up on the small goals we set together. Read a little every morning, stay curious, and keep asking questions when you do not understand something. Real progress rarely happens overnight. Instead, it grows quietly from steady, daily effort.

I also hope you take good care of your health and your friendships. Do not let busy schedules push away the people who care about you. Go for a walk when you feel tired, get enough sleep before big days, and forgive yourself when things do not go as planned.

When you open this letter in the future, maybe some dreams will already have come true, and maybe new challenges will stand before you. Either way, be proud of how far you have come—and keep moving forward with courage.

Warmly,
Your Younger Self

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: I am writing this letter on a quiet Sunday evening, wondering what your life looks like three years from now.
sentences.main_clause: I am writing this letter（主语 + 现在进行时谓语 + 宾语）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：wondering what your life looks like three years from now 是现在分词短语作伴随状语；其中 what your life looks like ... 为 what 引导的宾语从句，作 wondering 的宾语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Do not let busy schedules push away the people who care about you.
sentences.main_clause: Do not let busy schedules push away the people（否定祈使句）。
sentences.grammar: 解析：let ... do ... 表示“让……做……”；who care about you 是由 who 引导的定语从句，修饰先行词 the people。

translation:
亲爱的未来的我：

我是在一个安静的周日夜晚写下这封信的，心里好奇着三年后的你会过着怎样的生活。眼下，我正在努力养成更好的学习习惯。有时前路感觉很漫长，读英语或解难题时我也依然会犯不少错误。即便如此，我希望你记得今天的我是多么认真地在努力。

在接下来的几年里，我希望你不要放弃我们一起定下的小目标。每天早上读一点书，保持好奇心，遇到不懂的问题就继续发问。真正的进步很少在一夜之间发生，相反，它是在每天稳定持续的努力中悄悄生长出来的。

我也希望你好好照顾自己的健康，珍惜身边的友谊。不要让忙碌的日程把关心你的人推远。觉得累的时候就去散散步，在重要的日子之前保证充足睡眠，当事情不如计划那样顺利时，也要学会原谅自己。

当你在未来打开这封信时，也许有些梦想已经成真，也许新的挑战正摆在你面前。无论如何，都要为自己走过的路感到骄傲——然后带着勇气继续向前走。

温暖地问候，
年轻时的你

quizzes.question: What is the writer doing at the time of writing the letter?

options.text: Celebrating the end of a three-year trip.
Working hard to build better study habits.
Teaching English to young students.
Looking for a new job on Sunday morning.

quizzes.explanation: 由第一段第二句“Right now, I am trying hard to build better study habits.”可知，写信时作者正努力养成更好的学习习惯，故选 B。

quizzes.question: According to the letter, how does real progress happen?

options.text: It usually arrives overnight without hard work.
It only happens when you never make mistakes.
It grows from steady, daily effort over time.
It depends on avoiding all difficult problems.

quizzes.explanation: 由第二段第三、四句“Real progress rarely happens overnight. Instead, it grows quietly from steady, daily effort.”可知，真正的进步源于每天持续稳定的努力，故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: The Rise of Flexible Work（灵活办公与混合办公模式）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
For decades, the nine-to-five office routine was treated as an unbreakable rule of modern employment. Millions of workers woke up early, spent hours in crowded trains or heavy traffic, and sat at their desks until evening. In recent years, however, a quiet revolution has reshaped how companies and employees view the workplace. Flexible and hybrid work models, which allow staff to split their time between home and the office, have moved from rare perks to mainstream expectations.

The shift accelerated during the global health crisis, when businesses were forced to operate remotely almost overnight. Although many managers initially worried that productivity would drop without direct supervision, surveys later showed that most employees remained just as efficient—and often happier—when given greater control over their schedules. Freed from daily commutes, workers gained extra hours that could be invested in exercise, family life, or personal rest. In fact, several recent recruitment reports suggest that job seekers now turn down offers if remote options are missing completely.

Yet hybrid work is far from a simple solution without drawbacks. Critics argue that young professionals, who rely on casual conversations with experienced colleagues to learn workplace skills, may feel isolated when working from home too often. In addition, the boundary between professional duties and private life can easily become blurred if laptops remain open late into the night. Some team leaders also point out that spontaneous brainstorming is harder to spark during scheduled video calls.

To address these challenges, forward-thinking companies are experimenting with structured hybrid policies. Some firms designate Tuesday through Thursday as core collaboration days, while leaving Mondays and Fridays for focused individual work. Others redesign their offices into open meeting hubs rather than rows of identical cubicles. As technology continues to evolve, one thing is clear: work is no longer defined merely by the building where it is performed, but by the results that are delivered.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Flexible and hybrid work models, which allow staff to split their time between home and the office, have moved from rare perks to mainstream expectations.
sentences.main_clause: Flexible and hybrid work models have moved from rare perks to mainstream expectations.（灵活和混合办公模式已从罕见福利变成主流期待。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：which allow staff to split their time between home and the office 为非限制性定语从句，修饰先行词 Flexible and hybrid work models，补充说明混合办公的具体形式。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Although many managers initially worried that productivity would drop without direct supervision, surveys later showed that most employees remained just as efficient—and often happier—when given greater control over their schedules.
sentences.main_clause: surveys later showed that most employees remained just as efficient.（调查后来显示大多数员工依然保持同样高效。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Although... 引导让步状语从句，内嵌 that 引导的宾语从句；主句中 when given greater control... 为“连词 + 过去分词”构成的状语从句省略形式（完整为 when they were given...），含被动含义。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: As technology continues to evolve, one thing is clear: work is no longer defined merely by the building where it is performed, but by the results that are delivered.
sentences.main_clause: work is no longer defined by the building, but by the results.（工作不再由办公大楼来定义，而是由交付的成果来定义。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：As technology continues to evolve 为时间状语从句；is defined 和 are delivered 均为一般现在时被动语态；where it is performed 和 that are delivered 分别为定语从句，修饰 building 和 results。

translation:
几十年来，“朝九晚五”的办公室作息一直被视为现代职场不可打破的铁律。数以百万计的打工人早早起床，在拥挤的地铁或严重的堵车中耗费数小时，然后坐在工位上一直忙到傍晚。然而近年来，一场静悄悄的变革重塑了企业和员工对工作场所的看法。允许员工在家与办公室之间分配时间的灵活办公及混合办公模式，已经从昔日少见的额外福利变成了如今的主流期待。

这一转变在全球公共卫生危机期间大大加快，当时企业几乎在一夜之间被迫开展远程运营。尽管许多管理者最初担心没有直接监督会导致效率下降，但随后的调查表明，当员工对自己的日程拥有更大掌控权时，大多数人依然保持着同样的高效——而且往往心情更愉快。从日常通勤中解放出来后，员工获得了额外的时间，可以投入到锻炼、家庭生活或个人休息中。事实上，近期的几份招聘报告表明，如果完全没有远程办公选项，求职者如今甚至会拒绝录用通知。

不过，混合办公绝非一个毫无弊端的简单方案。批评人士指出，年轻职场人往往依赖与经验丰富的同事闲聊来学习工作技能，如果过于频繁地居家办公，他们可能会感到孤立。此外，如果笔记本电脑直到深夜仍开着，工作职责与私人生活之间的界限就很容易变得模糊。一些团队负责人还指出，在按日程安排的视频会议中，很难激发出自发的头脑风暴。

为了应对这些挑战，具有前瞻性的公司正在尝试制定结构化的混合办公政策。一些公司将周二至周四定为核心协作日，而把周一和周五留给专注的个人工作。另一些公司则把办公室重新设计成开放式会议中心，而不是一排排千篇一律的隔间。随着技术不断演进，有一点已经十分明确：工作不再仅仅由它所在的建筑来定义，而是由所交付的成果来衡量。

quizzes.question: What did surveys find about employees working remotely during the global health crisis?

options.text: They needed stricter supervision from managers.
They struggled to complete their daily tasks on time.
They stayed productive and often felt more satisfied.
They preferred spending more time commuting to work.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：C
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段第二句指出，调查显示当员工被赋予更多日程掌控权时，大多数人依然保持同样高效，而且往往更开心（just as efficient—and often happier），因此选 C。

quizzes.question: According to the passage, what is a potential disadvantage of hybrid work?

options.text: Companies have to spend more money on office cubicles.
Young staff may lose informal learning opportunities and feel lonely.
Employees are less likely to use modern technology at home.
Managers refuse to set clear schedules for collaboration days.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节推理题。第三段提到，批评者认为年轻职场人依赖与资深同事的日常交流学习技能，频繁居家办公可能感到孤立（feel isolated），这与 B 项吻合。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Digital Detox Among Young People（年轻人的“数字排毒”趋势）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
In an age where smartphones are rarely out of reach, a growing number of young adults are choosing to step back from constant connectivity. Known as a "digital detox," the practice involves deliberately limiting screen time or abandoning social media for days, weeks, or even months. Rather than rejecting technology completely, many participants simply want to regain control over their attention and protect their mental well-being.

For university students and young professionals, the pressure to stay online can feel exhausting. Notifications arrive around the clock, and carefully edited photos on social platforms often create unnecessary anxiety about appearance, career progress, and social life. When every quiet moment is filled with endless scrolling, people rarely have space to think deeply or enjoy real-world conversations without distraction. Psychologists warn that this continuous stream of updates keeps the brain in a state of mild stress, even during supposed leisure hours.

To break this habit, some young people are turning to surprisingly low-tech solutions. Sales of basic feature phones—devices that can make calls and send text messages but cannot run social apps—have seen a noticeable rise among Generation Z consumers. Others join weekend "offline clubs" in major cities, where phones are locked inside pouches at the door so guests can read books, play board games, or chat face to face. A few universities have even launched screen-free reading hours in campus cafés to encourage students to unwind together.

Early adopters say the benefits become clear within just a few days. After the initial discomfort of missing online updates fades, many report sleeping better, feeling calmer, and noticing small details in their surroundings again. While digital tools remain essential for study and work, the digital detox movement reminds a hyper-connected generation that true rest sometimes begins the moment a screen is switched off.

vocabulary.meaning: 显而易见的；值得注意的
采用；采纳（early adopter 早期尝试者）
高度互联的；过度联网的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: In an age where smartphones are rarely out of reach, a growing number of young adults are choosing to step back from constant connectivity.
sentences.main_clause: a growing number of young adults are choosing to step back from constant connectivity.（越来越多的年轻人正选择从持续不断的网络连接中抽身。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：where smartphones are rarely out of reach 是由关系副词 where 引导的定语从句，修饰先行词 age（时代），在从句中作时间/抽象地点状语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Others join weekend "offline clubs" in major cities, where phones are locked inside pouches at the door so guests can read books, play board games, or chat face to face.
sentences.main_clause: Others join weekend "offline clubs" in major cities.（另一些人则加入大城市的周末“线下俱乐部”。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：where phones are locked... 为非限制性定语从句，修饰 offline clubs，其中 are locked 为被动语态；so guests can... 引导目的状语从句。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: While digital tools remain essential for study and work, the digital detox movement reminds a hyper-connected generation that true rest sometimes begins the moment a screen is switched off.
sentences.main_clause: the digital detox movement reminds a hyper-connected generation that...（数字排毒运动提醒高度互联的一代人……）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：While... 引导让步状语从句（意为“尽管”）；that 引导宾语从句；the moment... 相当于连词（一……就……）引导时间状语从句，内含被动语态 is switched off。

translation:
在一个智能手机几乎触手可及的时代，越来越多的年轻人正选择从全天候的网络连接中后退一步。这种被称为“数字排毒”的做法，是指刻意限制屏幕使用时间，或暂停使用社交媒体数天、数周甚至数月。许多参与者并不是要彻底排斥科技，他们只是想重新夺回对自己注意力的掌控权，并保护自己的心理健康。

对大学生和年轻职场人而言，时刻保持在线的压力令人筋疲力尽。消息提示昼夜不停地弹出，而社交平台上经过精心修饰的照片，常常会让人对外貌、职业发展和社交生活产生不必要的焦虑。当每一个安静的片刻都被无休止的刷屏填满时，人们就很少有空间去深度思考，或者不受干扰地享受现实生活中的交谈。心理学家警告称，这种源源不断的信息流会让大脑在所谓的休闲时间里也处于轻度紧张状态。

为了戒掉这一习惯，一些年轻人正转向出人意料的低科技办法。基础功能机——只能打电话和发短信、却无法运行社交软件的设备——在 Z 世代消费者中的销量出现了明显增长。还有人加入大城市的周末“线下俱乐部”，在进门时就把手机锁进小袋子里，以便客人们读书、玩桌游或面对面聊天。少数大学甚至在校园咖啡馆推出了“无屏幕阅读时段”，鼓励学生聚在一起放松身心。

早期尝试者表示，短短几天内就能感受到明显益处。在最初因错过线上动态而产生的不适感消退后，许多人反映睡眠质量有所提高，心情更平静，也能重新留意到周围环境中的细微之处。尽管数字工具在学习和工作中依然不可或缺，但数字排毒运动提醒着这一代高度互联的年轻人：真正的休息，有时正是从关掉屏幕的那一刻开始的。

quizzes.question: Why do many young adults practice a "digital detox"?

options.text: Because they want to abandon modern technology forever.
Because they hope to take back control of their attention.
Because universities forbid students from using smartphones.
Because social media platforms charge high monthly fees.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第一段最后一句明确指出：Rather than rejecting technology completely, many participants simply want to regain control over their attention and protect their mental well-being. 故选 B。

quizzes.question: What happens at the weekend "offline clubs" mentioned in Paragraph 3?

options.text: Guests test the latest smartphones together.
Participants share edited photos from social platforms.
Phones are put away so people can interact in person.
Members learn how to design basic feature phones.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：C
   - 解析：细节理解题。第三段提到在“线下俱乐部”，手机在门口被锁进袋子里，客人们可以读书、玩桌游或面对面聊天（chat face to face），故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Online vs. Classroom Learning（在线教育能否替代传统课堂）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
Over the past decade, digital platforms have transformed how knowledge is shared across the world. From recorded university lectures to interactive language apps, online education has made learning more accessible than ever before. Yet as virtual courses continue to expand, educators and students alike are asking a central question: can online platforms ever truly replace the traditional classroom?

There is no doubt that digital learning offers remarkable convenience. Students who live in remote towns can now watch lessons taught by leading professors without leaving home, while working adults can study new skills at midnight after their daily jobs end. Because online materials can be paused, replayed, and reviewed at an individual pace, learners who need extra time to understand complex ideas are no longer left behind by a fast-moving lecture. Moreover, digital quizzes provide instant scores, allowing students to identify weak areas before an important exam arrives.

However, education involves much more than transferring information from a screen to a notebook. In a physical classroom, teachers notice subtle signs—a puzzled expression or a sudden silence—that tell them when an explanation needs to be adjusted. Classmates also motivate one another through group discussions, shared deadlines, and spontaneous debates that rarely happen with the same energy in an online chat box. Without the structure of regular class meetings, even highly motivated learners may struggle to stay disciplined when studying alone at home.

For these reasons, most experts believe that the future of education lies in balance rather than replacement. Digital tools are expected to remain a powerful supplement that widens access and personalizes practice. Still, the human connection, immediate feedback, and sense of community that are built inside a real classroom cannot easily be copied by software alone.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Students who live in remote towns can now watch lessons taught by leading professors without leaving home, while working adults can study new skills at midnight after their daily jobs end.
sentences.main_clause: Students can now watch lessons, while working adults can study new skills.（学生现在可以观看课程，而上班族可以在午夜学习新技能。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：who live in remote towns 为定语从句修饰 Students；taught by leading professors 为过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 lessons；while 连接两个对比并列分句，after... 引导时间状语从句。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Because online materials can be paused, replayed, and reviewed at an individual pace, learners who need extra time to understand complex ideas are no longer left behind by a fast-moving lecture.
sentences.main_clause: learners are no longer left behind by a fast-moving lecture.（学习者不再被节奏飞快的讲座落下。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Because... 引导原因状语从句，内含被动语态 can be paused, replayed, and reviewed；主句中 who need extra time... 为定语从句修饰 learners，are no longer left behind 为被动语态。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Still, the human connection, immediate feedback, and sense of community that are built inside a real classroom cannot easily be copied by software alone.
sentences.main_clause: the human connection, immediate feedback, and sense of community cannot easily be copied by software alone.（真实课堂中建立的人际联结、即时反馈和集体感，仅靠软件难以轻易复制。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：that are built inside a real classroom 为定语从句，修饰前面三个并列名词短语，从句中使用了被动语态 are built，主句谓语同样使用情态动词被动语态 cannot easily be copied。

translation:
在过去十年里，数字平台彻底改变了知识在世界范围内的传播方式。从大学录播课程到互动语言学习软件，在线教育让学习变得比以往任何时候都更容易获得。然而，随着虚拟课程不断扩展，教育者和学生都在思考一个核心问题：在线平台真的能取代传统课堂吗？

毫无疑问，数字学习提供了极大的便利。生活在偏远城镇的学生如今足不出户就能观看顶尖教授的课程，而忙碌的上班族也可以在日常工作结束后的深夜学习新技能。由于在线学习材料可以按个人节奏暂停、重放和复习，需要额外时间来理解复杂概念的学习者再也不会被节奏飞快的讲座抛在后面。此外，线上小测能即时给出分数，帮助学生在重要考试到来前找出薄弱环节。

然而，教育的意义远不止把信息从屏幕搬到笔记本上。在实体课堂中，老师能够察觉到细微的信号——比如困惑的表情或突然的沉默——从而判断何时需要调整讲解方式。同学之间还会通过小组讨论、共同的截止日期以及自发的辩论相互激励，而在网络聊天框里，这种碰撞很少能达到同样的活力。如果缺少定期上课的约束，即便很有动力的学习者在家独自学习时也可能难以保持自律。

基于这些原因，大多数专家认为，教育的未来在于平衡而非替代。数字工具预计将继续作为强有力的补充手段，拓宽教育渠道并实现个性化练习。但与此同时，在真实课堂内部建立起来的人际联结、即时反馈和群体归属感，绝非仅靠软件就能轻易复制。

quizzes.question: How do online materials help learners who need extra time to grasp difficult concepts?

options.text: By offering face-to-face tutoring after every class.
By allowing students to pause, replay, and review lessons.
By removing complex ideas from university courses.
By encouraging spontaneous debates in online chat boxes.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段第三句说明，在线材料可以按个人节奏暂停、重放和复习（paused, replayed, and reviewed），使需要额外时间的学生不至于掉队，故选 B。

quizzes.question: What is most experts' attitude toward the future of online education?

options.text: It will completely replace physical classrooms soon.
It should be banned for young school students.
It will work alongside traditional classrooms as a helpful tool.
It provides stronger human connections than real classrooms.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：C
   - 解析：观点态度题。第四段第一、二句指出专家认为教育未来在于平衡而非替代（balance rather than replacement），数字工具将作为强有力的补充（powerful supplement），故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Staycations and Local Travel（城市微度假与本地旅游）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
For years, taking a meaningful vacation meant booking expensive flights, packing large suitcases, and rushing through famous landmarks in distant countries. Today, however, a growing number of city residents are discovering the appeal of "staycations" and local micro-trips. Instead of traveling thousands of kilometers, people are choosing to explore hidden corners, historic neighborhoods, and quiet parks within a two-hour drive or train ride of home.

Several practical factors explain why local travel has gained popularity. Rising airfares and hotel prices have made long-distance holidays harder to afford, especially for young families. At the same time, many tired office workers find that brief, crowded overseas tours leave them needing another holiday just to recover. By contrast, a two-day stay at a boutique hotel nearby—or a weekend hike in a suburban valley—requires minimal planning and eliminates the stress of airport delays. Even when a trip lasts only forty-eight hours, stepping outside one's daily routine can restore energy surprisingly well.

This shift has also encouraged travelers to look at their own cities with fresh eyes. Guided walking tours that focus on local architecture, street food, and neighborhood history have attracted surprising numbers of residents who once ignored the culture right outside their doors. Local museums and independent bookstores, which used to rely heavily on foreign tourists, are now benefiting from steady weekend visits by people living nearby.

Tourism researchers note that micro-vacations are not merely a temporary budget choice; they also reflect a desire for slower, greener lifestyles. When fewer long-haul flights are taken, carbon emissions drop noticeably, and money spent on small cafés or family-run guesthouses stays inside the local community. Many travelers also discover that meaningful memories come less from ticking off famous sights than from slowing down. Sometimes, the best escape does not require a passport at all.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: At the same time, many tired office workers find that brief, crowded overseas tours leave them needing another holiday just to recover.
sentences.main_clause: many tired office workers find that...（许多疲惫的上班族发现……）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：that 引导宾语从句；在从句中，leave + 宾语(them) + 宾补(needing another holiday...) 表示“使……处于某种状态”，just to recover 为目的状语。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Guided walking tours that focus on local architecture, street food, and neighborhood history have attracted surprising numbers of residents who once ignored the culture right outside their doors.
sentences.main_clause: Guided walking tours have attracted surprising numbers of residents.（带队徒步游吸引了数量惊人的本地居民。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：句中嵌套两个定语从句：that focus on... 修饰先行词 Guided walking tours；who once ignored... 修饰先行词 residents。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: When fewer long-haul flights are taken, carbon emissions drop noticeably, and money spent on small cafés or family-run guesthouses stays inside the local community.
sentences.main_clause: carbon emissions drop noticeably, and money stays inside the local community.（碳排放显著下降，且花在小咖啡馆或家庭旅馆的钱留在了本地社区。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：When... 引导时间/条件状语从句，内含被动语态 are taken；后半句中 spent on small cafés... 为过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 money。

translation:
多年来，度过一个有意义的假期似乎意味着预订昂贵的机票、收拾大号行李箱，并在遥远国度的著名景点间匆忙打卡。然而如今，越来越多的城市居民正发现“宅度假”（staycations）和本地微旅行的魅力。人们不再动辄出行数千公里，而是选择去探索距离家两小时车程或火车车程以内的隐秘角落、历史街区和幽静公园。

几个现实因素解释了本地游为何日益流行。机票和酒店价格的上涨让长途度假变得更难负担，对年轻家庭而言尤其如此。与此同时，许多疲惫的上班族发现，时间仓促、人潮拥挤的海外游结束后，自己反而需要再放一次假来恢复精力。相比之下，在附近的精品酒店住上两天，或者周末去郊区山谷徒步，只需极少的规划，还能免去机场延误带来的焦虑。即便一次旅行只有短短四十八小时，跳出日常作息也能出人意料地恢复精力。

这一转变也促使旅行者以全新的眼光审视自己生活的城市。聚焦本地建筑、街头美食和街区历史的徒步导览活动，吸引了数量惊人的本地居民——他们过去往往忽略了近在咫尺的文化。过去严重依赖外国游客的本地博物馆和独立书店，如今也正受益于周边居民稳定的周末光顾。

旅游研究者指出，微度假绝不仅仅是一种暂时的省钱选择，它还体现了人们对更慢节奏、更环保生活方式的追求。当长途航班次数减少时，碳排放量会明显降低，而人们花在小咖啡馆或家庭式民宿上的资金也能留在本地社区内部。许多旅行者还发现，有意义的回忆与其说是来自打卡著名景点，不如说是来自放慢脚步。有时候，最棒的逃离根本不需要护照。

quizzes.question: What is one reason why local micro-trips are becoming more popular?

options.text: Long-haul flights have become cheaper than local trains.
City residents want to avoid high travel costs and tiring schedules.
Foreign tourists are no longer allowed to visit local museums.
Suburban valleys offer more luxury hotels than big cities.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段提到机票和酒店涨价让长途旅行难以负担（harder to afford），且拥挤的海外游让人疲惫，而本地游需要较少规划且没有机场延误的压力，故选 B。

quizzes.question: How do local businesses benefit from staycations according to the passage?

options.text: They receive steady support from nearby residents.
They can increase their prices during winter holidays.
They no longer need to hire local tour guides.
They earn most of their income from international guests.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：A
   - 解析：细节理解题。第三段提到本地博物馆和独立书店正受益于周边居民稳定的周末访问（steady weekend visits by people living nearby），第四段也提到消费留在了本地社区，故选 A。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Second-hand Economy and Sustainable Fashion（二手经济与可持续时尚）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
Not long ago, buying used clothing was often seen as a sign of financial hardship. Today, however, vintage jackets, pre-owned handbags, and secondhand books are proudly traded both online and in stylish neighborhood shops. Driven largely by younger consumers, the secondhand economy has grown into a major force that challenges the fast-fashion industry.

Fast fashion relies on producing cheap, trendy garments at rapid speed, which encourages shoppers to buy more and throw items away after only a few wears. Environmental studies show that the clothing industry accounts for massive water consumption and millions of tons of textile waste each year. In many cities, discarded clothes are burned or buried in landfills long before the fabric has actually worn out. Once young shoppers became aware of the hidden ecological cost behind a ten-dollar T-shirt, many began looking for greener alternatives.

Digital resale platforms have made trading pre-owned goods remarkably easy. With a few taps on a smartphone, sellers can upload photos of coats they rarely wear, while buyers can search for specific brands at a fraction of the original price. In addition to saving money, thrift shoppers often enjoy the thrill of finding unique pieces that cannot be bought in ordinary chain stores. For college students on tight budgets, buying secondhand furniture, textbooks, and winter coats has become both a practical habit and a creative way to express personal style.

Still, experts warn that secondhand shopping alone will not solve overconsumption if people treat resale apps just like another fast-fashion outlet. True sustainability depends on buying less overall and choosing durable items that can be repaired or passed along. Even so, the cultural shift is unmistakable: wearing pre-loved clothes is no longer something to hide, but a smart statement about style and responsibility.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Fast fashion relies on producing cheap, trendy garments at rapid speed, which encourages shoppers to buy more and throw items away after only a few wears.
sentences.main_clause: Fast fashion relies on producing cheap, trendy garments at rapid speed.（快时尚依赖以极快的速度生产廉价、时髦的服装。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：which encourages shoppers to buy more... 为非限制性定语从句，which 指代前面整个主句的内容，说明这种模式带来的结果。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Once young shoppers became aware of the hidden ecological cost behind a ten-dollar T-shirt, many began looking for greener alternatives.
sentences.main_clause: many began looking for greener alternatives.（许多人开始寻找更环保的替代选择。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Once... 引导时间/条件状语从句（意为“一旦……”），became aware of 为“意识到……”。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: True sustainability depends on buying less overall and choosing durable items that can be repaired or passed along.
sentences.main_clause: True sustainability depends on buying less overall and choosing durable items.（真正的可持续性取决于总体上少买，并选择耐用的物品。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：动名词短语 buying less... 和 choosing durable items 并列作介词 on 的宾语；that can be repaired or passed along 为定语从句修饰 items，内含被动语态 can be repaired or passed along。

translation:
不久前，购买旧衣服还常常被视为经济拮据的象征。然而今天，复古夹克、二手手袋和旧书无论在网络上还是在时髦的街区小店里，都被自豪地交易着。在年轻消费者的主要推动下，二手经济已经成长为一股重要力量，向快时尚产业发起了挑战。

快时尚依赖以极快速度生产廉价、时髦的服装，这促使消费者买得更多，并在仅穿几次后就把衣物丢弃。环境研究表明，服装行业每年消耗大量水资源，并产生数百万吨纺织垃圾。在许多城市，被丢弃的衣物往往在布料远未穿坏之前就被焚烧或填埋。一旦年轻消费者意识到一件 10 美元的 T 恤背后隐藏的生态代价，许多人便开始寻找更环保的替代方案。

数字转售平台让二手物品交易变得格外简单。只需在智能手机上轻点几下，卖家就能上传自己很少穿的外套照片，而买家则能以原价的一小部分淘到特定品牌。除了省钱之外，淘二手货的人还常常享受那种在普通连锁店里买不到的独特单品的惊喜感。对于预算紧张的大学生来说，购买二手家具、教材和冬衣既成了一种实用习惯，也成了表达个人风格的创意方式。

不过，专家也提醒说，如果人们把二手转售软件当成另一个快时尚卖场一样不停买买买，单靠买二手并无法解决过度消费问题。真正的可持续发展在于总体上减少购买，并选择可以修补或继续传下去的耐用物品。即便如此，这种文化转变依然显而易见：穿二手衣物不再是需要遮掩的事，而是彰显品味与责任感的明智表达。

quizzes.question: What drove many young consumers away from fast fashion according to Paragraph 2?

options.text: Fast-fashion stores stopped selling trendy T-shirts.
They realized the serious environmental cost of cheap clothes.
Chain stores raised their prices far above resale apps.
Vintage jackets became cheaper to produce in factories.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段最后一句指出，年轻消费者一旦意识到廉价 T 恤背后隐藏的生态成本（hidden ecological cost），便开始寻找更环保的选择，故选 B。

quizzes.question: What do experts suggest is necessary for true sustainability?

options.text: Buying fewer things in total and picking long-lasting goods.
Uploading photos of old coats to resale platforms every week.
Replacing all neighborhood shops with digital marketplaces.
Avoiding all secondhand items that require minor repairs.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：A
   - 解析：细节理解题。第四段第二句说明，真正的可持续性取决于总体上少买（buying less overall）以及选择可修补或传承的耐用物品（durable items），故选 A。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Modern University Libraries（大学图书馆的转型）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
Ask older graduates to describe their university library, and they will likely mention tall wooden shelves, dusty paper catalogs, and strict rules demanding total silence. While printed books still hold an honored place on campus, the modern university library looks and functions very differently from the quiet storage rooms of the past. Today, libraries are being redesigned as vibrant centers for collaboration, digital research, and creative exchange.

Because most academic journals and reference books can now be accessed online from a dorm room, universities faced a serious question: why do students still need a physical library? Campus planners quickly realized that students come not only for books, but for an inspiring environment where they can focus and work together. As a result, heavy stacks in many libraries have been moved to automated storage basements, freeing up bright upper floors for flexible seating, group study rooms, and even cafés.

Technology has also reshaped the services that librarians provide. Beyond helping students locate reliable sources, modern libraries offer data labs, video editing studios, and 3D printers that are open to learners from every major. Workshops on how to check facts, manage citations, and use artificial intelligence tools responsibly are routinely hosted by library staff, who now act more like research coaches than quiet caretakers. For students preparing graduation theses, one-on-one consultations with subject specialists are often booked weeks ahead.

Of course, traditional silent reading rooms have not vanished completely. Many students still treasure a peaceful corner where no whispers are allowed during exam season, and rare historical collections are carefully preserved in climate-controlled rooms. By combining quiet reflection with shared innovation, today's university library proves that it is not fading into irrelevance—it is simply writing a new chapter.

translation:
请老一辈毕业生描述一下他们的大学图书馆，他们很可能会提到高大的木制书架、落灰的纸质目录卡片，以及要求绝对安静的严格规定。虽然纸质书在校园里依然享有崇高地位，但现代大学图书馆的外观与功能，已经与过去安静的储书空间大相径庭。如今，图书馆正被重新设计成充满活力的协作、数字研究与创意交流中心。

由于大多数学术期刊和参考书现在都能在宿舍里在线查阅，大学曾面临一个严肃的问题：学生为什么还需要实体图书馆？校园规划者很快意识到，学生来图书馆不仅是为了找书，更是为了一个能让他们专注学习与彼此合作的激励环境。于是，许多图书馆里沉重的书架被移到了自动化地下书库，从而把明亮的高楼层腾出来，布置成灵活座位区、小组讨论室甚至咖啡角。

科技也重塑了图书馆员所提供的服务。除了帮助学生查找可靠资料外，现代图书馆还提供向所有专业学生开放的数据实验室、视频剪辑室和 3D 打印机。关于如何核查事实、管理文献引用以及负责任地使用人工智能工具的研讨会，也由图书馆工作人员定期举办——他们如今更像是研究导师，而不仅仅是安静的管理员。对于准备毕业论文的学生而言，与学科馆员的一对一咨询常常需要提前数周预约。

当然，传统的静音阅览室并没有完全消失。许多学生在考试季依然珍视那个连窃窃私语都不被允许的宁静角落，珍稀的历史馆藏也被精心保存在恒温恒湿的库房里。通过将安静思考与共享创新结合起来，当今的大学图书馆证明自己并未走向过时——它只是在书写新的篇章。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Deep Reading in the Short-Video Era（短视频时代如何保持深度阅读）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
In just fifteen seconds, a short video can make us laugh, teach us a cooking trick, or summarize the plot of a classic novel. Designed to capture attention instantly, short-video platforms have become a daily habit for hundreds of millions of people. Yet as our minds grow accustomed to rapid clips and constant stimulation, many readers notice an unsettling change: sitting down with a serious book for half an hour feels harder than it used to.

Neuroscientists explain that deep reading requires patience and sustained mental effort. Unlike passive scrolling, reading a long article or novel forces the brain to build mental images, connect complex arguments, and pause for reflection. When people switch repeatedly between short videos and messages, their attention is trained to jump quickly rather than stay anchored on a single page. Over time, even well-educated readers may find themselves skimming paragraphs impatiently when an idea takes several minutes to unfold.

Fortunately, deep reading is not a lost art—it is a skill that can be rebuilt through deliberate practice. Reading experts suggest starting with small, realistic goals, such as reading ten pages before bed with the phone placed in another room. Choosing physical books or e-readers without web browsers also helps, since fewer alerts will interrupt your train of thought. Just as physical fitness returns after regular walks, reading stamina recovers when quiet focus is practiced daily.

Another effective strategy is reading actively with a pen in hand. Underlining key ideas or writing brief questions in the margin slows the mind down in a productive way and turns reading into a conversation with the author. Joining a local book club can add helpful accountability too. Short videos may deliver quick entertainment, but only deep reading gives our thoughts the quiet room they need to grow.

vocabulary.meaning: 令人不安的；使人焦虑的

translation:
短短十五秒钟，一段短视频就能逗笑我们、教我们一个烹饪技巧，或者概括一部经典小说的剧情。为了瞬间抓住注意力而设计的短视频平台，已经成为数亿人的日常习惯。然而，随着我们的大脑越来越习惯快速切换的片段和持续不断的刺激，许多读者注意到一个令人不安的变化：静下心来啃半小时严肃书籍，似乎比以前难多了。

神经科学家解释说，深度阅读需要耐心和持续的脑力投入。与被动刷屏不同，阅读长篇文章或小说会促使大脑构建心理图像、串联复杂论点并停下来思考。当人们在短视频和聊天消息之间反复切换时，注意力就被训练成快速跳跃的状态，而很难稳稳停留在同一页纸上。久而久之，当一个观点需要几分钟才能展开时，甚至连受过良好教育的读者都会发现自己正不耐烦地略读段落。

幸运的是，深度阅读并没有失传——它是一种可以通过刻意练习重新找回的能力。阅读专家建议从切合实际的小目标做起，比如睡前把手机放在另一个房间里，坚持读十页书。选择纸质书或没有网页浏览器的电子阅读器也很有帮助，因为这样就不会有频繁的弹窗打断你的思路。正如规律散步能恢复体能一样，每天练习安静专注也能让阅读耐力逐渐恢复。

另一个有效的策略是手里拿着笔进行主动阅读。在核心观点下划线，或者在页边空白处写下简短的疑问，能以一种富有成效的方式让大脑慢下来，把阅读变成与作者的对话。加入本地读书会也能带来有益的监督与陪伴。短视频或许能带来快速的消遣，但唯有深度阅读，才能给予我们的思想成长所需的安静空间。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Aging Societies and Community Care（人口老龄化与社区互助）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
Across much of the world, people are living longer than any previous generation, while birth rates are steadily falling. As a result, countries from Japan and Germany to China are entering an era of rapid population aging. While longer life expectancy is a triumph of modern medicine, it also creates an urgent question for cities and families: how can millions of older adults be cared for with dignity and warmth?

Traditionally, elderly parents were supported directly by their adult children under the same roof. Today, however, smaller family sizes and job mobility mean that many seniors live alone or far away from their relatives. Relying entirely on large nursing homes is neither financially practical for every family nor desirable for older people who wish to remain in familiar neighborhoods where they have built lifelong friendships.

In response, community-based care models are gaining strong momentum. In many urban districts, neighborhood centers now provide affordable hot lunches, daily health checks, and daytime social clubs where seniors can learn painting or practice Tai Chi. Volunteer teams also visit homebound residents regularly to check heating equipment, deliver medicine, or simply share a cup of tea. At the same time, "time bank" programs have been introduced in several cities: younger volunteers earn hours by helping elderly neighbors buy groceries or use smartphones, and those hours can later be saved for their own future care.

Experts emphasize that aging does not mean older citizens only receive help; many healthy retirees serve as mentors, reading guides, and active volunteers themselves. In several neighborhoods, retired teachers and engineers even run free homework clubs for local schoolchildren after class. When communities are designed to connect different generations rather than separate them, growing old becomes a shared social responsibility—and a far less lonely journey.

vocabulary.meaning: 预期；期待（life expectancy 预期寿命）
负担得起的；价格公道的
足不出户的；长期居家的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: While longer life expectancy is a triumph of modern medicine, it also creates an urgent question for cities and families: how can millions of older adults be cared for with dignity and warmth?
sentences.main_clause: it also creates an urgent question for cities and families.（它也为城市和家庭带来了一个紧迫的问题。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：While... 引导让步状语从句；冒号后为具体问题，内含情态动词被动语态 can ... be cared for。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: At the same time, "time bank" programs have been introduced in several cities: younger volunteers earn hours by helping elderly neighbors buy groceries or use smartphones, and those hours can later be saved for their own future care.
sentences.main_clause: "time bank" programs have been introduced in several cities.（“时间银行”项目已在多个城市推出。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：have been introduced 为现在完成时被动语态；冒号后两个由 and 连接的并列句解释运作机制，后句也含被动语态 can later be saved。

translation:
在世界许多地方，人们的寿命比以往任何一代人都要长，而出生率却在稳步下降。因此，从日本、德国到中国，许多国家正步入人口快速老龄化时代。虽然预期寿命延长是现代医学的巨大胜利，但它也为城市和家庭提出了一个紧迫的问题：如何才能让数以百万计的老年人有尊严、有温度地安享晚年？

传统上，年迈的父母由成年子女在同一屋檐下直接照料。然而如今，家庭规模缩小加上就业流动性增强，意味着许多老人独自居住，或与亲属相隔千里。完全依赖大型养老院，对每个家庭而言在经济上并不现实，对希望留在建立了毕生友谊的熟悉街区的老年人来说，也并非理想选择。

为此，以社区为基础的养老模式正获得强劲发展势头。在许多城区，社区中心如今提供价格公道的现做热餐、日常体检，以及供老年人学习绘画或练习太极的日间社交俱乐部。志愿者团队还会定期上门探望行动不便的居家老人，检查供暖设备、代送药品，或者只是陪着喝杯茶。与此同时，多个城市还引入了“时间银行”项目：年轻志愿者通过帮老年邻居买菜或教用智能手机来赚取服务时长，这些时长日后可以储存起来用于换取自己未来的照护服务。

专家强调，老龄化并不意味着老年公民只是单方面接受帮助；许多健康的退休老人本身就担任着导师、阅读领读员和活跃志愿者。在不少街区，退休教师和工程师甚至在放学后为当地小学生开办免费的作业辅导班。当社区被设计用来连接不同代际而非将他们隔离开来时，变老就会成为一种共担的社会责任——以及一段远不那么孤独的旅程。

   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段最后一句说明，完全依赖大型养老院在经济上并非每个家庭都能负担（neither financially practical），而且希望留在熟悉街区的老人也不愿意（nor desirable），故选 B。

quizzes.explanation:

   - 解析：细节理解题。第三段最后一句解释了“时间银行”：年轻志愿者帮老人买菜或用手机赚取时长，以后可以用于自己未来的照料，故选 B。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Fighting Food Waste with "Mystery Bags"（食物浪费与“盲盒剩菜”App）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
Every evening before closing time, bakeries, cafés, and supermarkets around the world face the same dilemma: shelves are still stocked with fresh bread, sandwiches, and fruit that cannot legally or practically be sold the next morning. Traditionally, tons of perfectly edible food ended up in garbage bins simply because it did not sell before dusk. In recent years, however, a clever mobile app trend has turned leftover food into affordable "mystery bags."

The concept behind these anti-waste apps is straightforward. Local shops list surplus items on the platform at roughly one-third of their original price, without promising the exact menu inside each bag. Customers browse nearby offers on their phones, reserve a bag online, and pick it up during a short collection window before closing. Because buyers do not know precisely which pastries or vegetables they will receive, the purchase feels a bit like opening a surprise gift. In many college towns, popular bakery bags are claimed within minutes of being posted.

For all sides involved, the benefits are clear. Shop owners recover part of their production costs instead of paying to throw unsold food away, and they also attract new walk-in customers who might return later at full price. Students and budget-conscious residents enjoy high-quality meals at a fraction of normal prices, while trying new dishes they might not otherwise order. Most importantly, every bag rescued keeps good food out of landfills, where rotting waste releases harmful greenhouse gases.

Although mystery-bag apps cannot eliminate food waste across the entire supply chain, they show how simple digital tools can align economic incentives with environmental care. Local governments and community groups have also begun praising participating shops for setting a practical example. When saving the planet also saves money on dinner, sustainable habits become much easier for ordinary people to adopt.

vocabulary.meaning: 精打细算的；注重预算的

sentences.label: 句子 1

sentences.main_clause: bakeries, cafés, and supermarkets face the same dilemma.（面包店、咖啡馆和超市面临着同样的困境。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：冒号后为解释说明，are still stocked with 为被动语态；that cannot legally or practically be sold... 为定语从句，修饰 fresh bread, sandwiches, and fruit，内含情态动词被动语态 cannot ... be sold。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Because buyers do not know precisely which pastries or vegetables they will receive, the purchase feels a bit like opening a surprise gift.
sentences.main_clause: the purchase feels a bit like opening a surprise gift.（这次购买感觉有点像拆开一份惊喜礼物。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Because... 引导原因状语从句，其中 which pastries or vegetables they will receive 为 which 引导的宾语从句，作 know 的宾语。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Most importantly, every bag rescued keeps good food out of landfills, where rotting waste releases harmful greenhouse gases.
