translation:
每天傍晚打烊前，世界各地的面包店、咖啡馆和超市都面临着同样的难题：货架上仍然摆满了新鲜的面包、三明治和水果，而这些食物在法规上或实际操作中都无法留到第二天早上继续售卖。传统上，成吨完全可以食用的食物仅仅因为天黑前没卖完，最终就被扔进了垃圾桶。然而近年来，一股巧妙的手机应用潮流把剩余食物变成了价格实惠的“神秘盲盒”。

这些反浪费应用背后的理念十分直接。本地商家在平台上以大约原价三分之一的价格挂出剩余商品，但并不提前承诺每个袋子里的具体品类。顾客在手机上浏览附近的优惠，在线预订一个盲盒，并在打烊前较短的取货时段内到店自提。由于买家并不知道自己具体会收到哪些糕点或蔬菜，这种消费体验有点像拆开一份惊喜礼物。在许多大学城，热门面包店的盲盒往往一经发布几分钟内就会被抢购一空。

对参与各方而言，益处都显而易见。店主得以收回部分生产成本，而不用再花钱把未售出的食物处理掉，同时还能吸引新的到店顾客，他们日后可能会按原价再次光顾。学生和注重预算的居民能以平时一小部分的价格享用高品质餐食，同时尝到平常未必会点的新菜品。最重要的是，每一个被“拯救”的盲盒都让完好的食物免于进入垃圾填埋场——在那里，腐烂的垃圾会释放有害的温室气体。

尽管“剩菜盲盒”应用无法消除整个供应链上的食物浪费，但它们证明了简单的数字工具如何将经济激励与环境保护统一起来。地方政府和社区团体也开始赞扬参与其中的商家树立了切实可行的榜样。当拯救地球的同时还能在晚饭上省钱时，普通人也就更容易养成可持续的生活习惯。

quizzes.question: Why are the leftover food packages called "mystery bags"?

options.text: The shops do not reveal the pickup time in advance.
Buyers do not know the exact items inside until they pick them up.
Customers cannot see the price before arriving at the store.
Only rare imported fruits are placed inside the bags.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段提到商家不承诺每个袋子里的具体菜单，买家事先不知道会收到哪些糕点或蔬菜，就像拆惊喜礼物（opening a surprise gift），故选 B。

quizzes.question: What environmental benefit is mentioned in Paragraph 3?

options.text: Fewer greenhouse gases are produced by food rotting in landfills.
Bakeries stop using plastic packaging for sandwiches.
Supermarkets reduce their electricity use before closing time.
Farms grow less bread and fruit during summer months.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：A
   - 解析：细节理解题。第三段最后一句指出，拯救食物使其免于进入垃圾填埋场，在那里腐烂的垃圾会释放有害温室气体（harmful greenhouse gases），故选 A。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: The Revival of Crafts Among Youth（为什么越来越多年轻人学习手工）
difficulty: 第二阶段 ⭐⭐⭐（CEFR B1+–B2 / 大学英语四级水平）
body:
In bright weekend studios across major cities, young office workers and college students are putting down their keyboards and picking up clay, yarn, and woodworking tools. Far from being hobbies reserved for retired grandparents, pottery, knitting, and leathercraft have enjoyed a remarkable revival among people in their twenties and thirties. Craft workshops that once struggled to attract visitors are now frequently booked out weeks in advance.

Psychologists point out that much of modern work happens behind glass screens, where progress feels abstract and invisible. After spending forty hours a week editing spreadsheets or replying to emails, many young adults crave the satisfaction of creating something real that they can hold in their hands. Shaping a bowl on a spinning wheel or sewing a canvas bag offers clear, immediate proof of effort—even when the final piece is slightly uneven. Unlike digital files that vanish into cloud folders, a handmade mug stays on the breakfast table as a daily reminder of patience.

Working with one's hands also serves as a gentle form of stress relief. Because pottery or embroidery demands steady focus on physical movement, anxious thoughts about deadlines and social comparisons are temporarily pushed aside. In addition, craft studios provide relaxed social spaces where strangers bond over shared mistakes, trade tips, and celebrate small achievements together without the pressure of formal networking.

Some enthusiasts even turn their weekend passion into small side businesses on social media, selling handmade mugs or knitted scarves to buyers who value individuality over mass production. Others simply keep their creations as thoughtful gifts for close friends or donate knitted blankets to local animal shelters. Whether done purely for joy or extra income, traditional crafts remind a fast-moving generation that slow, patient making still holds lasting value.

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: After spending forty hours a week editing spreadsheets or replying to emails, many young adults crave the satisfaction of creating something real that they can hold in their hands.
sentences.main_clause: many young adults crave the satisfaction of creating something real.（许多年轻人渴望创造出真实事物的满足感。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：After spending... 为时间状语；that they can hold in their hands 为定语从句，修饰先行词 something real（当先行词为不定代词 something 等时，关系代词通常用 that）。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Because pottery or embroidery demands steady focus on physical movement, anxious thoughts about deadlines and social comparisons are temporarily pushed aside.
sentences.main_clause: anxious thoughts are temporarily pushed aside.（关于截止日期和社交攀比的焦虑念头会被暂时抛到一边。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：Because... 引导原因状语从句；主句中使用一般现在时被动语态 are temporarily pushed aside。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Some enthusiasts even turn their weekend passion into small side businesses on social media, selling handmade mugs or knitted scarves to buyers who value individuality over mass production.
sentences.main_clause: Some enthusiasts even turn their weekend passion into small side businesses on social media.（一些爱好者甚至把周末爱好变成了社交媒体上的小副业。）
sentences.grammar: 语法点：selling handmade mugs... 为现在分词短语作伴随状语；who value individuality over mass production 为定语从句，修饰 buyers。

translation:
在大城市明亮的周末工作室里，年轻的上班族和大学生正放下键盘，拿起陶土、毛线和木工工具。陶艺、编织和皮具制作远非只有退休祖父母才会喜欢的消遣，它们在二三十岁的年轻人中迎来了显著的复兴。过去门可罗雀的手工坊，如今常常提前几周就被预订一空。

心理学家指出，现代工作大多发生在玻璃屏幕之后，进展显得抽象而无形。每周花四十个小时编辑电子表格或回复邮件后，许多年轻人渴望获得亲手创造出真实物品的满足感。在旋转的拉坯机上塑出一只碗，或者缝制一个帆布包，都能为努力提供清晰、即时的证明——即便成品稍微有些不够平整。与消失在云端文件夹里的数字文件不同，一只手工马克杯会留在早餐桌上，每天提醒着这份耐心。

动手做手工也是一种温和的减压方式。由于陶艺或刺绣需要把注意力稳定地集中在身体动作上，关于截止日期和社交攀比的焦虑念头会被暂时抛到一边。此外，手工工作室还提供了轻松的社交空间，陌生人可以在这里因为共同的失误而拉近距离，交流技巧，并一起为小小的成果庆祝，而无需承受正式社交的压力。

一些爱好者甚至把周末的热爱发展成社交媒体上的小副业，把手工马克杯或针织围巾卖给那些看重个性胜过批量生产的买家。另一些人则干脆把自己的作品留作送给挚友的贴心礼物，或将编织毛毯捐赠给当地的动物收容所。无论是纯粹为了快乐还是为了增加收入，传统手工艺都在提醒这个快节奏的一代人：缓慢而耐心的创造，依然拥有持久的价值。

quizzes.question: Why do many young office workers enjoy making things by hand?

options.text: Because screen-based work often feels abstract and lacks physical results.
Because craft workshops are cheaper than staying at home.
Because companies require employees to learn traditional skills.
Because handmade bags are always stronger than factory products.

quizzes.explanation:
1. 答案：A
   - 解析：细节理解题。第二段指出，现代工作大多在屏幕后进行，进展抽象无形（abstract and invisible），因此年轻人渴望创造出能握在手里的真实物品（something real），故选 A。

quizzes.question: How do craft activities help reduce anxiety according to Paragraph 3?

options.text: They allow people to finish office emails much faster.
They require steady concentration on physical tasks, pushing worries away.
They force strangers to compete for awards in weekend classes.
They guarantee a large extra income on social media.

quizzes.explanation:
2. 答案：B
   - 解析：细节理解题。第三段第二句说明，陶艺或刺绣需要持续专注于身体动作（steady focus on physical movement），从而把焦虑念头暂时推开，故选 B。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Why Cities Are Planting Pocket Forests（城市“口袋森林”的兴起）
body:
In crowded cities where glass towers and concrete roads dominate the skyline, finding a quiet patch of green can feel like a luxury. Yet a growing urban movement is proving that you do not need hundreds of hectares to build a thriving ecosystem. Across Europe, Asia, and North America, local councils and community volunteers are turning neglected parking lots, roadside strips, and schoolyards into "pocket forests"—dense mini-woodlands no larger than a tennis court.

The concept is largely inspired by the Miyawaki method, a planting technique that was developed by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki in the 1970s. Instead of spacing out a single type of ornamental tree in neat rows, gardeners enrich the soil with organic compost and plant dozens of native species tightly together. Because the young trees must compete for sunlight from the very beginning, they grow significantly faster than those in conventional parks. Within just two or three years, the canopy closes, creating a shaded microclimate that cools the surrounding streets during summer heatwaves.

Environmental researchers note that these tiny woodlands offer benefits far beyond their modest size. Studies conducted in the Netherlands and India found that pocket forests can support far greater biodiversity than standard urban lawns, attracting pollinators, songbirds, and beneficial insects back into city centers. Furthermore, their deep root systems absorb heavy rainwater more efficiently, which reduces the risk of flash flooding after intense storms.

Although a single mini-forest cannot solve climate change on its own, urban planners view it as a practical and visible starting point. When residents help plant and care for a woodland right outside their apartment blocks, abstract environmental goals become a shared neighborhood achievement. As cities search for affordable ways to adapt to rising temperatures, these compact green islands show that small spaces can still spark meaningful ecological change.

vocabulary.meaning: 支配；占据主导地位；俯瞰

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: In crowded cities where glass towers and concrete roads dominate the skyline, finding a quiet patch of green can feel like a luxury.
sentences.main_clause: finding a quiet patch of green (主语，动名词短语) + can feel like (系动词短语) + a luxury (表语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：In crowded cities... 是地点状语；where glass towers and concrete roads dominate the skyline 是由 where 引导的定语从句，修饰先行词 cities。
参考理解：在玻璃高楼与混凝土道路占据天际线的拥挤城市里，寻找一片宁静的绿意宛如一种奢侈。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: The concept is largely inspired by the Miyawaki method, a planting technique that was developed by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki in the 1970s.
sentences.main_clause: The concept + is largely inspired by (一般现在时被动语态) + the Miyawaki method (介词宾语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：a planting technique... 作 the Miyawaki method 的同位语；that was developed by... 是 that 引导的定语从句（含一般过去时被动语态），修饰 technique。
参考理解：这一理念很大程度上受到“宫胁造林法”的启发，这是日本植物学家宫胁昭在20世纪70年代研发的一种种植技术。

sentences.label: 例句 3
sentences.quote: Furthermore, their deep root systems absorb heavy rainwater more efficiently, which reduces the risk of flash flooding after intense storms.
sentences.main_clause: their deep root systems (主语) + absorb (谓语) + heavy rainwater (宾语) + more efficiently (方式状语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：which reduces the risk... 是由 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，指代前面整句话所描述的现象。
参考理解：此外，它们深扎的根系能更高效地吸收强降雨，从而降低强风暴雨后发生山洪暴发的风险。

translation:
在玻璃高楼与混凝土道路占据天际线的拥挤城市里，寻找一片宁静的绿意宛如一种奢侈。然而，一项不断壮大的城市运动正在证明，人们并不需要数百公顷的土地才能打造一个生机勃勃的生态系统。在欧洲、亚洲和北美各地，地方市政委员会与社区志愿者正将无人照管的停车场、路边空地和校园角落改造成“口袋森林”——这种密集的微型林地面积不过一个网球场大小。

这一理念很大程度上受到“宫胁造林法”的启发，这是日本植物学家宫胁昭在20世纪70年代研发的一种种植技术。园丁们不再把单一品种的观赏树木整齐地隔行栽种，而是用有机堆肥改良土壤，并将数十种本土植物紧密地种在一起。由于幼树从一开始就必须争夺阳光，它们的生长速度明显快于传统公园里的树木。短短两三年内，树冠便会合拢，形成一个阴凉的微气候，在夏季热浪期间为周边街道降温。

环境研究人员指出，这些微型林地带来的益处远超其有限的面积。在荷兰和印度开展的研究发现，口袋森林能够承载比普通城市草坪丰富得多的生物多样性，吸引传粉昆虫、鸣禽以及益虫重返市中心。此外，它们深扎的根系能更高效地吸收强降雨，从而降低强风暴雨后发生山洪暴发的风险。

尽管单靠一片微型森林无法独立解决气候变化问题，但城市规划者将其视为一个切实可行且直观可见的起点。当居民在自家公寓楼外亲手种下并照料一片林地时，抽象的环保目标就变成了邻里共享的成果。随着城市不断寻找经济实惠的方法来适应日益上升的气温，这些紧凑的绿色岛屿表明，微小空间同样可以激发深远的生态变革。

quizzes.question: Why do trees in pocket forests grow faster than those in conventional parks?

options.text: They are watered more frequently by community volunteers.
They are planted close together and have to compete for sunlight.
They belong to a single fast-growing ornamental species.
They are protected from summer heatwaves by tall glass towers.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。由第二段第三句“Because the young trees must compete for sunlight from the very beginning, they grow significantly faster than those in conventional parks.”可知，紧凑种植让幼树从一开始就竞争阳光，从而长得更快。故选 B。

quizzes.question: What is the urban planners' attitude toward pocket forests?

options.text: Doubtful, because they are too small to affect the environment.
Worried, because they may increase the risk of flooding.
Positive, seeing them as a practical step in adapting to climate change.
Indifferent, as they prefer building large standard urban lawns.

quizzes.explanation: 观点态度题。由最后一段第一句“urban planners view it as a practical and visible starting point”及尾句可知，规划者持积极态度，认为它们是应对气温升高的实用起点。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: How AI Is Reshaping Language Learning（人工智能如何改变语言学习）
body:
For decades, mastering a foreign language meant memorizing long vocabulary lists, completing grammar drills, and waiting nervously for a teacher to correct your pronunciation. Today, however, artificial intelligence is quietly transforming that familiar routine. Across smartphones and laptops, AI-powered language tools are offering learners something once reserved for wealthy students who could afford private tutors: instant, personalized feedback available at any hour of the day.

Unlike early language apps that relied mainly on multiple-choice quizzes, modern systems use natural language processing to hold realistic conversations. A student preparing for a job interview in English or a trip to Madrid can practice speaking with a virtual partner that adapts to their skill level. When a mistake is made in sentence structure or word choice, the software gently explains why a different phrase sounds more natural. Because learners do not have to worry about feeling embarrassed in front of a classroom, many report greater willingness to speak aloud.

Still, experienced educators warn that technology should not be mistaken for a magic shortcut. Language is deeply tied to culture, humor, and human emotion—areas where algorithms still struggle to match real interaction. If learners depend entirely on machine-generated translations during daily tasks, they may lose the patience required to build genuine fluency. In addition, studies suggest that motivation tends to drop once the novelty of a smart app wears off.

Rather than replacing human teachers, AI appears most effective when it works alongside traditional instruction. While software handles repetitive pronunciation practice and tracks individual weak spots, teachers can dedicate class time to meaningful debate, cultural context, and creative writing. When used thoughtfully, these digital tools act not as a substitute for effort, but as a bridge that makes language learning more accessible to people around the world.

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Across smartphones and laptops, AI-powered language tools are offering learners something once reserved for wealthy students who could afford private tutors: instant, personalized feedback available at any hour of the day.
sentences.main_clause: AI-powered language tools (主语) + are offering (谓语) + learners (间接宾语) + something (直接宾语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：once reserved for wealthy students 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 something；who could afford private tutors 是定语从句修饰 students；冒号后内容具体解释 something。
参考理解：在智能手机和笔记本电脑上，人工智能驱动的语言工具正在为学习者提供曾经只有请得起私教的富裕学生才能享有的资源：全天候提供的即时、个性化反馈。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: Because learners do not have to worry about feeling embarrassed in front of a classroom, many report greater willingness to speak aloud.
sentences.main_clause: many (主语) + report (谓语) + greater willingness to speak aloud (宾语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：Because learners do not have to worry... 是原因状语从句，说明许多学习者更愿意大声开口的原因。
参考理解：由于学习者不必担心在全班同学面前感到尴尬，许多人表示自己更愿意大声说出来。

sentences.label: 例句 3
sentences.quote: While software handles repetitive pronunciation practice and tracks individual weak spots, teachers can dedicate class time to meaningful debate, cultural context, and creative writing.
sentences.main_clause: teachers + can dedicate + class time + to meaningful debate, cultural context, and creative writing。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：While software handles... 是由 While 引导的状语从句，表示“在……的同时”（带有对比意味）。
参考理解：当软件负责重复性的发音练习并追踪个人薄弱环节时，教师就可以把课堂时间投入到有意义的辩论、文化背景讲解和创意写作中。

translation:
几十年来，掌握一门外语意味着背诵长长的单词表、做完语法练习，并紧张地等待老师纠正你的发音。然而今天，人工智能正在悄然改变这种熟悉的模式。在智能手机和笔记本电脑上，人工智能驱动的语言工具正在为学习者提供曾经只有请得起私教的富裕学生才能享有的资源：全天候提供的即时、个性化反馈。

与早期主要依赖选择题测验的语言应用不同，现代系统利用自然语言处理技术来进行逼真的对话。准备英语求职面试或马德里之旅的学生，可以与一个能根据自身水平调整难度的虚拟伙伴练习口语。当句子结构或用词出现错误时，软件会温和地解释为什么另一种表达听起来更地道。由于学习者不必担心在全班同学面前感到尴尬，许多人表示自己更愿意大声说出来。

尽管如此，经验丰富的教育工作者警告称，不应把技术误认为是神奇的捷径。语言与文化、幽默和人类情感紧密相连——在这些领域，算法仍难以媲美真实的人际互动。如果学习者在日常任务中完全依赖机器生成的翻译，他们可能会失去培养真正流利度所需的耐心。此外，研究表明，一旦智能应用的新鲜感消退，学习动力往往会随之下降。

人工智能与其说是取代人类教师，不如说在与传统教学配合使用时最为有效。当软件负责重复性的发音练习并追踪个人薄弱环节时，教师就可以把课堂时间投入到有意义的辩论、文化背景讲解和创意写作中。只要使用得当，这些数字工具并非努力的替代品，而是让世界各地的人们更容易接触到语言学习的桥梁。

quizzes.question: What advantage do modern AI language tools have over early language apps?

options.text: They rely entirely on multiple-choice grammar quizzes.
They can hold realistic conversations and explain natural expressions.
They guarantee native-level fluency within a few weeks.
They allow students to avoid all pronunciation practice.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段指出，早期应用主要依赖选择题，而现代系统利用自然语言处理进行逼真对话，并解释为何某些表达更自然。故选 B。

quizzes.question: According to the passage, why is AI unable to completely replace human teachers?

options.text: AI software is too expensive for most schools to afford.
Algorithms still struggle with cultural context and human emotion.
Students feel too embarrassed when talking to a virtual partner.
Teachers are better at tracking repetitive pronunciation drills.

quizzes.explanation: 推理判断题。第三段提到“Language is deeply tied to culture, humor, and human emotion—areas where algorithms still struggle to match real interaction.”说明算法在这些方面仍不如真人互动。故选 B。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Work-Life Boundaries and Mental Health（职场中的“边界感”与心理健康）
body:
It is 9:30 p.m. on a Tuesday, and a work message lights up your phone screen. Even though the message does not require an immediate reply, the habit of checking it pulls your mind straight back to unfinished spreadsheets and tomorrow's meeting. In an era where laptops and messaging apps allow offices to follow employees into their living rooms, the line between professional duty and personal rest has become increasingly blurred.

For years, constant availability was often praised as a sign of dedication. Yet psychologists and workplace researchers warn that an "always-on" culture carries serious hidden costs. When workers feel pressured to answer emails during dinner or over the weekend, their brains rarely get the uninterrupted downtime needed to recover from daily stress. Over time, this chronic mental fatigue can lead to burnout, poorer sleep quality, and declining focus during actual working hours.

In response, both governments and forward-thinking companies are beginning to protect employees' right to disconnect. Countries such as France, Australia, and Portugal have introduced laws that limit employers from expecting responses outside official working hours. Meanwhile, some organizations have adopted simple practical rules, such as disabling internal chat notifications after 6:00 p.m. or scheduling messages to be delivered the next morning.

Building healthier boundaries, however, does not depend on legislation alone. Career coaches suggest that individual workers can start by setting clear expectations with their teams and turning off work alerts on personal devices. Taking a quiet walk without a phone or keeping one evening a week strictly free from professional tasks may seem like small steps. Yet when rest is treated with the same respect as productivity, employees often return to their desks calmer, sharper, and far more resilient.

vocabulary.meaning: 有韧性的；能迅速恢复的

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: In an era where laptops and messaging apps allow offices to follow employees into their living rooms, the line between professional duty and personal rest has become increasingly blurred.
sentences.main_clause: the line (主语) + has become (系动词) + increasingly blurred (表语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：In an era... 是时间状语；where laptops and messaging apps allow... 是定语从句修饰 era；between professional duty and personal rest 是介词短语作后置定语修饰 line。
参考理解：在一个笔记本电脑和即时通讯应用让办公室一路“跟进”员工客厅的时代，职业职责与个人休息之间的界限变得越来越模糊。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: When workers feel pressured to answer emails during dinner or over the weekend, their brains rarely get the uninterrupted downtime needed to recover from daily stress.
sentences.main_clause: their brains + rarely get + the uninterrupted downtime。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：When workers feel pressured... 是时间状语从句；needed to recover from daily stress 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 downtime。
参考理解：当员工在吃晚饭或周末感到不得不回复邮件的压力时，他们的大脑就很难获得从日常压力中恢复所需的不受打扰的休息时间。

sentences.label: 例句 3
sentences.quote: Countries such as France, Australia, and Portugal have introduced laws that limit employers from expecting responses outside official working hours.
sentences.main_clause: Countries + have introduced + laws。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：such as France, Australia, and Portugal 举例修饰 Countries；that limit employers from expecting responses... 是定语从句修饰 laws。
参考理解：法国、澳大利亚和葡萄牙等国家已经出台法律，限制雇主在正式工作时间之外要求员工回复信息。

translation:
周二晚上九点半，一条工作消息点亮了你的手机屏幕。尽管这条消息并不需要立刻回复，但习惯性地查看还是瞬间把你的思绪拉回了未完成的表格和明天的会议上。在一个笔记本电脑和即时通讯应用让办公室一路“跟进”员工客厅的时代，职业职责与个人休息之间的界限变得越来越模糊。

多年来，随叫随到常常被赞誉为敬业的表现。然而，心理学家和职场研究人员警告说，“永远在线”的文化潜藏着严重的隐性代价。当员工在吃晚饭或周末感到不得不回复邮件的压力时，他们的大脑就很难获得从日常压力中恢复所需的不受打扰的休息时间。久而久之，这种长期的精神疲惫会导致职业倦怠、睡眠质量下降，以及真正工作时段专注力的减退。

作为回应，各国政府和具有前瞻性的企业正开始保护员工的“离线权”。法国、澳大利亚和葡萄牙等国家已经出台法律，限制雇主在正式工作时间之外要求员工回复信息。与此同时，一些机构采取了简单实用的规定，例如在晚上六点后关闭内部聊天通知，或将消息设定在次日早上发送。

然而，建立更健康的边界感不能仅仅依赖立法。职业规划师建议，员工个人也可以从与团队明确沟通预期、关闭私人设备上的工作提醒做起。不带手机去安静地散个步，或者每周严格留出一个晚上远离工作事务，这些看似微小的举动却大有裨益。当休息获得与高效产出同等的尊重时，员工回到办公桌前往往会更加从容、敏锐，也更有抗压韧性。

quizzes.question: What is a long-term consequence of an 'always-on' work culture mentioned in paragraph 2?

options.text: Employees receive fewer promotions and lower salaries.
Workers experience burnout, poor sleep, and reduced focus.
Companies stop using messaging apps for internal communication.
Employees spend less time with their laptops at the office.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段最后一句明确指出“Over time, this chronic mental fatigue can lead to burnout, poorer sleep quality, and declining focus during actual working hours.”。故选 B。

quizzes.question: What does the author imply in the last paragraph?

options.text: Laws alone are enough to solve workplace stress.
Checking emails at night increases personal productivity.
Respecting personal rest actually improves work performance.
Employees should quit their jobs if they receive messages after 6:00 p.m.

quizzes.explanation: 推理判断题。最后一段尾句指出“when rest is treated with the same respect as productivity, employees often return to their desks calmer, sharper, and far more resilient”，说明尊重休息反而有助于提升工作状态与表现。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Bike Sharing and Green Urban Transport（共享单车与绿色城市交通）
body:
Every weekday morning outside busy subway stations in Beijing, Amsterdam, and London, rows of brightly colored bicycles wait for commuters making the final leg of their journey. Over the past decade, bike-sharing schemes have evolved from experimental pilot programs into an essential part of modern public transit. For millions of city residents, scanning a quick code on a smartphone has replaced short taxi rides or long walks between bus stops and office buildings.

The environmental case for shared bicycles is straightforward. When short trips under three kilometers are shifted from private cars to bikes, cities see immediate drops in tailpipe emissions and traffic congestion. Equally important is the way cycling connects neighborhoods to rail networks, solving the classic "last-mile" problem that often discourages people from leaving their cars at home. In addition, regular cycling offers clear public health benefits, turning a daily commute into low-impact exercise.

Yet the rapid rise of bike sharing has not been without growing pains. In the early boom years, dockless bicycles were sometimes left piled across narrow sidewalks, frustrating pedestrians and forcing municipal authorities to step in. In response, many cities have introduced stricter management rules, including designated parking zones guided by satellite positioning and limits on fleet sizes. Meanwhile, urban planners have realized that software alone cannot protect cyclists; wider, physically separated bike lanes must be built if riding is to feel safe for beginners and older adults.

As governments aim to meet ambitious carbon-reduction targets, green urban transport requires more than simply adding bikes to the street. It demands a thoughtful redesign of road space that gives equal priority to cyclists, pedestrians, and buses. Where safe infrastructure and smart regulation work hand in hand, bike sharing proves to be far more than a passing trend—it becomes a cornerstone of cleaner, more livable cities.

vocabulary.meaning: 通勤者；上下班往返的人

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Equally important is the way cycling connects neighborhoods to rail networks, solving the classic 'last-mile' problem that often discourages people from leaving their cars at home.
sentences.main_clause: 倒装结构，Equally important (表语) + is (系动词) + the way (主语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：cycling connects neighborhoods to rail networks 是定语从句修饰 way（省略了关系词 that/in which）；solving the classic 'last-mile' problem 是现在分词短语作结果状语；that often discourages... 是定语从句修饰 problem。
参考理解：同样重要的是骑行将社区与轨道交通网络衔接起来的方式，它解决了常常让人们不愿把私家车留在家里（而选择公共交通）的经典“最后一公里”难题。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: Meanwhile, urban planners have realized that software alone cannot protect cyclists; wider, physically separated bike lanes must be built if riding is to feel safe for beginners and older adults.
sentences.main_clause: urban planners + have realized + that 从句（宾语从句）；分号后为并列分句，含被动语态 must be built。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：if riding is to feel safe... 是条件状语从句，说明修建隔离自行车道的前提需求。
参考理解：与此同时，城市规划者也意识到，仅靠软件无法保护骑行者的安全；如果要让新手和老年人也觉得骑车安全，就必须修建更宽敞且带有物理隔离的自行车道。

translation:
每个工作日的早晨，在北京、阿姆斯特丹和伦敦繁忙的地铁站外，一排排色彩鲜艳的自行车都在等待着即将完成最后一程通勤的人们。过去十年间，共享单车项目已经从试验性的试点计划，演变为现代公共交通不可或缺的一部分。对于数百万城市居民而言，用手机快速扫码已经取代了短途打车，或是在公交站与写字楼之间的长距离步行。

推广共享单车的环保理由显而易见。当三公里以内的短途出行从私家车转向自行车时，城市的尾气排放和交通拥堵会立竿见影地减少。同样重要的是骑行将社区与轨道交通网络衔接起来的方式，它解决了常常让人们不愿把私家车留在家里的经典“最后一公里”难题。此外，经常骑车还带来显著的公共健康益处，将日常通勤转化为低强度的体育锻炼。

然而，共享单车的迅猛发展也伴随着成长的烦恼。在早期的爆发式增长阶段，无桩共享单车有时会杂乱地堆放在狭窄的人行道上，令行人恼火，并迫使市政部门介入管理。作为回应，许多城市出台了更严格的管理规定，包括由卫星定位引导的指定停车区以及对投放总量的限制。与此同时，城市规划者也意识到，仅靠软件无法保护骑行者的安全；如果要让新手和老年人也觉得骑车安全，就必须修建更宽敞且带有物理隔离的自行车道。

随着各国政府致力于实现雄心勃勃的减碳目标，绿色城市交通需要的不仅仅是在街上投放更多自行车，更需要对道路空间进行深思熟虑的重新设计，让骑行者、行人与公交车获得同等的优先权。当安全的基础设施与智慧监管携手并进时，共享单车便证明自己远非一时潮流——它正成为更洁净、更宜居城市的基石。

quizzes.question: How does bike sharing help solve the 'last-mile' problem?

options.text: By replacing long-distance subway lines with bicycles.
By connecting residential neighborhoods to rail and bus networks.
By banning private cars from entering city centers.
By encouraging people to walk longer distances to work.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段第三句指出“the way cycling connects neighborhoods to rail networks, solving the classic 'last-mile' problem”。故选 B。

quizzes.question: According to the third paragraph, what is still needed to make cycling feel safe for more people?

options.text: Faster smartphone scanning apps.
More dockless bicycles piled near subway stations.
Wider bike lanes that are physically separated from other traffic.
Higher fines for pedestrians walking on sidewalks.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第三段最后一句明确提到“wider, physically separated bike lanes must be built if riding is to feel safe for beginners and older adults”。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Esports Enters the Mainstream Sports Arena（电子竞技成为正式体育项目）
body:
Not long ago, competitive video gaming was widely dismissed by parents and traditional sports fans as a harmless hobby at best, and a waste of time at worst. Yet when esports debuted as an official medal event at the 19th Asian Games in Hangzhou, millions of viewers watched national teams compete under roaring stadium lights. What once took place in quiet internet cafés has now stepped firmly onto the global sporting stage.

Supporters of this shift point out that elite esports requires far more than fast fingers. Professional players train for hours every day, studying tactical replays, refining team communication, and maintaining sharp mental focus under intense pressure. Just like chess masters or Olympic archers, gamers must make split-second strategic decisions while managing stress and physical fatigue. In fact, many top clubs now employ fitness coaches, nutritionists, and sports psychologists to keep their squads in peak condition.

Despite its booming popularity, the inclusion of esports in major sporting events still sparks lively debate. Critics argue that true athletics should involve significant physical movement rather than sitting in front of a screen. Others raise concerns about the commercial nature of video games, since every title is owned and regularly updated by a private company—unlike soccer or swimming, whose rules belong to no single corporation. There are also persistent worries that glorifying competitive gaming might encourage unhealthy screen habits among teenagers.

Even so, international sporting bodies recognize that audiences are changing rapidly. By welcoming esports into the arena, events like the Asian Games hope to connect with younger generations who already treat digital tournaments as mainstream entertainment. Whether or not everyone agrees on the definition of "sport," competitive gaming has clearly earned its place in modern cultural life—and its influence shows no sign of slowing down.

vocabulary.meaning: 持续存在的；坚持不懈的

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Not long ago, competitive video gaming was widely dismissed by parents and traditional sports fans as a harmless hobby at best, and a waste of time at worst.
sentences.main_clause: competitive video gaming (主语) + was widely dismissed (一般过去时被动语态) + as a harmless hobby... (介词短语作补语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：Not long ago 是时间状语；by parents and traditional sports fans 是被动语态的动作发出者；at best / at worst 构成对称对比，意为“往好了说……往坏了说……”。
参考理解：就在不久前，竞技类电子游戏还被家长和传统体育迷普遍轻视——往好了说不过是一种无害的消遣，往坏了说则是浪费时间。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: Others raise concerns about the commercial nature of video games, since every title is owned and regularly updated by a private company—unlike soccer or swimming, whose rules belong to no single corporation.
sentences.main_clause: Others + raise + concerns。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：since every title is owned and regularly updated... 是原因状语从句（含被动语态）；破折号后 unlike soccer or swimming 作对比，其中 whose rules belong to no single corporation 是非限制性定语从句，修饰 soccer or swimming。
参考理解：另一些人则对电子游戏的商业属性表示担忧，因为每一款游戏都由私人公司拥有并定期更新——这与足球或游泳不同，后者的规则不属于任何一家单独的企业。

translation:
就在不久前，竞技类电子游戏还被家长和传统体育迷普遍轻视——往好了说不过是一种无害的消遣，往坏了说则是浪费时间。然而，当电子竞技作为正式奖牌项目在杭州第19届亚运会首次亮相时，数百万观众目睹了各国代表队在喧嚣的体育场灯光下展开角逐。曾经发生在安静网吧里的比拼，如今已稳稳踏上全球体育的舞台。

支持这一转变的人士指出，顶尖电子竞技所需要的远不止手指灵活。职业选手每天训练数小时，研究战术回放、磨合团队沟通，并在巨大压力下保持高度集中的注意力。正如国际象棋大师或奥运射箭选手一样，电竞选手必须在应对压力和身体疲劳的同时，在毫秒之间做出战略决策。事实上，如今许多顶级俱乐部都聘请了体能教练、营养师和运动心理学家，以使队伍保持巅峰状态。

尽管人气飙升，电竞被纳入大型体育赛事仍然引发了热烈争论。批评者认为，真正的体育运动应当包含大量的身体活动，而不是坐在屏幕前。另一些人则对电子游戏的商业属性表示担忧，因为每一款游戏都由私人公司拥有并定期更新——这与足球或游泳不同，后者的规则不属于任何一家单独的企业。此外，人们还持续担心，赞美竞技游戏可能会助长青少年不健康的屏幕使用习惯。

即便如此，国际体育组织已经意识到观众群体正在迅速变化。通过接纳电竞进入赛场，亚运会等赛事希望能与早已将数字锦标赛视为常规娱乐的年轻一代建立联系。无论人们是否对“体育”的定义达成一致，电子竞技显然已经在现代文化生活中赢得了一席之地——而且其影响力丝毫没有放缓的迹象。

quizzes.question: Why do many top esports clubs hire fitness coaches and sports psychologists?

options.text: To help players design new video game rules.
To keep players in top physical and mental condition.
To teach traditional sports such as soccer and swimming.
To reduce the commercial cost of running tournaments.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段尾句指出“many top clubs now employ fitness coaches, nutritionists, and sports psychologists to keep their squads in peak condition”，即帮助队员保持最佳身心状态。故选 B。

quizzes.question: Which concern about esports is mentioned in paragraph 3?

options.text: Esports matches do not attract enough young viewers.
Professional players refuse to practice team communication.
Individual video games are controlled by private companies.
Stadium lights cause serious eye injuries to spectators.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第三段提到批评者的三点担忧：缺乏大量肢体运动、游戏归私人公司所有并更新（商业属性）、以及对青少年屏幕习惯的影响。C 项与原文“every title is owned and regularly updated by a private company”一致。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Thinking Beyond the Plastic Straw Ban（塑料吸管禁令背后的环保思考）
body:
When cafes and fast-food chains across the globe began replacing single-use plastic straws with paper ones, many consumers welcomed the move as a victory for the oceans. Images of marine animals harmed by plastic waste had sparked widespread public anger, turning the humble drinking straw into a powerful symbol of environmental action. Yet as paper straws dissolved quickly in iced drinks and plastic cups continued to pile up in bins, scientists started asking an uncomfortable question: were we focusing on the easiest target rather than the biggest problem?

Research shows that plastic straws actually account for less than one percent of the plastic waste entering the world's oceans each year. Far larger shares come from discarded fishing nets, food wrappers, and single-use bottles. In addition, some alternatives are not always as green as they appear. Certain paper straws are coated with thin chemical layers to keep them from going soft, which can prevent them from breaking down cleanly in nature or being recycled alongside ordinary paper.

None of this means that banning plastic straws was pointless. Behavioral economists note that visible, everyday changes often raise public awareness and encourage people to rethink their habits. A customer who refuses a straw may soon notice how much unnecessary packaging surrounds their lunch and start carrying a reusable cup or cloth bag.

However, environmental experts emphasize that symbolic gestures must lead to deeper systemic reform if real progress is to be achieved. Rather than simply swapping one disposable item for another, governments and manufacturers need to redesign packaging systems, invest in better recycling infrastructure, and hold companies responsible for the entire life cycle of their products. Real sustainability begins not when we feel guilty about a single straw, but when reducing waste becomes the effortless default choice.

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Certain paper straws are coated with thin chemical layers to keep them from going soft, which can prevent them from breaking down cleanly in nature or being recycled alongside ordinary paper.
sentences.main_clause: Certain paper straws + are coated with (一般现在时被动语态) + thin chemical layers。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：to keep them from going soft 是目的状语；which can prevent them from... 是非限制性定语从句，指代前面整件事（涂有化学涂层）。
参考理解：某些纸吸管表面涂有薄薄的化学涂层以防止其变软，而这反而会阻碍它们在自然界中彻底降解，或无法与普通纸张一同回收。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: Real sustainability begins not when we feel guilty about a single straw, but when reducing waste becomes the effortless default choice.
sentences.main_clause: Real sustainability + begins + not when... but when...（由 not... but... 连接两个时间状语从句作对比）。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 参考理解：真正的可持续发展，并非始于我们对一根吸管产生愧疚之时，而是始于减少浪费成为毫不费力的默认选择之时。

translation:
当全球各地的咖啡馆和快餐连锁店开始用纸吸管取代一次性塑料吸管时，许多消费者将这一举措视为海洋保护的胜利。海洋动物受塑料垃圾伤害的画面激起了广泛的公众愤怒，使这根不起眼的吸管变成了环保行动的有力象征。然而，随着纸吸管在冰饮中迅速泡软，而塑料杯依然在垃圾桶里堆积如山，科学家们开始提出一个令人不安的问题：我们是不是只盯住了最容易下手的目标，而忽略了真正的大问题？

研究表明，塑料吸管实际上只占每年流入全球海洋塑料垃圾的不到百分之一。占更大比重的是废弃渔网、食品包装袋以及一次性塑料瓶。此外，一些替代品也并不总是像表面看起来那样环保。某些纸吸管表面涂有薄薄的化学涂层以防止其变软，而这反而会阻碍它们在自然界中彻底降解，或无法与普通纸张一同回收。

这并不意味着禁用塑料吸管毫无意义。行为经济学家指出，日常可见的微小改变往往能提高公众意识，并促使人们重新审视自己的生活习惯。一位拒绝使用吸管的顾客，可能很快就会注意到午餐周围有多少不必要的包装，从而开始随身携带可重复使用的水杯或布袋。

然而，环境专家强调，若想取得实质性进展，象征性的姿态必须推动更深层次的系统性改革。政府和制造商不能仅仅把一种一次性用品换成另一种，而需要重新设计包装体系，投资更完善的回收基础设施，并要求企业对其产品的整个生命周期负责。真正的可持续发展，并非始于我们对一根吸管产生愧疚之时，而是始于减少浪费成为毫不费力的默认选择之时。

quizzes.question: Why do scientists question the real impact of replacing plastic straws with paper ones?

options.text: Plastic straws make up a very small fraction of ocean plastic waste.
Paper straws are too expensive for fast-food chains to produce.
Consumers refuse to buy iced drinks without plastic straws.
Fishing nets are easier to recycle than ordinary paper.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段第一句指出“plastic straws actually account for less than one percent of the plastic waste entering the world's oceans each year”，且某些纸吸管因涂层也难降解。故选 A。

quizzes.question: According to the last paragraph, what is key to achieving real sustainability?

options.text: Making consumers feel guilty whenever they buy packaged food.
Redesigning packaging systems and improving recycling infrastructure.
Replacing every plastic product with paper alternatives.
Asking individual customers to stop visiting cafes.

quizzes.explanation: 主旨与细节理解题。最后一段提出，需要“redesign packaging systems, invest in better recycling infrastructure, and hold companies responsible...”，即系统性改革与完善回收体系。故选 B。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Why Boredom Can Spark Creativity（为什么“无聊”反而激发创造力）
body:
Whenever we find ourselves standing in a slow grocery line or waiting for a delayed train, our hands almost automatically reach into our pockets for a smartphone. Within seconds, short videos, news alerts, and social feeds fill every quiet gap in the day. While digital entertainment makes waiting effortless, psychologists warn that modern people are quietly losing a surprisingly valuable mental state: boredom.

At first glance, boredom feels unpleasant—a restless itch that we want to scratch as quickly as possible. Yet brain researchers explain that when our minds are not occupied by urgent tasks or constant screen stimulation, a special neural system called the "default mode network" switches on. This is the state in which the brain wanders freely, connects distant memories, and rehearses future scenarios. Many novelists, scientists, and designers report that their best ideas arrive not while staring intensely at a desk, but while taking a shower, folding laundry, or gazing out of a train window.

Laboratory studies support this observation. In one well-known experiment, participants who were first given a dull, repetitive task—such as copying phone numbers from a directory—later came up with far more original uses for everyday objects than a group that had moved straight into the creative test. By forcing the mind to slow down, mild boredom seems to push people to seek internal curiosity rather than external distraction.

Of course, sitting idle all day will not automatically turn anyone into a genius. The benefits of boredom appear most clearly when it serves as brief breathing room between periods of focused study or work. Learning to leave a few unscheduled minutes without reaching for a screen may feel awkward at first. Yet those quiet pauses give our minds the space they need to reflect, problem-solve, and imagine something genuinely new.

vocabulary.meaning: 排练；预演；在脑海中演练
未安排日程的；计划外的

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Yet brain researchers explain that when our minds are not occupied by urgent tasks or constant screen stimulation, a special neural system called the 'default mode network' switches on.
sentences.main_clause: brain researchers + explain + that 从句（宾语从句）。
sentences.grammar:
结构拆解：
宾语从句内部：when our minds are not occupied... 为时间状语从句（含被动语态）；a special neural system... switches on 为从句主干，其中 called the 'default mode network' 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 system。
notes: 参考理解：然而，脑科学研究者解释说，当我们的思维没有被紧急任务或持续的屏幕刺激占满时，一个被称为“默认模式网络”的特殊神经系统就会开启。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: In one well-known experiment, participants who were first given a dull, repetitive task—such as copying phone numbers from a directory—later came up with far more original uses for everyday objects than a group that had moved straight into the creative test.
sentences.main_clause: participants (主语) + later came up with (谓语) + far more original uses (宾语) + than a group... (比较状语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：who were first given a dull, repetitive task... 是定语从句修饰 participants；that had moved straight into the creative test 是定语从句修饰 group。
参考理解：在一项著名的实验中，先被分配去做枯燥重复任务（如抄写电话簿号码）的参与者，随后为日常物品想出的新颖用途，比直接进入创意测试的那一组要多得多。

translation:
每当我们发现自己正排在缓慢前行的超市队伍里，或等待一趟晚点的火车时，手几乎会下意识地伸进口袋掏出智能手机。短短几秒钟内，短视频、新闻推送和社交动态便填满了生活中的每一处安静缝隙。尽管数字娱乐让等待变得毫不费力，但心理学家警告称，现代人正在悄然失去一种出人意料地宝贵的心理状态：无聊。

乍一看，无聊让人感到不适——就像一种让人想尽快挠一挠的躁动痒感。然而，脑科学研究者解释说，当我们的思维没有被紧急任务或持续的屏幕刺激占满时，一个被称为“默认模式网络”的特殊神经系统就会开启。在这种状态下，大脑会自由漫游，将遥远的记忆串联起来，并预演未来的各种情景。许多小说家、科学家和设计师都表示，他们最棒的灵感往往不是在伏案苦思时迸发的，而是在淋浴、叠衣服或凝望火车窗外时悄然而至。

实验室研究也印证了这一观察。在一项著名的实验中，先被分配去做枯燥重复任务（如抄写电话簿号码）的参与者，随后为日常物品想出的新颖用途，比直接进入创意测试的那一组要多得多。适度的无聊通过迫使思维放慢节奏，似乎能推动人们去探索内在的好奇心，而非依赖外界的消遣。

当然，整天无所事事并不会自动把任何人变成天才。当无聊充当专注学习或工作间隙短暂的“喘息空间”时，它的益处最为明显。学会在日程中留出几分钟空白而不去伸手拿手机，起初可能会让人觉得别扭。但正是这些安静的停顿，给了我们的大脑所需的空间，去反思、解决问题，并构想出真正崭新的事物。

quizzes.question: What happens when the brain's 'default mode network' switches on?

options.text: People feel compelled to check news alerts immediately.
The mind wanders, links memories, and imagines future scenarios.
Concentration on urgent spreadsheet tasks increases sharply.
The brain shuts down completely to recover from fatigue.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段第三句明确说明“This is the state in which the brain wanders freely, connects distant memories, and rehearses future scenarios.”。故选 B。

quizzes.question: Why did the participants who copied phone numbers perform better in the creative test?

options.text: Copying numbers improved their memory of everyday objects.
They had more time to practice the creative test beforehand.
Experiencing mild boredom stimulated their internal creativity.
They were allowed to watch short videos between tasks.

quizzes.explanation: 推理判断题。第三段通过实验说明，先经历枯燥任务带来适度无聊，迫使思维放慢并激发内在好奇心，从而提出更多独创想法。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Digital Museums and Virtual Exhibitions（博物馆数字化与虚拟看展）
body:
For centuries, stepping inside a great museum required buying a ticket, queuing at the entrance, and sometimes traveling halfway across the world. Today, however, a curious visitor in a small town can examine brushstroke details on an oil painting in Paris or rotate a three-dimensional model of an ancient bronze vessel in Xi'an—all from a tablet at the kitchen table. Driven by high-resolution scanning and virtual reality, museums are opening their collections to a global audience on an unprecedented scale.

Digital technology has changed far more than where people view art; it has transformed how history is preserved and explained. Fragile manuscripts and faded silk scrolls that are too delicate to be displayed under bright gallery lights can now be photographed under specialized cameras and studied freely online. In physical halls, augmented reality glasses and interactive touchscreens allow visitors to see how a broken marble statue once looked when it was brightly painted, bridging the gap between silent artifacts and living stories.

Critics sometimes worry that virtual tours might weaken the magic of standing in front of a real masterpiece. Looking at a glowing screen, they argue, cannot replace the sense of awe felt inside a quiet cathedral-like gallery. Museum directors largely agree that digital access is not meant to replace physical visits. In fact, many institutions report that viewers who discover an exhibition online often become eager to travel and see the original pieces in person.

Perhaps the greatest achievement of digital museums lies in educational equality. Students in rural schools who may never visit a capital city can now explore world heritage alongside expert commentary, free of charge. By turning locked storage rooms into open digital archives, museums are proving that preserving the past and embracing modern technology can strengthen one another.

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Fragile manuscripts and faded silk scrolls that are too delicate to be displayed under bright gallery lights can now be photographed under specialized cameras and studied freely online.
sentences.main_clause: Fragile manuscripts and faded silk scrolls (主语) + can now be photographed and studied (含情态动词的被动语态)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：that are too delicate to be displayed under bright gallery lights 是定语从句，修饰 manuscripts and silk scrolls，其中含 too... to... 结构。
参考理解：那些过于脆弱、无法在明亮展厅灯光下展出的珍贵手稿和褪色丝绸卷轴，如今可以在专业相机下完成拍摄，并在网上自由研读。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: In fact, many institutions report that viewers who discover an exhibition online often become eager to travel and see the original pieces in person.
sentences.main_clause: many institutions + report + that 从句（宾语从句）。
sentences.grammar:
结构拆解：
宾语从句内部：viewers (主语) + often become eager to travel and see...；其中 who discover an exhibition online 是定语从句修饰 viewers。
notes: 参考理解：事实上，许多文博机构反映，在网上发现某个展览的观众，往往会更渴望亲自前往一睹真迹。

translation:
几个世纪以来，走进一座知名博物馆意味着买票、在入口排队，有时甚至需要跨越半个地球去旅行。然而今天，小镇上一位充满好奇心的访客，只需在餐桌旁打开平板电脑，就能端详巴黎一幅油画上的笔触细节，或旋转西安一件古代青铜器的三维模型。在高分辨率扫描与虚拟现实技术的推动下，博物馆正以前所未有的规模向全球观众敞开馆藏大门。

数字技术改变的远不止人们看展的地点，它还革新了历史被保存和阐释的方式。那些过于脆弱、无法在明亮展厅灯光下展出的珍贵手稿和褪色丝绸卷轴，如今可以在专业相机下完成拍摄，并在网上自由研读。在实体展馆中，增强现实眼镜和交互式触控屏让参观者得以看到一尊残破的大理石雕像昔日鲜艳上色时的模样，在沉默的文物与鲜活的故事之间架起桥梁。

批评者有时会担心，虚拟游览可能会削弱站在真正杰作面前的魔力。他们认为，盯着发光的屏幕无法替代置身于教堂般肃穆展厅中的敬畏之感。对此，博物馆馆长们普遍认同，数字化开放并非旨在取代实地参观。事实上，许多文博机构反映，在网上发现某个展览的观众，往往会更渴望亲自前往一睹真迹。

数字化博物馆最伟大的成就或许在于促进教育公平。那些可能从未去过首都城市的乡村学校学生，如今可以免费在专家讲解的陪伴下探索世界遗产。通过将紧锁的文物库房转变为开放的数字档案库，博物馆正在证明，守护过去与拥抱现代科技完全可以相辅相成。

quizzes.question: How does digital technology help protect fragile historical items?

options.text: By placing brighter lights over silk scrolls in physical halls.
By photographing them so they can be studied online without display damage.
By repainting broken marble statues with modern colors.
By locking all museum entrances to reduce visitor numbers.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段第二句说明“Fragile manuscripts and faded silk scrolls that are too delicate to be displayed... can now be photographed under specialized cameras and studied freely online”，避免强光展出损害文物。故选 B。

quizzes.question: According to museum directors, what effect does online access often have on physical visits?

options.text: It encourages online viewers to visit the museum in person.
It causes a permanent drop in ticket sales.
It replaces the need for expert commentary.
It makes rural students less interested in world heritage.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第三段最后一句提到，网上发现展览的观众往往会渴望亲自前往看真迹。故选 A。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Part-Time Jobs and Practical Skills（大学生兼职与实践能力）
body:
Ask university graduates what surprised them most during their first full-time job, and many will mention the gap between lecture halls and the real workplace. While degree courses provide vital theoretical knowledge, employers frequently notice that fresh graduates still struggle with everyday professional skills: managing tight deadlines, handling difficult customers, or working smoothly in a diverse team. That is one major reason why part-time jobs during college are increasingly valued by both students and career advisors.

Whether working as a campus library assistant, a coffee shop server, or a junior intern at a local business, students gain lessons that textbooks rarely teach. A busy weekend shift at a café, for instance, trains a young person to stay calm under pressure and communicate clearly with impatient guests. Even routine tasks—such as balancing a cash register or organizing delivery schedules—help build reliability and a sense of accountability. Furthermore, earning a modest paycheck often teaches students how to budget wisely and appreciate the value of hard work.

Of course, taking on paid work during term time carries clear risks if it is not managed carefully. Research in higher education shows that students who work excessive hours—often more than twenty hours a week—tend to experience higher stress and lower exam scores. When late-night shifts leave no time for reading or rest, a job meant to support future career prospects can end up harming academic performance.

Finding the right balance therefore requires thoughtful planning. Career centers recommend choosing roles that offer flexible schedules or relate loosely to a student's long-term interests. When kept within reasonable limits, part-time work does not compete with university study; instead, it complements classroom learning and helps young people step into the job market with greater confidence.

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Whether working as a campus library assistant, a coffee shop server, or a junior intern at a local business, students gain lessons that textbooks rarely teach.
sentences.main_clause: students (主语) + gain (谓语) + lessons (宾语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：Whether working as... 是让步状语从句（省略了主语和 be 动词 they are）；that textbooks rarely teach 是定语从句修饰 lessons。
参考理解：无论是担任校园图书馆助理、咖啡店服务员，还是本地企业的初级实习生，学生们都能收获课本上极少传授的经验。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: When late-night shifts leave no time for reading or rest, a job meant to support future career prospects can end up harming academic performance.
sentences.main_clause: a job (主语) + can end up harming (谓语) + academic performance (宾语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：When late-night shifts leave... 是时间状语从句；meant to support future career prospects 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 job。
参考理解：当深夜班次让人无暇阅读或休息时，一份原本旨在助力未来职业前景的工作，最终反而可能损害学业表现。

translation:
问问大学毕业生第一份全职工作中最让他们惊讶的是什么，许多人都会提到课堂讲授与真实职场之间的落差。尽管学位课程提供了至关重要的理论知识，但雇主们经常注意到，应届毕业生在日常职业技能方面仍有欠缺：比如把控紧凑的截止日期、应对难缠的顾客，或者在多元化的团队中顺畅协作。这正是大学期间的兼职工作越来越受到学生和职业顾问重视的一个重要原因。

无论是担任校园图书馆助理、咖啡店服务员，还是本地企业的初级实习生，学生们都能收获课本上极少传授的经验。例如，在咖啡馆忙碌的周末班次中工作，能够训练年轻人在压力下保持冷静，并与缺乏耐心的客人清晰沟通。即便是核对收银账目或安排配送日程这类日常杂务，也有助于培养可靠性和责任感。此外，赚取一份微薄的薪水往往能教会学生如何精明预算，并体会劳动的价值。

当然，如果安排不当，学期内从事有偿工作也伴随着明显的风险。高等教育领域的研究表明，每周工作时间过长——通常超过20小时——的学生，往往面临更高的心理压力和更低的考试成绩。当深夜班次让人无暇阅读或休息时，一份原本旨在助力未来职业前景的工作，最终反而可能损害学业表现。

因此，找到恰当的平衡需要周密的规划。就业指导中心建议选择时间灵活，或与自身长期兴趣有一定关联的岗位。只要控制在合理范围内，兼职工作就不会与大学学业相冲突；相反，它能与课堂学习相辅相成，帮助年轻人更加自信地迈入职场。

quizzes.question: What is one benefit of working a part-time job during university mentioned in paragraph 2?

options.text: It guarantees a high-paying job immediately after graduation.
It helps students develop calmness, reliability, and budgeting skills.
It allows students to skip theoretical degree courses.
It replaces the need for campus libraries and career advisors.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段指出兼职可以让人在压力下保持冷静（stay calm under pressure）、培养可靠性（reliability）以及学会合理预算（budget wisely）。故选 B。

quizzes.question: When can a part-time job negatively affect a student?

options.text: When it relates closely to the student's future career interests.
When it takes up too many hours and leaves little time for study or rest.
When the student works as a junior intern at a local company.
When the student learns how to communicate with impatient guests.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第三段明确提到每周工作超过20小时、深夜班次挤占阅读和休息时间时，会损害学业表现。故选 B。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: The Rise of the Sleep Economy（睡眠经济：助眠产品的流行）
body:
In an age of endless notifications and late-night work culture, getting eight hours of peaceful rest has become something many people are willing to pay handsomely for. Walk down a pharmacy aisle or browse an online marketplace, and you will find a booming industry dedicated entirely to bedtime: weighted blankets, smart mattresses that track breathing, herbal teas, white-noise machines, and guided meditation apps. Economists call this fast-growing sector the "sleep economy," which is now valued at hundreds of billions of dollars worldwide.

Younger adults, particularly urban professionals and college students, are driving much of this surging demand. Facing intense academic competition, irregular work schedules, and constant screen exposure before bed, millions report difficulty falling asleep or waking up feeling truly refreshed. Because poor rest affects mood, memory, immunity, and long-term physical health, consumers increasingly treat sleep products not as luxury items, but as essential investments in daily self-care.

Yet sleep specialists urge shoppers to look closely at marketing claims before filling their online shopping carts. While a cooling pillow or a thick blackout curtain can genuinely make a bedroom darker and more comfortable, many expensive high-tech gadgets lack strong independent scientific evidence. In fact, doctors warn that obsessing over nightly sleep scores generated by wearable trackers can sometimes backfire, creating extra anxiety that makes it even harder to fall asleep.

Ultimately, experts remind us that quality rest cannot simply be purchased in a box or downloaded from an app store. Maintaining consistent bedtimes, keeping the bedroom dim and quiet, and putting away smartphones an hour before sleep remain the most reliable remedies—and they cost nothing at all. As the sleep economy continues to expand rapidly, the healthiest approach may be combining sensible, practical tools with disciplined daily habits, rather than expecting technology alone to fix an exhausted lifestyle.

sentences.label: 例句 1
sentences.quote: Economists call this fast-growing sector the 'sleep economy,' which is now valued at hundreds of billions of dollars worldwide.
sentences.main_clause: Economists (主语) + call (谓语) + this fast-growing sector (宾语) + the 'sleep economy' (宾语补足语)。
sentences.grammar: 结构拆解：
notes: 修饰成分：which is now valued at... 是非限制性定语从句（含被动语态），补充说明 the 'sleep economy' 的全球估值规模。
参考理解：经济学家将这一快速增长的领域称为“睡眠经济”，目前其在全球的估值已达数千亿美元。

sentences.label: 例句 2
sentences.quote: In fact, doctors warn that obsessing over nightly sleep scores generated by wearable trackers can sometimes backfire, creating extra anxiety that makes it even harder to fall asleep.
sentences.main_clause: doctors + warn + that 从句（宾语从句）。
sentences.grammar:
结构拆解：
宾语从句内部：obsessing over nightly sleep scores... (动名词短语作主语) + can sometimes backfire (谓语)；其中 generated by wearable trackers 是过去分词短语修饰 scores；creating extra anxiety... 是现在分词短语作结果状语；that makes it even harder to fall asleep 是定语从句修饰 anxiety。
notes: 参考理解：事实上，医生警告说，过度纠结可穿戴追踪设备生成的每晚睡眠评分有时会适得其反，反而制造额外焦虑，让人更难入睡。

translation:
在消息通知无穷无尽、熬夜加班司空见惯的时代，睡足八小时安稳好觉已经成为许多人愿意慷慨花钱购买的体验。走进药妆店货架通道或浏览网购平台，你会发现一个完全围绕就寝时间蓬勃发展的产业：重力毯、能追踪呼吸的智能床垫、草本助眠茶、白噪音机以及引导式冥想应用程序。经济学家将这一快速增长的领域称为“睡眠经济”，目前其在全球的估值已达数千亿美元。

年轻群体，尤其是都市职场人和大学生，正推动着这一激增需求的大部分增长。面对激烈的学业竞争、不规律的工作作息以及睡前持续的屏幕接触，数百万人反映自己难以入睡或醒来后未能真正恢复精力。由于睡眠不佳会影响情绪、记忆力、免疫力以及长期身体健康，消费者越来越多地将助眠产品视为日常自我关怀的必要投入，而非奢侈品。

然而，睡眠专家提醒购物者在塞满网络购物车之前，先仔细审视商家的宣传话术。虽然凉感枕头或厚实的遮光窗帘确实能让卧室更暗、更舒适，但许多昂贵的高科技小工具缺乏有力的独立科学证据。事实上，医生警告说，过度纠结可穿戴追踪设备生成的每晚睡眠评分有时会适得其反，反而制造额外焦虑，让人更难入睡。

归根结底，专家们提醒我们，高质量的休息无法简单地装在盒子里买回家，也无法从应用商店下载。保持规律的就寝时间、让卧室保持昏暗安静，以及睡前一小时放下手机，依然是最可靠的良方——而且分文不花。随着睡眠经济持续快速扩张，最健康的做法或许是将实用合理的工具与自律的日常习惯结合起来，而不是指望单靠科技去修补一种本就透支的生活方式。

quizzes.question: Why do younger adults treat sleep products as essential investments rather than luxuries?

options.text: Because sleep trackers are required by most universities.
Because poor sleep negatively impacts mood, memory, and long-term health.
Because herbal teas and weighted blankets are cheaper than food.
Because economists advise everyone to spend more at night.

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第二段最后一句明确指出“Because poor rest affects mood, memory, and long-term health, consumers increasingly treat sleep products not as luxury items, but as essential investments in self-care.”。故选 B。

quizzes.question: What is the experts' main advice in the last two paragraphs?

options.text: Buy the most expensive smart mattress available online.
Check your nightly sleep score immediately after waking up.
Combine sensible tools with healthy, consistent sleep habits.
Avoid using blackout curtains or quiet bedrooms.

quizzes.explanation: 主旨理解题。最后两段提醒消费者不要盲信昂贵设备，最后一句点明“the healthiest approach may be combining sensible tools with disciplined daily habits”。故选 C。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: The Power of Micro-Habits（微习惯的力量）
body:
Every January, millions of people make ambitious resolutions to transform their lives, yet most of these promises are abandoned before February arrives. Why do big plans fail so often? According to behavioral psychologists, the human brain is naturally wired to resist sudden, drastic changes that require high levels of willpower. When a goal feels overwhelming, we tend to procrastinate rather than take action.

This is where micro-habits offer a surprisingly effective alternative. A micro-habit is an action so small that it seems almost effortless—such as reading two pages of a book before bed, doing five push-ups after brushing your teeth, or writing a single sentence in a journal. Because the barrier to starting is extremely low, the brain rarely triggers the stress response that usually blocks new routines. Once the initial step is completed, momentum often carries you further than you originally planned.

In a widely discussed study conducted by researchers at University College London, participants who attached tiny behaviors to existing daily routines formed lasting habits much faster than those who relied on strict schedules. For instance, a commuter who listens to a five-minute English podcast while waiting for the subway is more likely to stay consistent than someone who sets aside an entire hour on weekends. Over time, these modest actions are compounded into meaningful progress, much like small deposits growing in a savings account.

Of course, micro-habits are not meant to replace long-term ambition. Instead, they serve as reliable stepping stones that build self-trust and consistency. When you prove to yourself that you can keep a small promise every day, larger challenges gradually become less intimidating. Real transformation, it turns out, is rarely achieved through dramatic overnight effort; rather, it is quietly shaped by the tiny choices we repeat when nobody is watching.

vocabulary.meaning: 有雄心的；宏大的；费力的
行为的；行为科学方面的
使复利增长；使加重；合成

sentences.label: 句子 1

sentences.main_clause: the human brain is wired to resist sudden, drastic changes（人脑天生倾向于抗拒突如其来的剧烈变化）。

notes: 修饰成分：According to behavioral psychologists 为介词短语作状语；is naturally wired to... 为被动语态结构（be wired to do“天生倾向于做……”）；that require high levels of willpower 是 that 引导的定语从句，修饰先行词 changes。

translation:
每年一月，数百万人都会立下雄心勃勃的新年决心来改变生活，但大多数承诺还没等到二月到来就已经被放弃了。为什么宏大的计划总是这么容易失败呢？行为心理学家指出，人类的大脑天生倾向于抗拒那些需要高度意志力的突然且剧烈的改变。当一个目标让人感到难以承受时，我们往往会选择拖延，而不是立刻行动。

这正是微习惯能够提供一种令人惊喜的有效替代方案的原因。所谓微习惯，是指小到几乎不费吹灰之力的行动——比如睡前读两页书、刷完牙后做五个俯卧撑，或者在日记本上写下一句话。由于开始的门槛极低，大脑很少会触发通常阻碍新习惯养成的压力反应。一旦迈出了第一步，行动的势头往往会推着你走得比原计划更远。

在伦敦大学学院研究人员开展的一项广受讨论的研究中，将微小行为与现有日常习惯绑定在一起的参与者，比依赖严格时间表的人更快地养成了持久的习惯。例如，在等地铁时听五分钟英语播客的通勤者，比周末专门腾出一整小时学习的人更容易坚持下来。随着时间推移，这些微小的行动会像储蓄账户里不断复利增长的小额存款一样，累积成实实在在的进步。

当然，微习惯并不是为了取代长远的抱负。相反，它们充当了可靠的垫脚石，帮助人们建立自信与持之以恒的能力。当你向自己证明你每天都能信守一个小小的承诺时，更大的挑战就会逐渐变得不再那么令人生畏。事实证明，真正的蜕变很少通过一夜之间的剧烈努力来实现；相反，它是由我们在无人注视时日复一日重复的微小选择悄悄塑造出来的。

quizzes.question: Why do people often fail to keep ambitious New Year's resolutions according to the passage?

options.text: They lack useful advice from behavioral psychologists.
Their brains tend to resist sudden changes demanding strong willpower.
They are too busy commuting to follow any daily routine.
Most goals cannot be measured in a short period of time.

quizzes.explanation:
答案：B
- 解析：细节理解题。根据第一段第三句“the human brain is naturally wired to resist sudden, drastic changes that require high levels of willpower”，大脑天生抗拒需要强大意志力的剧烈改变，因此宏大计划容易失败。B 项为同义改写。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Ocean Conservation and Coral Reef Restoration（海洋保护与珊瑚礁修复）
body:
Beneath the surface of tropical oceans, coral reefs form vibrant underwater cities that support roughly a quarter of all marine species. Often called the rainforests of the sea, these fragile ecosystems also protect coastal communities from powerful storms and sustain local fishing and tourism industries. However, over the past few decades, rising ocean temperatures and pollution have severely damaged reefs around the world. When water becomes too warm, corals expel the microscopic algae that give them both color and nutrients, a process known as coral bleaching.

In response to this crisis, marine scientists and conservationists are turning to innovative restoration methods. One promising technique is known as "coral gardening," in which healthy coral fragments are collected and grown in underwater nurseries until they are strong enough to be transplanted back onto damaged reefs. Although this approach requires careful monitoring, it has already helped revive degraded areas in the Caribbean and parts of Southeast Asia. Local divers and community volunteers are frequently trained to clean algae from the nursery frames, turning conservation into a shared regional effort.

Beyond physical replanting, researchers are also exploring biological solutions. Some laboratories are breeding heat-tolerant coral varieties that can survive warmer seas, while others use underwater speakers to play the sounds of healthy reefs. Studies have shown that young fish and coral larvae are attracted to these lively acoustic environments, which encourages them to settle and rebuild the ecosystem naturally.

Still, experts emphasize that restoration projects alone cannot save the oceans if the root causes of degradation are ignored. Unless global carbon emissions are reduced and plastic waste is properly managed, newly planted corals will continue to face extreme stress. Protecting coral reefs ultimately requires combining scientific innovation with determined policy action, ensuring that these irreplaceable marine habitats remain alive for future generations.

vocabulary.meaning: 不可替代的；独一无二的

notes: 修饰成分：in which... 是“介词 + 关系代词”引导的非限制性定语从句，修饰 coral gardening，从句中包含被动语态（are collected and grown）；until they are strong enough to be transplanted... 为 until 引导的时间状语从句，其中 to be transplanted 为不定式的被动形式。

translation:
在热带海洋的水面之下，珊瑚礁构成了生机勃勃的水下城市，支撑着大约四分之一的海洋物种。这些被称为“海洋雨林”的脆弱生态系统，还保护着沿海社区免受强风暴的侵袭，并维系着当地的渔业和旅游业。然而，在过去几十年里，海水温度上升和污染严重破坏了世界各地的珊瑚礁。当水温过高时，珊瑚会排出为其提供色彩和养分的微藻，这一过程被称为“珊瑚白化”。

为了应对这一危机，海洋科学家和环保人士正转向创新的修复方法。一种颇具前景的技术被称为“珊瑚园艺”，即采集健康的珊瑚碎片并在水下苗圃中培育，直到它们足够强壮后再被移植回受损的珊瑚礁上。尽管这种方法需要细致的监测，但它已经在加勒比海和东南亚部分地区帮助恢复了退化的海域。当地潜水员和社区志愿者也经常接受培训，负责清理苗圃架上的藻类，使生态保护成为一项区域共同参与的事业。

除了人工补种之外，研究人员也在探索生物学解决方案。一些实验室正在培育能够适应更温暖海域的耐热珊瑚品种，而另一些研究团队则利用水下扬声器播放健康珊瑚礁的声音。研究表明，幼鱼和珊瑚幼虫会被这种热闹的声学环境所吸引，从而促使它们在此定居并自然地重建生态系统。

不过，专家们强调，如果忽视导致生态退化的根本原因，仅靠修复项目无法拯救海洋。除非全球碳排放得到削减、塑料垃圾得到妥善管理，否则新种植的珊瑚仍将继续承受巨大压力。保护珊瑚礁归根结底需要将科学创新与坚定的政策行动结合起来，确保这些不可替代的海洋栖息地能够为后代继续保持生机。

quizzes.question: What happens when ocean water becomes too warm?

options.text: Coral reefs grow faster in underwater nurseries.
Corals lose the tiny algae that provide them with color and food.
Young fish leave coastal communities for deeper seas.
Plastic waste breaks down into harmful chemicals.

quizzes.explanation:
答案：B
- 解析：细节理解题。第一段末句指出，当水温过高时，“corals expel the microscopic algae that give them both color and nutrients”，即珊瑚排出赋予其颜色和养分的微藻，导致白化。B 项正确。

stage_label: 第二阶段 · 过渡衔接期
title: Social Media and Consumerism（社交媒体与消费主义）
body:
Scrolling through a social media feed today often feels less like catching up with friends and more like walking through an endless digital shopping mall. Between short cooking clips and travel photos, users are constantly presented with curated product recommendations, limited-time discounts, and subtle sponsorships. Over the past decade, social platforms have reshaped not only how we communicate, but also how we desire and purchase goods.

Much of this shift is driven by influencer marketing and sophisticated recommendation algorithms. Unlike traditional television commercials, which viewers could easily recognize as advertisements, online content often blurs the line between genuine personal advice and paid promotion. When a relatable creator shares a skincare routine or an aesthetic desk setup, followers may feel as though they are receiving a tip from a trusted friend. Meanwhile, algorithms track every pause, click, and search, ensuring that similar items quickly appear across multiple apps.

This seamless integration of entertainment and commerce has encouraged impulse buying, particularly among younger consumers. Because purchases can be completed in seconds through embedded links and mobile wallets, the natural pause for reflection is largely removed. As a result, people frequently buy trendy items that are soon forgotten in a drawer, contributing to both personal financial stress and growing environmental waste.

Nevertheless, consumers are not entirely powerless in this digital marketplace. A growing number of users are practicing "de-influencing," a trend in which creators openly discuss products that are overpriced or unnecessary. At the same time, media literacy programs are helping young people recognize persuasive marketing tactics before they tap the checkout button. While social media will likely remain a powerful engine of modern consumerism, conscious habits—such as waiting 48 hours before making a non-essential purchase—can help individuals regain control over their spending.

素养；读写能力（media literacy 媒介素养）
