stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 人口出生率下降与社会福利制度转型 (Demographic Shifts and Welfare)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
Across much of East Asia and Europe, the demographic pyramid that sustained twentieth-century welfare states is quietly inverting. Falling fertility rates, combined with rising life expectancy, have shrunk the ratio of working-age taxpayers to retirees at a pace few postwar planners anticipated. In countries from South Korea to Italy, total fertility has plunged well below the replacement threshold of 2.1 children per woman, transforming what was once an abstract actuarial projection into an urgent fiscal reckoning.

Most public pension and healthcare systems still operate on a pay-as-you-go basis, wherein current workers finance the benefits of today's elderly under an implicit intergenerational compact. So long as cohorts of young entrants outnumbered pensioners, that arrangement appeared effortlessly solvent. Today, however, shrinking labor forces strain public budgets from both ends: tax bases contract even as age-related outlays for chronic care and long-term support climb relentlessly. Left unreformed, existing entitlements threaten either to crowd out productive public investment in education and infrastructure or to impose punitive payroll taxes on an ever-smaller pool of young earners.

Policy responses have thus far struggled against political gravity. Raising the statutory retirement age—arguably the most straightforward fiscal lever—repeatedly provokes fierce street protests and electoral backlash, particularly among manual laborers whose health declines earlier than that of white-collar professionals. Meanwhile, pronatalist cash transfers, subsidized childcare, and generous parental leave have yielded only modest, often temporary bumps in birth rates, suggesting that delayed family formation reflects deeper structural barriers: unaffordable urban housing, precarious early-career employment, and persistent gender imbalances in unpaid domestic work.

Consequently, a growing chorus of demographers urges societies to adapt to longevity rather than pinning fiscal salvation on an improbable baby boom. Adapting does not mean dismantling social safety nets; rather, it entails redesigning them for a century-long life course. Shifting toward partially funded pension accounts, indexing retirement ages transparently to gains in healthy life expectancy, and investing in lifelong retraining can keep older workers engaged without penalizing physical strain. Similarly, community-based preventive healthcare can compress late-life morbidity, curbing skyrocketing hospital expenses before chronic illness turns debilitating. Above all, boosting total factor productivity through automation and broader labor participation—including welcoming skilled migrants where politically feasible—offers a more durable cushion than demographics alone. Unless welfare institutions evolve alongside the populations they serve, the social contract risks fraying along generational lines.

契约；协议（考研熟词僻义：作形容词表“紧凑的”，作名词可指“契约/协议”）
有偿付能力的；不欠债的（熟词僻义：化学中指“溶剂”，经济金融语境指“有偿债能力的”）
挤出；排挤（经济学中指公共支出或福利挤压其他投资）
不稳定的；朝不保夕的（考研阅读高频词）
磨损；破裂；变得紧张（喻指社会契约出现裂痕）

translation:
在东亚和欧洲的大部分地区，曾经支撑起二十世纪福利国家的“人口金字塔”正悄然倒置。生育率的下降与预期寿命的延长相互叠加，使劳动年龄纳税人与退休人员的比例以战后规划者几乎未曾预料的速度急剧萎缩。从韩国到意大利，总和生育率已大幅跌破每名女性生育 2.1 个孩子的更替门槛，将昔日抽象的精算预测变成了迫在眉睫的财政清算。

大多数公共养老金与医疗体系至今仍以“现收现付制”运转，即在一种隐含的代际契约下，由在职劳动者供养当代老年人的福利。只要年轻入职人群的数量持续超过退休人员，这种安排看起来便能毫不费力地维持偿付能力。然而如今，萎缩的劳动力正从两端挤压公共预算：税基不断收缩，而用于慢性病护理和长期照护的涉老支出却节节攀升。若不加改革，现有的福利权益要么会挤占教育和基础设施等生产性公共投资，要么将对日益减少的年轻工薪阶层征收近乎惩罚性的工资税。

迄今为止，政策应对一直在与政治阻力苦苦搏斗。提高法定退休年龄——这或许是最直接的财政杠杆——屡屡引发激烈的街头抗议与选民反弹，在健康状况比白领更早走下坡路的体力劳动者群体中尤为如此。与此同时，鼓励生育的现金补贴、托育补助以及优厚的育儿假，在生育率上仅带来了幅度有限且往往短暂的回升，这表明推迟组建家庭反映的是更深层次的结构性障碍：难以负担的城市住房、不稳定的职业早期就业，以及无偿家务劳动中长期存在的性别失衡。

因此，越来越多的人口学家呼吁社会去适应长寿时代，而非将财政救赎寄托于一场不太可能出现的婴儿潮。适应并不意味着拆除社会安全网，而是围绕长达百岁的人生周期对其加以重塑。转向部分积累制养老金账户、将退休年龄与健康预期寿命的增长透明挂钩，以及投资终身再培训，能够在不惩罚体力消耗的前提下让年长劳动者继续参与工作。同样，以社区为基础的预防性医疗能够压缩生命晚期的患病期，在慢性病演变为致残重症之前遏制飙升的住院开支。最重要的是，通过自动化和扩大劳动力参与度——在政治可行的情况下也包括吸纳技术移民——来提升全要素生产率，能提供比单纯依靠人口规模更持久的缓冲。除非福利制度能够与其服务的人口结构同步演进，否则社会契约便可能沿着代际界线出现裂痕。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 合成生物学在医药领域的应用前景 (Synthetic Biology in Medicine)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
For most of modern pharmacology, drug discovery resembled prospecting: researchers screened thousands of natural compounds or chemically synthesized molecules, hoping one would bind selectively to a biological target without causing unacceptable toxicity. Synthetic biology proposes a radically different paradigm. Rather than merely borrowing what evolution happened to produce, scientists increasingly treat living cells as programmable chassis—modular platforms into which engineered genetic circuits can be installed to sense disease, manufacture therapeutics on site, and dismantle themselves once their task is complete.

Early clinical milestones have already moved beyond proof-of-concept. In oncology, engineered immune cells equipped with chimeric antigen receptors (CAR-T) can hunt down hematological malignancies that once resisted conventional chemotherapy. Next-generation designs go further, incorporating logic-gated switches that instruct modified T cells to activate only when two distinct tumor markers appear simultaneously, thereby sparing healthy tissue from collateral damage. Parallel breakthroughs are unfolding in the microbiome, where researchers rewire benign gut bacteria to detect inflammatory flares or secrete missing metabolic enzymes directly inside the digestive tract.

Equally transformative is synthetic biology's potential to compress drug manufacturing bottlenecks. Traditional biologics—monoclonal antibodies or complex vaccines—depend on delicate mammalian cell cultures housed in sprawling, capital-intensive bioreactors. By refactoring biosynthetic pathways into fast-growing yeast or cell-free transcription systems, laboratories can synthesize rare plant-derived compounds, such as antimalarial precursors or painkillers, in days rather than seasons, insulating supply from agricultural volatility.

Yet turning cellular programming into routine medicine confronts formidable hurdles. Biological systems are notoriously noisy: engineered circuits that behave predictably in pristine petri dishes often drift, mutate, or falter inside the turbulent microenvironment of a human organ. Moreover, living therapies pose novel regulatory dilemmas. How should agencies evaluate a treatment capable of reproducing inside a patient or transferring genetic payloads to neighboring microbes? Biosafety mechanisms such as genetic "kill switches" offer partial reassurance, though evolution remains adept at bypassing human safeguards.

Even so, the convergence of automated DNA synthesis, CRISPR gene editing, and machine-learning protein design is steadily reducing the trial-and-error cost of biological engineering. Public-private consortia are also establishing standardized biofoundries that benchmark safety protocols and accelerate regulatory review for modular cell therapies. Should clinical safety keep pace with technical ingenuity, medicine may soon shift from administering static chemicals to deploying adaptive, living cures—ushering in an era where therapies respond dynamically to the shifting contours of disease.

底盘；框架（合成生物学中指可装载基因回路的“底盘细胞”）

重构（借自软件工程术语，指重新设计生物合成路径）

纯净的；未受污染的；原始完美的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Rather than merely borrowing what evolution happened to produce, scientists increasingly treat living cells as programmable chassis—modular platforms into which engineered genetic circuits can be installed to sense disease, manufacture therapeutics on site, and dismantle themselves once their task is complete.
sentences.main_clause: scientists increasingly treat living cells as programmable chassis。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：对比状语（含宾语从句）+ 破折号同位语 + 介词提前的定语从句 + 目的不定式并列 + 时间状语从句。
从句与修饰：what evolution happened to produce 作 borrowing 的宾语从句；破折号后 modular platforms 为 chassis 的同位语；into which engineered genetic circuits can be installed 为“介词+关系代词”引导的定语从句，修饰 platforms；不定式 to sense..., manufacture..., and dismantle... 三者并列作目的状语，末尾 once their task is complete 作时间状语从句。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Biological systems are notoriously noisy: engineered circuits that behave predictably in pristine petri dishes often drift, mutate, or falter inside the turbulent microenvironment of a human organ.
sentences.main_clause: 前半句 Biological systems are notoriously noisy；后半句 engineered circuits often drift, mutate, or falter。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：冒号引出具体阐释 + 嵌套定语从句。
从句与修饰：that behave predictably in pristine petri dishes 修饰先行词 engineered circuits，通过 pristine petri dishes（纯净培养皿）与 turbulent microenvironment（动荡微环境）的鲜明对比，解释何为生物系统的 noisy（高噪音/不确定性）。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Should clinical safety keep pace with technical ingenuity, medicine may soon shift from administering static chemicals to deploying adaptive, living cures.
sentences.main_clause: medicine may soon shift from... to...。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：倒装条件状语从句 + 动名词介词结构对比。
从句与修饰：Should clinical safety keep pace... 为省略 if 的虚拟/假设条件句倒装；shift from administering... to deploying... 中 to 为介词，故前后均接动名词短语，形成“静态化学药物”向“自适应活体疗法”范式转变的精准对照。

translation:
在现代药理学的绝大部分历史中，药物研发犹如找矿：研究人员筛选成千上万种天然化合物或化学合成分子，期盼其中一种能够选择性地结合生物靶点，同时不至于引发不可接受的毒性。合成生物学则提出了一种截然不同的范式。科学家不再仅仅借用自然演化碰巧留下的产物，而是日益将活细胞视为可编程的“底盘”——一种模块化平台，可以将人工设计的基因回路装载其中，使其能够感知疾病、就地制造治疗药物，并在任务完成后自行解体。

早期的临床里程碑已经超越了概念验证阶段。在肿瘤学领域，装有嵌合抗原受体（CAR-T）的工程化免疫细胞，能够精准追踪并消灭曾对传统化疗产生耐药性的血液恶性肿瘤。下一代设计走得更远，引入了逻辑门控开关，指示改造后的 T 细胞仅在两种不同的肿瘤标志物同时出现时才被激活，从而保护健康组织免受附带损伤。在微生物组领域，类似的突破也在同步展开，研究人员通过重编程无害的肠道细菌，使其直接在消化道内检测炎症发作或分泌缺失的代谢酶。

同样具有变革意义的是合成生物学压缩药物生产瓶颈的潜力。单克隆抗体或复杂疫苗等传统生物制剂，依赖于放置在庞大且资本密集型生物反应器中娇贵的哺乳动物细胞培养物。通过将生物合成路径重构到快速生长的酵母或无细胞转录系统中，实验室可以在数天而非数个季节内合成抗疟疾前体或镇痛剂等稀有植物源化合物，使供应链免受农业波动的冲击。

然而，将细胞编程转化为常规医疗手段仍面临严峻障碍。生物系统向来充满噪音：在纯净的培养皿中表现可预测的工程回路，一旦进入人体器官动荡的微环境中，往往会发生漂移、突变甚至失灵。此外，活体疗法也带来了全新的监管难题。监管机构应当如何评估一种能够在患者体内自我繁殖，或将基因载荷转移给邻近微生物的疗法？诸如基因“自毁开关”之类的生物安全机制虽能提供部分保障，但演化向来擅长绕过人类设下的防线。

即便如此，自动化 DNA 合成、CRISPR 基因编辑与机器学习蛋白质设计的融合，正稳步降低生物工程的试错成本。公私合作联盟也正在建立标准化的生物铸造厂，用以确立安全规程基准，并加快模块化细胞疗法的监管审批进程。倘若临床安全性能够跟上技术巧思的步伐，医学或许很快就会从施用静态化学物质，转向部署能够自我适应的“活体疗法”——开启一个治疗方案能够动态响应疾病变化轨迹的新时代。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 城市热岛效应与绿色基础设施投资 (Urban Heat Islands and Infrastructure)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
During summer heatwaves, metropolitan areas routinely record temperatures several degrees Celsius higher than surrounding rural landscapes—a phenomenon known as the urban heat island (UHI) effect. Conventional asphalt roads, dark rooftops, and heat-trapping concrete canyons absorb solar radiation throughout the afternoon and release it slowly after sunset, depriving cities of nocturnal cooling. As climate change lengthens and intensifies extreme heat events, this built-in thermal amplification is shifting from a seasonal nuisance into a lethal public-health hazard and an escalating drain on municipal power grids.

Historically, cities responded to rising temperatures primarily through mechanical cooling—expanding air-conditioning capacity to insulate indoor spaces. Yet air conditioning operates as a thermodynamic double-edged sword: while lowering indoor temperatures, exhaust units vent waste heat directly onto streetscapes, further warming outdoor air and penalizing residents who cannot afford continuous cooling. Moreover, peak electricity demand during heatwaves frequently pushes aging transmission networks to the brink of blackouts, precisely when vulnerable populations depend most heavily on uninterrupted power.

To break this vicious cycle, urban planners are increasingly championing "green infrastructure"—strategic investments in urban tree canopies, permeable pavements, vegetated roofs, and restored wetlands. Through evapotranspiration and direct shading, healthy street trees can lower surface temperatures by double digits while filtering particulate pollution and absorbing stormwater runoff. Cities such as Medellín and Singapore have demonstrated that interconnected "green corridors" can shave measurable degrees off ambient neighborhood heat without consuming megawatts of grid capacity.

Nevertheless, green infrastructure is no panacea, nor is its implementation frictionless. Mature tree canopies take decades to establish and demand sustained irrigation and maintenance—resources often lacking in cash-strapped municipalities during droughts. Worse still, cooling investments frequently reflect and reinforce existing socioeconomic divides. Low-income districts, which typically feature denser concrete and sparser parkland, often endure the harshest heat exposure yet receive the smallest share of ecological upgrades; conversely, poorly designed greening projects can trigger "climate gentrification," pricing out the very residents they were intended to protect.

Addressing urban heat therefore requires treating shade and vegetation as core civic infrastructure rather than decorative landscaping. Pairing green corridors with reflective "cool roofs," revised zoning codes, and targeted subsidies for underserved neighborhoods can deliver equitable thermal relief while reducing peak grid strain. Municipal bond markets and climate-adaptation funds are also beginning to price avoided hospitalizations and lower energy bills into long-term infrastructure appraisals. Only when cooling policy integrates ecological design with social equity will cities become genuinely habitable in a warming century.

可渗透的；透水的（permeable pavements 透水路面）

士绅化；高档化（指社区改造后地价飙升迫使原低收入居民搬离）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Conventional asphalt roads, dark rooftops, and heat-trapping concrete canyons absorb solar radiation throughout the afternoon and release it slowly after sunset, depriving cities of nocturnal cooling.

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Low-income districts, which typically feature denser concrete and sparser parkland, often endure the harshest heat exposure yet receive the smallest share of ecological upgrades; conversely, poorly designed greening projects can trigger "climate gentrification," pricing out the very residents they were intended to protect.
sentences.main_clause: 前半句 Low-income districts often endure the harshest heat exposure yet receive the smallest share...；后半句 poorly designed greening projects can trigger "climate gentrification"。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：非限制性定语从句 + 转折并列谓语 + 分号对比 + 现在分词作结果状语 + 定语从句。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Only when cooling policy integrates ecological design with social equity will cities become genuinely habitable in a warming century.
sentences.main_clause: cities will become genuinely habitable（因 Only when... 置于句首，情态动词 will 提至主语 cities 之前）。

结构类型：Only + 状语从句 置于句首引起的主句部分倒装。

translation:
在夏季热浪期间，大都市区的气温通常会比周边的乡村地带高出数摄氏度——这一现象被称为“城市热岛效应”。传统的沥青道路、深色屋顶以及蓄热的混凝土峡谷在整个下午吸收太阳辐射，并在日落之后缓慢释放热量，从而剥夺了城市在夜间自然降温的机会。随着气候变化拉长并加剧极端高温事件，这种建筑自带的热放大效应正从季节性的烦扰演变为致命的公共健康危害，以及城市电网日益沉重的负担。

历史上，城市应对气温上升主要依赖机械制冷——即扩大空调装机容量以隔绝室内热浪。然而，空调实际上是一把热力学意义上的双刃剑：它在降低室内温度的同时，室外机将废热直接排入街道空间，进一步推高室外气温，并让那些无力承担持续制冷费用的居民雪上加霜。此外，热浪期间的用电高峰往往将老化的输电网络推向停电边缘，而这恰恰发生在脆弱人群最依赖不间断供电的时刻。

为了打破这一恶性循环，城市规划者正日益大力倡导“绿色基础设施”——对城市树冠、透水路面、植被屋顶以及修复后的湿地进行战略性投资。通过蒸散作用和直接遮阴，健康的街道树木能够将地表温度降低十余度，同时过滤颗粒物污染并吸纳暴雨径流。麦德林和新加坡等城市已经证明，相互连通的“绿色走廊”无需消耗电网的兆瓦电力，便能显著拉低社区的环境温度。

尽管如此，绿色基础设施既非万能灵药，其落地过程也绝非毫无阻力。成熟的树冠需要数十年才能长成，且需要持续的灌溉与养护——而在干旱时期，财政吃紧的市政当局往往缺乏此类资源。更糟糕的是，降温投资常常反映并强化既有的社会经济鸿沟。低收入社区通常混凝土更密集、公园绿地更稀少，承受着最严酷的高温暴露，却往往获得最少份额的生态升级；反过来，设计不当的绿化项目还可能引发“气候士绅化”，通过抬高生活成本，把它们原本旨在保护的居民挤出社区。

因此，应对城市高温需要将树荫与植被视为核心市政基础设施，而非装饰性的景观美化。将绿色走廊与高反射率的“凉爽屋顶”、修订后的分区规划法规以及面向弱势社区的精准补贴相结合，既能实现公平的降温效果，又能缓解电网高峰负荷。市政债券市场与气候适应基金也已开始将由此避免的住院费用和节省的能源账单纳入长期基础设施评估之中。唯有当降温政策将生态设计与社会公平融为一体时，城市才能在日益变暖的本世纪真正保持宜居。

quizzes.question: Why does the author call air conditioning a 'thermodynamic double-edged sword' (Paragraph 2)?

options.text: It cools indoor spaces while worsening outdoor heat and straining power grids.
It consumes excessive water resources that are urgently needed for street trees.
It fails to lower indoor temperatures during periods of high urban humidity.
It discourages municipal governments from building affordable housing.

quizzes.explanation: 细节与修辞理解题。第二段紧接着冒号给出解释：空调在降低室内温度的同时，向街道排出废热（vent waste heat directly onto streetscapes）进一步加热室外空气，且高峰用电将电网推向断电边缘。因此 A 项准确概括了“双刃剑”的两面。

quizzes.question: What concern is raised about poorly designed greening projects in Paragraph 4?

options.text: They increase stormwater runoff in densely paved concrete areas.
They may drive up living costs and displace disadvantaged residents.
They attract invasive insects that damage aging transmission lines.
They consume more electricity than conventional cooling systems.

quizzes.explanation: 细节定位题。第四段末句明确指出，设计不良的绿化项目可能触发 climate gentrification（气候士绅化），从而 pricing out the very residents they were intended to protect（因价格上涨把原本要保护的居民挤出去），对应 B 项。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 认知偏差：确认偏误如何影响判断 (Confirmation Bias)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
Human beings pride themselves on acting as dispassionate seekers of truth, weighing evidence before arriving at reasoned conclusions. Cognitive science, however, paints a less flattering portrait. Far from operating like impartial judges, human minds frequently behave like skilled defense attorneys, recruiting facts selectively to acquit beliefs they already hold. This deep-seated tendency—known as confirmation bias—shapes everything from casual political arguments to high-stakes medical diagnoses and financial investments.

Confirmation bias operates through three interlocking mechanisms: selective search, biased interpretation, and asymmetric recall. When investigating a hypothesis, people gravitate toward sources likely to affirm their priors while steering clear of disconfirming data. Even when confronted with identical, ambiguous evidence, opposing camps routinely extract opposite lessons, scrutinizing hostile findings for methodological flaws while accepting congenial studies at face value. Over time, memory itself acts as a partisan filter, preserving anecdotes that vindicate our worldview while letting inconvenient counterexamples slip quietly from consciousness.

Crucially, this cognitive distortion is not simply a hallmark of ignorance. Empirical research reveals that individuals with higher analytical ability and greater domain knowledge are often just as susceptible to confirmation bias—and sometimes more so—because intellectual sophistication equips them with sharper tools to rationalize favored narratives. Rather than correcting error, raw intelligence can inadvertently fortify ideological trenches, a phenomenon psychologists term "motivated reasoning."

Why would evolution bequeath us a mental shortcut so hostile to objective accuracy? One influential theory posits that human reasoning evolved less to discover solitary truths than to win arguments and signal tribal loyalty within cooperative groups. In ancestral environments, maintaining social standing among allies often mattered more for survival than holding flawlessly calibrated beliefs about distant phenomena. What once served social cohesion, however, grows hazardous in complex modern institutions where flawed risk assessments carry systemic consequences—such as intelligence agencies dismissing warning signs before geopolitical crises, or investors ignoring early indicators of asset bubbles.

Overcoming confirmation bias demands structural countermeasures rather than mere willpower. Because individuals are notoriously blind to their own blind spots, effective decision-making relies on institutionalized dissent: pre-mortem exercises that ask teams to imagine why a favored plan failed, blind peer review in science, and adversarial "red teams" tasked with challenging consensus assumptions. Equally vital is cultivating intellectual humility—training analysts and citizens alike to treat updated beliefs as signs of rigor rather than betrayal. Only by designing environments that reward falsification can human judgment edge closer to genuine objectivity.

宣判……无罪（文中喻指大脑像辩护律师一样为既有信念开脱）
相互关联的；环环相扣的
合意的；投合心意的（congenial studies 指符合自身观点的研究）
遗留；传给（进化心理学语境中指演化“赋予”人类某种特征）
对抗性的；提出反对意见的

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Even when confronted with identical, ambiguous evidence, opposing camps routinely extract opposite lessons, scrutinizing hostile findings for methodological flaws while accepting congenial studies at face value.
sentences.main_clause: opposing camps routinely extract opposite lessons。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：让步状语从句省略 + 主句 + 双重现在分词伴随对比结构。
从句与修饰：Even when confronted with... 省略了 they are；主句后的 scrutinizing... while accepting... 通过 while 构成鲜明的对称对比，精准描摹了“严以律敌、宽以待己”的双重标准（at face value 意为“按表面价值全盘接受”）。

sentences.label: 句子 2

sentences.grammar:
结构类型：宾语从句（含插入比较） + 原因状语从句。
从句与修饰：宾语从句内部插入 —and sometimes more so—（有时甚至更甚）作为程度递进；because 引导的原因状语从句解释了看似反常的现象：智力越强，为既定立场自圆其说（rationalize）的武器反而越锋利。

结构类型：Only + 介词短语 置于句首引发的部分倒装 + 定语从句。
从句与修饰：that reward falsification 为定语从句，修饰 environments，其中 falsification（证伪）点出了科学哲学与批判性思维的核心原则。

translation:
人类素以自己是冷静客观的真理追寻者而自豪，在得出理性结论之前会审慎权衡证据。然而，认知科学却描绘了一幅远没那么讨喜的图景。人类大脑非但不像公正的法官那样运作，反而常常表现得像老练的辩护律师，有选择地征集事实，只为给早已持有的信念开脱罪责。这种根深蒂固的倾向——即“确认偏误”——塑造了从日常政治争论到高风险医疗诊断及金融投资的一切判断。

确认偏误通过三种环环相扣的机制发挥作用：选择性搜寻、偏颇性解读以及不对称回忆。在检验某个假设时，人们倾向于寻找可能印证既有观点的信源，同时避开与之相悖的数据。即便面对完全相同且模棱两可的证据，对立阵营也常常从中提炼出截然相反的教训：他们会拿着放大镜挑剔敌对结论的方法论漏洞，却对合乎己意的研究全盘照收。假以时日，记忆本身也会充当党派过滤器，留存那些印证我们世界观的轶事，而任由令人不适的反例悄然滑出意识之外。

至关重要的是，这种认知扭曲并不仅仅是无知的标志。实证研究表明，分析能力更强、专业知识更丰富的人，往往同样容易陷入确认偏误——有时甚至陷得更深——因为智力上的老练为他们配备了更锋利的工具，去为偏爱的叙事自圆其说。纯粹的聪明不仅未能纠错，反而可能在无意中加固意识形态的战壕，心理学家将这一现象称为“动机性推理”。

为什么演化会留给我们一种如此敌视客观准确性的心理捷径？一种颇具影响力的理论认为，人类推理能力在演化上的初衷，与其说是为了发现孤立的真理，不如说是为了在协作群体中赢得争论并释放部落忠诚信号。在远古环境中，在盟友中维持社会地位对生存的重要性，往往高于对遥远现象持有精准校准的信念。然而，这种曾经服务于社会凝聚力的机制，在错误的评估会带来系统性后果的复杂现代机构中却变得危险重重——例如情报机构在地缘危机前夕对预警信号视而不见，或投资者无视资产泡沫的早期征兆。

克服确认偏误需要的是制度性对策，而非单凭个人意志力。由于个体对自己思维盲点的察觉向来迟钝，有效的决策依赖于制度化的异议机制：例如要求团队设想一个备受青睐的计划为何会失败的“事前验尸”演练、科学界的盲审制度，以及专门负责挑战共识假设的对抗性“红队”。同样重要的是培养智力谦逊——训练分析人员与普通公民将修正既有信念视为严谨求真的体现，而非对立场的背叛。唯有设计出奖励“证伪”的环境，人类的判断才能向真正的客观性更近一步。

quizzes.question: Why might highly intelligent individuals be even more prone to confirmation bias?

options.text: They rarely encounter ambiguous evidence in their professional domains.
They are better at constructing plausible justifications for their existing beliefs.
They rely more heavily on partisan memory than on empirical data.
They tend to ignore warning signs of systemic institutional failures.

quizzes.explanation: 细节定位题。第三段明确解释：分析能力强和知识丰富的人有时更容易产生确认偏误，因为 intellectual sophistication equips them with sharper tools to rationalize favored narratives（智力上的老练使他们拥有更锐利的工具来合理化偏爱的叙事），对应 B 项。

quizzes.question: According to the evolutionary explanation in Paragraph 4, confirmation bias originally helped humans to ______.

options.text: predict distant environmental hazards more accurately
strengthen group cohesion and social standing among allies
avoid costly arguments within ancestral cooperative tribes
build complex institutions resistant to systemic crises

quizzes.explanation: 细节题。第四段指出推理演化的目的在于 win arguments and signal tribal loyalty（赢得争论并释放忠诚信号），维持在盟友中的社会地位，并总结为 What once served social cohesion，对应 B 项。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 博物馆文物归还的法律与道德博弈 (Repatriation of Cultural Artifacts)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
Walk through the grand galleries of London, Paris, or New York, and you encounter a paradox carved in stone and bronze: institutions celebrating human civilization's shared heritage are filled with treasures acquired during eras of colonial domination. For generations, Western "encyclopedic museums" defended their custodianship on universalist grounds, contending that centralizing artifacts in well-funded metropolitan capitals made world history accessible to global audiences and safeguarded fragile relics from neglect. Over the past decade, however, escalating demands from formerly colonized nations have forced a reckoning over who rightfully owns the material past.

Legally, the terrain remains stubbornly tilted toward incumbent holders. The landmark 1970 UNESCO Convention prohibits the illicit trafficking of cultural property, yet it is non-retroactive, leaving artifacts removed during nineteenth-century imperial expeditions or punitive military raids beyond its formal reach. Compounding this legal vacuum, flagship institutions such as the British Museum operate under national statutes that explicitly bar trustees from permanently deaccessioning collection items, turning moral restitution into a parliamentary hurdle rather than a curatorial choice.

Proponents of retaining disputed works warn that wholesale repatriation could empty major museums, fracturing comparative displays that allow scholars and visitors to trace cross-cultural exchange side by side. They also raise pragmatic anxieties about conservation standards and political instability in certain countries of origin. Yet critics dismiss these objections as paternalistic relics of imperial arrogance. Keeping looted artifacts on display so distant tourists can admire them, they argue, perpetuates historical dispossession while denying local communities the chance to reconnect with vital symbols of identity and memory.

Significantly, the stalemate has begun to thaw through pragmatic compromise rather than sweeping legal verdicts. Several European museums and universities have voluntarily returned Benin Bronzes to Nigeria, acknowledging that objects seized during the 1897 British punitive expedition were indisputably plundered. Meanwhile, newer frameworks explore creative alternatives to zero-sum ownership: long-term rotating loans, joint curatorship, digital repatriation through high-resolution 3D scans, and collaborative conservation funding.

The controversy over cultural restitution ultimately transcends museum floor plans. It tests whether Western institutions can relinquish unilateral authority over global heritage and negotiate with former colonies on equal footing. Provenance research—once relegated to dusty archives—now demands sustained funding and transparent public databases so source communities can trace displaced objects without years of opaque litigation. While no single formula fits every contested sculpture or manuscript, enduring legitimacy will belong not to those who hoard the past, but to those willing to share custody of its meaning.

非法的；违禁的（注意区分 elicit 引出）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Compounding this legal vacuum, flagship institutions such as the British Museum operate under national statutes that explicitly bar trustees from permanently deaccessioning collection items, turning moral restitution into a parliamentary hurdle rather than a curatorial choice.

sentences.grammar:

从句与修饰：Compounding this legal vacuum（使这一法律真空雪上加霜的是）修饰整个主句；that explicitly bar trustees from... 修饰 statutes；末尾 turning... into... 作结果状语，说明法定禁止注销藏品使归还问题升级为议会立法障碍（parliamentary hurdle），而非馆长所能决定的策展选择。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Keeping looted artifacts on display so distant tourists can admire them, they argue, perpetuates historical dispossession while denying local communities the chance to reconnect with vital symbols of identity and memory.

sentences.grammar:
结构类型：动名词短语作主语（含目的状语从句）+ 插入语 + 并列对比状语。
从句与修饰：they argue 为主谓插入语；so distant tourists can admire them 省略了 that，作目的状语；while denying local communities... 引导伴随对比，点出“远方游客欣赏”与“本土社群失落身份象征”之间的伦理失衡。

sentences.quote: While no single formula fits every contested sculpture or manuscript, enduring legitimacy will belong not to those who hoard the past, but to those willing to share custody of its meaning.

sentences.grammar:
结构类型：让步状语从句 + not... but... 对称结构 + 定语从句与形容词后置定语。
从句与修饰：While 引导让步状语从句（“尽管……”）；主句通过 not to those who hoard... 与 but to those willing to share... 形成鲜明的修辞对照，升华了全文关于文化共享与合法性的主旨。

translation:
漫步在伦敦、巴黎或纽约宏伟的博物馆展厅中，你会遭遇一种镌刻在石器与青铜上的悖论：那些旨在礼赞人类共同文明遗产的机构，内部却充斥着在殖民统治时期掠夺而来的珍宝。几代人以来，西方的“百科全书式博物馆”一直以普世主义为由为自身的保管权辩护，主张将文物集中存放在资金雄厚的大都市，既能让全球观众接触世界历史，也能保护脆弱的古物免遭疏于照料之苦。然而，过去十年间，前殖民地国家日益高涨的诉求，正迫使人们重新审视究竟谁才真正拥有这些物质化的过去。

在法律层面上，格局依然顽固地向现有持有方倾斜。具有里程碑意义的 1970 年联合国教科文组织公约禁止非法贩运文化财产，但该公约不具备溯及力，使得在十九世纪帝国远征或惩罚性军事突袭中被掠走的文物游离于其正式管辖之外。使这一法律真空雪上加霜的是，大英博物馆等旗舰机构受制于国家成文法，这些法律明文禁止受托人永久注销馆藏物品，从而将道德层面的文物归还变成了议会立法层面的障碍，而非单纯的策展选择。

主张保留争议文物的人士警告称，全面归还可能会掏空各大博物馆，割裂对比性展陈，而正是这种展陈让学者与游客得以并排追溯跨文化交流的脉络。他们还对部分原属国的保护水准及政治动荡表达了现实担忧。然而，批评者将这些反对意见斥为帝国傲慢残留下的家长式作风。他们认为，把被掠夺的文物继续陈列出来让远方游客赞叹，无异于延续历史上的剥夺行为，同时剥夺了当地社群重新连接自身身份与记忆重要象征的机会。

值得注意的是，这一僵局已开始通过务实的妥协而非一刀切的法律裁决逐渐破冰。多家欧洲博物馆和大学已自愿向尼日利亚归还贝宁青铜器，承认在 1897 年英国惩罚性远征中被夺走的器物无疑属于战利品掠夺。与此同时，更新的框架也在探索零和所有权之外的创造性替代方案：长期轮流借展、联合策展、通过高精度三维扫描实现的数字归还，以及合作提供文物保护资金。

围绕文化归还的争议最终超越了博物馆的展厅布局。它考验着西方机构能否放弃对全球遗产的单边权威，并与前殖民地国家在平等基础上展开谈判。曾被冷落在尘封档案库中的文物来源溯源研究，如今亟需持续资金与透明的公共数据库支撑，从而让原属地社群无需历经多年晦暗不明的诉讼，便能追踪流散文物的下落。尽管没有任何单一方案适用于每一件存在争议的雕塑或手稿，但持久的合法性终将不属于那些囤积历史的人，而属于那些愿意共同守护历史意义的人。

quizzes.question: According to Paragraph 2, why is the British Museum unable to easily return contested artifacts?

options.text: The 1970 UNESCO Convention explicitly permits nineteenth-century imperial acquisitions.
National laws legally forbid its trustees from permanently removing items from collections.
Its curators lack the diplomatic channels to negotiate with former colonies.
The countries of origin have refused to sign digital repatriation agreements.

quizzes.explanation: 细节定位题。第二段第二句指出，如大英博物馆等旗舰机构受制于国家法律（national statutes），明文禁止受托人永久注销馆藏（bar trustees from permanently deaccessioning collection items），因此必须经由议会层面突破，对应 B 项。

quizzes.question: What recent shift in handling cultural restitution is highlighted in Paragraph 4?

options.text: International courts have issued sweeping mandates ordering immediate returns.
Western universities have stopped acquiring any historical artifacts from abroad.
Flexible compromises and voluntary returns are gradually breaking the deadlock.
High-resolution 3D scans have completely replaced physical ownership disputes.

quizzes.explanation: 段落主旨题。第四段首句指出僵局正通过 pragmatic compromise rather than sweeping legal verdicts 逐渐破冰，举例包括自愿归还贝宁青铜器，以及轮流借展、联合策展、数字归还等灵活方案，对应 C 项。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 零工经济中的劳动者权益保护 (Gig Economy and Labor Rights)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
Over the past decade, digital labor platforms have reimagined how work is organized, connecting riders, drivers, and freelance specialists with customers through smartphone algorithms. Supporters celebrate the gig economy as an engine of opportunity: with minimal barriers to entry, workers gain unprecedented flexibility to log on between classes, caregiving duties, or second jobs, while consumers enjoy rapid delivery at depressed prices. Yet beneath this frictionless interface lies an intensifying clash over whether app-based workers represent genuine micro-entrepreneurs or misclassified employees stripped of basic protections.

At the heart of the dispute sits a century-old legal binary. Traditional labor law distinguishes sharply between full-time employees—entitled to minimum wages, paid leave, and collective bargaining—and independent contractors, who trade statutory security for commercial autonomy. Platforms insist their workers fall squarely into the latter camp because they choose when to work and supply their own vehicles or devices. Labor advocates counter that algorithmic management renders such autonomy largely illusory. When software dictates prices, penalizes declined tasks, and monitors real-time performance through opaque rating systems, platforms exercise far tighter control than typical clients ever exert over true freelancers.

Regulatory experiments have produced uneven results. Attempts in California and parts of Europe to reclassify gig workers wholesale as formal employees triggered fierce corporate lobbying and fears that rigid scheduling rules might force platforms to slash flexible shifts or exit smaller markets altogether. Conversely, carving out a "third category" of dependent contractors—offering modest benefits without full employment status—has drawn criticism from unions, who warn that a diluted tier risks eroding hard-won labor standards across broader service industries. Worse still, protracted litigation leaves couriers and drivers absorbing medical bills and income shocks while courts debate definitions.

Rather than forcing twentieth-century boxes onto twenty-first-century work, a growing number of policymakers advocate portable, universal benefits decoupled from a single employer. Under such models, every hour worked on a platform triggers proportional contributions into personal accounts covering health insurance, injury protection, and retirement savings, regardless of how many apps a worker uses. Paired with algorithmic transparency—granting workers the right to inspect how pay rates and deactivation decisions are calculated—and accessible dispute-resolution channels, portable safeguards could preserve genuine scheduling freedom without subsidizing precariousness. Ultimately, whether digital capitalism achieves durable social legitimacy will hinge on proving that flexibility and dignity need not be mutually exclusive.

vocabulary.meaning: 二元对立；非此即彼的分类（legal binary 指法律上的二分法）
虚幻的；名不副实的（源自 illusion）
不透明的；晦涩难懂的（常形容算法或决策黑箱）
大规模地；全盘地（考研熟词僻义：除“批发”外，作副词/形容词常表“全面地、一刀切地”）
被稀释的；削弱的（a diluted tier 指缩水的保障层级）
可携带的；可跨平台转移的（portable benefits 可转移福利）
使脱钩；分离（decouple A from B）
停用；封号（零工平台常用“停用账号”代替解雇）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Yet beneath this frictionless interface lies an intensifying clash over whether app-based workers represent genuine micro-entrepreneurs or misclassified employees stripped of basic protections.
sentences.main_clause: an intensifying clash lies beneath this frictionless interface（因地点状语 beneath... 置于句首且主语为名词短语，发生完全倒装）。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：地点状语前置引起完全倒装 + whether... or... 介词宾语从句 + 过去分词后置定语。
从句与修饰：over 后接 whether... or... 引导的宾语从句；stripped of basic protections 为过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 employees，精准点出零工劳动者身份界定的核心争议。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When software dictates prices, penalizes declined tasks, and monitors real-time performance through opaque rating systems, platforms exercise far tighter control than typical clients ever exert over true freelancers.
sentences.main_clause: platforms exercise far tighter control than typical clients ever exert over true freelancers。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：时间/条件状语从句（三动词并列） + 比较状语从句。
从句与修饰：When 从句内用 dictates..., penalizes..., and monitors... 三个并列谓语揭露“算法控制”的实质；主句比较级结构直指平台控制的强度远超普通客户对自由职业者的约束，以此反驳平台自称“仅仅是撮合中介”的说辞。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Whether digital capitalism achieves durable social legitimacy will hinge on proving that flexibility and dignity need not be mutually exclusive.
sentences.main_clause: [Whether-clause] will hinge on proving [that-clause]。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：Whether 引导的主语从句 + 动名词作介词宾语 + 宾语从句。
从句与修饰：句首 Whether... legitimacy 整体作主语（注意此时不可用 if 替换）；hinge on 后接动名词 proving，其宾语从句点出全文立意核心——灵活性与劳动尊严并非非此即彼、相互排斥。

translation:
过去十年间，数字劳动平台重塑了工作的组织方式，通过智能手机算法将骑手、司机与自由职业专才同客户连接在一起。支持者将零工经济盛赞为机遇引擎：凭借极低的准入门槛，劳动者获得了前所未有的灵活性，得以在课程、育儿照护或第二份工作的间隙上线接单，而消费者则享受到了价格低廉的快捷配送服务。然而，在这层顺畅无阻的界面之下，一场愈演愈烈的冲突正在上演：依托应用接单的劳动者究竟是名副其实的微型创业者，还是被错误归类、遭剥夺基本保障的雇员？

这场争端的核心在于一套延续了百年的法律二元划分。传统劳动法在全职雇员与独立承包商之间划出了一条泾渭分明的界线：前者有权享有最低工资、带薪休假与集体谈判权，而后者则以法定的职业保障来换取商业自主权。平台坚称其劳动者完全属于后一类，理由是他们可以自主选择工作时间并自备车辆或设备。但劳工权益倡导者反驳称，算法管理使这种自主权在很大程度上沦为幻象。当软件单方面决定价格、对拒单行为施加惩罚，并通过不透明的评分系统实时监控表现时，平台所施加的控制远比普通客户对真正自由职业者的约束要严苛得多。

各地的监管实验迄今结果参差不齐。加州及欧洲部分地区试图将零工劳动者全盘重新归类为正式雇员，此举不仅招致企业界猛烈游说，也引发担忧：僵化的排班规则可能迫使平台大幅削减弹性班次，甚至彻底退出较小市场。反过来，专门开辟“依赖型承包商”这一“第三类别”——即在不赋予完全雇员身份的前提下提供有限福利——又遭到工会批评，工会警告称，这种缩水的保障层级可能会侵蚀更广泛服务行业历尽艰辛才争取到的劳动标准。更糟糕的是，旷日持久的诉讼让外卖员与网约车司机不得不在法庭争论法律定义的同时，自行承担医疗账单与收入冲击。

与其将二十世纪的条条框框硬套在二十一世纪的工作形态之上，越来越多的政策制定者开始倡导与单一雇主脱钩的、可携带的普惠型福利。在此类模式下，劳动者在平台上工作的每一小时都会触发按比例向个人账户的缴费，无论其同时使用多少个应用程序，资金均可用于医疗保险、工伤保障及养老储蓄。若再辅以算法透明度——赋予劳动者查看报酬计算方式及账号停用决定的权利——以及便捷的争议解决渠道，可携带的保障机制既能保留真正的排班自由，又不至于变相补贴不稳定性。归根结底，数字资本主义能否赢得持久的社会合法性，将取决于它能否证明灵活性与尊严并非水火不容。

quizzes.question: Why do labor advocates argue that gig workers' autonomy is 'largely illusory' (Paragraph 2)?

options.text: Workers are legally required to purchase vehicles directly from platform companies.
Algorithms tightly regulate pricing, task acceptance, and performance evaluation.
Most gig workers spend all their earnings paying off minimum-wage deductions.
Consumers routinely force delivery riders to accept unfavorable working hours.

quizzes.explanation: 因果细节题。第二段紧接着 illusory 解释道：软件决定价格、惩罚拒单、通过不透明评分监控表现（dictates prices, penalizes declined tasks, and monitors real-time performance），即平台通过算法施加了严密控制，对应 B 项。

quizzes.question: According to Paragraph 4, 'portable, universal benefits' are designed to ______.

options.text: force digital platforms to convert all contractors into salaried employees
replace traditional health insurance with algorithmic performance bonuses
tie social protections to hours worked across platforms rather than one employer
eliminate rating systems so workers cannot be deactivated by algorithms

quizzes.explanation: 细节理解题。第四段指出可携带福利与单一雇主脱钩（decoupled from a single employer），无论使用多少个 app，每工作一小时都会按比例向涵盖医保、工伤和养老的个人账户缴费，对应 C 项。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 太空资源开采的国际法空白 (Space Mining and International Law)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
As rocket launch costs plummet and autonomous robotics mature, harvesting platinum-group metals from near-Earth asteroids or extracting water ice from lunar craters is migrating from speculative fiction into corporate business plans. Proponents envision orbital refueling depots powered by lunar propellant and terrestrial clean-tech industries freed from environmentally destructive rare-earth mining. Yet this technological acceleration is outpacing the legal architecture meant to govern the cosmos, exposing an unsettling ambiguity at the heart of international space law.

The foundational charter, the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, declares celestial bodies the "province of all mankind" and explicitly forbids nations from asserting territorial sovereignty over the Moon or asteroids through claim, occupation, or any other means. Drafted during the Cold War primarily to forestall orbital nuclear proliferation and colonial land grabs, the treaty was silent on a decisive commercial question: if no state may own an asteroid, may a private company nonetheless extract, refine, and sell its minerals for profit?

Major spacefaring powers have rushed to fill that silence unilaterally. In 2015, the United States enacted legislation affirming citizens' property rights over extracted space resources, a precedent soon echoed by Luxembourg, the United Arab Emirates, and Japan. Supporters contend that without secure title to mined materials, no investor will finance multi-billion-dollar ventures carrying immense technical risk. Critics, particularly among developing nations, retort that domestic laws cannot legitimize the enclosure of a global common. When a handful of wealthy states grant themselves permission to mine scarce lunar sites—such as permanently shadowed polar craters rich in water ice—they effectively establish de facto monopoly control without firing a shot or planting a sovereign flag.

Attempts to forge consensus have foundered on geopolitical rivalry. The 1979 Moon Agreement, which sought to classify space minerals as the "common heritage of mankind" subject to an international redistribution regime, was shunned by every major spacefaring nation. More recently, competing coalitions—led respectively by Washington's Artemis Accords and Sino-Russian lunar initiatives—have offered divergent interpretations of "safety zones" and resource sharing, raising the specter of fragmented rules and orbital friction.

Without an updated multilateral framework, humanity risks repeating the tragedy of maritime overexploitation on a celestial scale. Establishing transparent registration, environmental impact protocols, and equitable benefit-sharing mechanisms need not stifle commercial pioneers; rather, clear global rules offer the only durable shield against future resource conflicts beyond Earth.

vocabulary.meaning: 暴跌；急剧下降（考研外刊高频上升/下降类动词）
地球上的；陆地的（与 celestial 天体的相对）
圈占；围封（原指英国“圈地运动”，文中指将全球公域私有化圈占）
事实上的（拉丁语借词，与 de jure 法律上的相对）
失败；沉没；触礁（考研高频熟词僻义：作名词指“创始人”，作动词表“计划/谈判失败或船只沉没”）
幽灵；挥之不去的阴影/威胁

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: Drafted during the Cold War primarily to forestall orbital nuclear proliferation and colonial land grabs, the treaty was silent on a decisive commercial question: if no state may own an asteroid, may a private company nonetheless extract, refine, and sell its minerals for profit?
sentences.main_clause: the treaty was silent on a decisive commercial question。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：过去分词短语作时间/背景状语 + 冒号引出设问式同位语（内含条件状语从句）。
从句与修饰：Drafted during the Cold War... 的逻辑主语是 the treaty（被动关系）；冒号后的问句具体阐释了 question 的内容，用 if no state may... 与 may a private company nonetheless... 构成尖锐的法理张力（国家不得占有主权 vs. 私企能否占有矿产）。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: When a handful of wealthy states grant themselves permission to mine scarce lunar sites—such as permanently shadowed polar craters rich in water ice—they effectively establish de facto monopoly control without firing a shot or planting a sovereign flag.
sentences.main_clause: they effectively establish de facto monopoly control。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：时间/条件状语从句 + 双破折号举例插入语 + 方式状语。
从句与修饰：双破折号内列举 permanently shadowed polar craters（永久阴影极地陨石坑），其中 rich in water ice 为形容词短语作后置定语；句末 without firing a shot or planting a sovereign flag 以具象画面说明“无需宣示主权即可形成事实垄断”。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: The 1979 Moon Agreement, which sought to classify space minerals as the "common heritage of mankind" subject to an international redistribution regime, was shunned by every major spacefaring nation.
sentences.main_clause: The 1979 Moon Agreement was shunned by every major spacefaring nation。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：非限制性定语从句 + 形容词短语作后置定语 + 被动语态。
从句与修饰：which sought to classify... 修饰 Moon Agreement；其中 subject to an international redistribution regime 为形容词短语作后置定语，修饰 minerals 或 heritage，表明该协定受制于国际再分配机制，这也是航天大国对其避而远之的根本原因。

translation:
随着火箭发射成本暴跌以及自主机器人技术的日臻成熟，从近地小行星开采铂族金属或从月球陨石坑提取水冰，正从科幻猜想步入企业商业计划书。支持者描绘了由月球推进剂供能的轨道加注站，以及摆脱破坏环境的地面稀土开采的清洁科技产业。然而，这种技术加速正在甩开本应规范宇宙秩序的法律架构，暴露出国际空间法核心地带令人不安的模糊性。

作为奠基性宪章的 1967 年《外层空间条约》宣布天体属于“全人类共同探索和利用的领域”，并明确禁止任何国家通过主张、占领或任何其他方式对月球或小行星宣示领土主权。该条约起草于冷战时期，初衷主要是防范轨道核扩散与殖民式的跑马圈地，却在一个决定性的商业问题上保持了沉默：既然任何国家都不得拥有小行星，那么私营企业是否仍可开采、提炼并出售其矿物以牟利？

主要航天大国已争相单方面填补这一法律沉默。2015 年，美国颁布立法确认公民对所开采太空资源拥有财产权，这一先例很快得到卢森堡、阿联酋和日本的效仿。支持者认为，若没有对所采矿产的稳固产权，就没有投资者愿意为一个背负巨大技术风险、耗资数十亿美元的项目出资。但批评者——尤其是发展中国家——反驳称，国内法无法使“圈占全球公域”的行为合法化。当少数富裕国家自行批准去开采稀缺的月球点位（例如富含水冰的极地永久阴影陨石坑）时，它们实际上无需一枪一弹、也无需插上主权旗帜，便确立了事实上的垄断控制。

凝聚全球共识的努力却在地缘政治竞争中频频触礁。1979 年的《月球协定》试图将太空矿产界定为受国际再分配机制约束的“人类共同继承财产”，结果遭到所有主要航天大国的冷落。近年来，分别以美国主导的《阿尔忒弥斯协定》与中俄月球合作倡议为代表的竞争性联盟，对“安全区”和资源共享提出了大相径庭的解读，令规则碎片化与轨道摩擦的阴影再度浮现。

若缺乏更新的多边框架，人类恐将在天体尺度上重演海洋过度开发的悲剧。建立透明的登记制度、环境影响评估规程以及公平的利益共享机制，未必会扼杀商业先驱；相反，清晰的全球规则正是防范地球之外未来资源冲突的唯一持久盾牌。

quizzes.question: What is the fundamental ambiguity in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty?

options.text: It bans orbital nuclear weapons but permits military bases on asteroids.
It bars national sovereignty over celestial bodies without clarifying private mining rights.
It grants exclusive mineral rights to countries capable of autonomous robotics.
It requires developing nations to fund international conservation programs.

quizzes.explanation: 细节定位题。第二段明确指出 1967 年条约禁止国家对月球或小行星宣示主权（forbids nations from asserting territorial sovereignty），却对私营企业能否开采并出售矿产盈利保持沉默（silent on a decisive commercial question），对应 B 项。

quizzes.question: Why do critics object to national space-mining legislation such as the 2015 U.S. law?

options.text: Such laws violate domestic constitutional rules on private property.
They discourage private investors from funding costly orbital refueling depots.
They enable wealthy nations to monopolize scarce lunar resources unilaterally.
They force spacefaring powers to share proprietary technology with rivals.

quizzes.explanation: 细节推理题。第三段指出批评者认为国内法不能让圈占全球公域合法化，少数富裕国家批准自己开采稀缺月球点位实际上确立了事实上的垄断控制（de facto monopoly control），对应 C 项。

stage_label: 第三阶段 · 考研对标期
title: 技术乐观主义与人类能动性的边界 (Technological Optimism and Human Agency)
difficulty: 第三阶段 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐（考研英语一/二真题难度 · CEFR B2+–C1）
body:
In Silicon Valley's prevailing gospel, technological acceleration is rarely framed as a choice; it is presented as an unstoppable evolutionary tide. From generative artificial intelligence to geoengineering, techno-optimists contend that human ingenuity will inevitably outrun the side effects of its own creations, turning existential anxieties—climate breakdown, resource scarcity, or cognitive stagnation—into mere engineering problems awaiting brighter software. History offers seductive support for this faith: steam power, antibiotics, and semiconductor lithography lifted billions out of material deprivation within a fraction of human existence.

Yet equating technical capability with automatic human flourishing commits a subtle philosophical error. Tools do not merely amplify human power; they quietly reorganize social priorities, redistribute wealth, and reshape what societies deem normal or unavoidable. When algorithmic feeds optimize for outrage to capture attention, or automated screening software rejects job applicants on opaque statistical correlations, the resulting harms stem not from malfunctioning code, but from systems performing precisely as their incentives dictate. Treating such outcomes as "inevitable" byproducts of progress conveniently absolves designers and corporations of moral accountability.

Equally troubling is the psychological temptation to outsource human agency to purportedly autonomous machines. As predictive models grow more articulate and persuasive, citizens and institutions face a subtle erosion of judgment—what researchers call "automation complacency." Doctors defer prematurely to diagnostic algorithms; students bypass the productive friction of analytical writing; policymakers await technological "silver bullets" rather than enacting politically difficult emissions cuts today. Far from liberating human potential, uncritical faith in future inventions can paralyze present-day responsibility.

None of this justifies reflexive Luddism or romantic nostalgia for pre-industrial hardship. Technology remains an indispensable lever for expanding human freedom, provided it stays tethered to democratic deliberation rather than Silicon Valley determinism. Reclaiming public governance requires funding independent safety audits, strengthening antitrust oversight, ensuring civic literacy keeps pace with computational scale, and preserving meaningful human discretion across high-stakes public decisions—from criminal sentencing to clinical triage. Genuine agency lies neither in halting innovation nor in surrendering blindly to its momentum, but in insisting on foundational questions before deployment: who bears the risks of a given breakthrough, whose values are encoded in its design, and whether society still retains the power to say no. Progress, properly understood, is measured not by the sheer velocity of invention, but by the wisdom with which a civilization steers its creations.

vocabulary.meaning: 信条；奉为圭臬的学说（熟词僻义：原指宗教福音，外刊常喻指某种流行教条）
光刻技术（semiconductor lithography 半导体光刻）
免除……的责任；赦免（absolve sb. of sth.）
外包；推卸给外部（文中喻指将人类自主判断“外包”给机器）
据称；号称（常带有一丝怀疑态度）
自满；麻痹大意（automation complacency 自动化自满/盲从效应）
银弹；一劳永逸的神奇解药
卢德主义（盲目反对或破坏新技术的思潮）
拴住；使受约束（stay tethered to 受制于/锚定于）

sentences.label: 句子 1
sentences.quote: When algorithmic feeds optimize for outrage to capture attention, or automated screening software rejects job applicants on opaque statistical correlations, the resulting harms stem not from malfunctioning code, but from systems performing precisely as their incentives dictate.
sentences.main_clause: the resulting harms stem not from malfunctioning code, but from systems [performing...]。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：When 引导的并列条件/时间状语从句 + not from... but from... 因果辨析结构。
从句与修饰：not from... but from... 揭示本质：技术之恶往往并非“代码故障”，而是系统严格按照其背后的商业激励机制运作的结果（as their incentives dictate 作方式状语从句），直接击碎了“技术中立”的托词。

sentences.label: 句子 2
sentences.quote: Technology remains an indispensable lever for expanding human freedom, provided it stays tethered to democratic deliberation rather than Silicon Valley determinism.
sentences.main_clause: Technology remains an indispensable lever (for expanding human freedom)。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：主系表结构 + provided 引导的条件状语从句。
从句与修饰：provided (that)... 意为“前提是/只要”，引导条件状语从句；rather than 连接 democratic deliberation（民主商议）与 Silicon Valley determinism（硅谷决定论），指明技术应当服务于人类集体选择而非技术宿命论。

sentences.label: 句子 3
sentences.quote: Progress, properly understood, is measured not by the sheer velocity of invention, but by the wisdom with which a civilization steers its creations.
sentences.main_clause: Progress is measured not by the sheer velocity (of invention), but by the wisdom。
sentences.grammar:
结构类型：过去分词插入语 + 被动语态 + not by... but by... 对比 + 介词提前的定语从句。
从句与修饰：properly understood 为插入语（“如果加以正确理解的话”）；with which a civilization steers its creations 修饰先行词 wisdom（steer... with wisdom 意为“以智慧驾驭其造物”），为全篇收束点睛之笔。

translation:
在硅谷盛行的信条中，技术加速很少被表述为一种选择，而是被描绘成一股不可阻挡的演化浪潮。从生成式人工智能到地球工程，技术乐观主义者坚信，人类的创造力终将跑赢自身造物所带来的副作用，把气候崩溃、资源稀缺或认知停滞等生存焦虑，统统化作等待更聪明软件去解决的纯工程难题。历史似乎也为这种信念提供了诱人的佐证：蒸汽动力、抗生素以及半导体光刻技术，在人类存在史的一瞬之间便让数十亿人摆脱了物质匮乏。

然而，将技术能力等同于人类自动获得福祉，犯下了一个微妙的哲学错误。工具绝非仅仅放大了人类的力量；它们还会悄然重组社会优先事项、重新分配财富，并重塑一个社会对何为“正常”或“不可避免”的认知。当算法信息流为了博取注意力而专门优化激怒情绪，或者自动筛选软件依据不透明的统计相关性拒绝求职者时，由此产生的伤害并非源于代码故障，而是源于这些系统恰恰在按照其激励机制的指令精准运转。将此类结果轻描淡写为进步的“必然”副产品，实则是极其方便地豁免了设计者与企业的道德责任。

同样令人忧虑的，是那种在心理上将人类能动性“外包”给号称自主运行的机器的诱惑。随着预测模型变得愈发口若悬河且极具说服力，公民与机构正面临判断力的隐性侵蚀——研究人员称之为“自动化自满”。医生过早地盲从诊断算法；学生绕过了分析性写作中有益的思维摩擦；政策制定者坐等技术“银弹”降临，而不愿在当下推行在政治上棘手的减排措施。对未来发明不加批判的盲信，不仅远未解放人类潜能，反而可能使当下的责任意识陷入瘫痪。

凡此种种，都绝非为条件反射式的卢德主义，或对前工业时代艰辛生活的浪漫怀旧提供辩护。只要技术依然受制于民主商议，而非硅谷式的技术决定论，它就仍是拓展人类自由不可或缺的杠杆。重塑公共治理需要资助独立的安全审计、强化反垄断监管、确保公民数字素养跟上算力扩张的步伐，并在从刑事量刑到临床分诊等高风险公共决策中保留实质性的人类裁量权。真正的能动性既不在于叫停创新，也不在于盲目屈服于创新的惯性，而在于在部署之前坚持追问根本性的问题：谁在承担某项突破的风险？它的设计中编码了谁的价值观？社会是否依然保留着说“不”的权力？真正意义上的进步，衡量的标准从来不是发明创造的单纯速度，而是一个文明驾驭自身造物的智慧。

quizzes.question: By saying algorithmic harms stem from 'systems performing precisely as their incentives dictate' (Paragraph 2), the author implies that ______.

options.text: software engineers lack the technical expertise to prevent coding errors
social problems caused by technology often reflect deliberate commercial priorities
artificial intelligence has already developed autonomous moral intentions
statistical correlations are inherently useless in modern hiring practices

quizzes.explanation: 句意推理题。第二段指出问题不在于代码出故障（malfunctioning code），而在于系统精确按照激励机制运行，把这些后果说成“必然副产品”会掩盖设计者和企业的道德责任（absolves designers and corporations of moral accountability）。由此推知技术伤害往往源于人为设定的商业激励和优先级，对应 B 项。

quizzes.question: What is the author's primary purpose in writing this passage?

options.text: To urge governments to halt the development of generative artificial intelligence
To trace the historical evolution of steam power and semiconductor technology
To argue that technological progress must be guided by human judgment and accountability
To demonstrate why students and doctors should avoid using predictive models altogether

quizzes.explanation: 写作意图/主旨题。全文批判盲目技术乐观主义与“自动化自满”，并在末段明确反对盲目反技术（reflexive Luddism），强调技术需受制于民主商议与人类能动性，进步取决于文明驾驭造物的智慧，对应 C 项。
